Furthermore, the convergence of biosensors with the Internet of Things (IoT), smartphone‐based imaging, machine learning, and cloud computing has accelerated the development of intelligent, connected food safety monitoring systems. Despite these advances, challenges related to matrix effects, long‐term stability, scalability, commercialization, standardization, and regulatory approval continue to hinder widespread implementation. This review critically discusses these limitations while highlighting commercialization strategies, technology readiness, and future research directions, including microfluidic integration, biodegradable sensing materials, explainable artificial intelligence, and blockchain‐enabled traceability, to support the development of reliable, scalable, and globally deployable food safety monitoring systems.
authors: Mohima Akther Any; Abid Hassan Arnab; Liza Akter; Yusuf Chowdhury; Md. Hassan Bin Nabi; Md Abu Rayhan; Nazmul Islam; Wahidu Zzaman

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN MENTAL HEALTH: BENEFITS AND CHALLENGES OF ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS
abstract: A incorporação de novas tecnologias de inteligência artificial aos electronic healthcare records (EHRs) tem proporcionado um forte aumento na capacidade de acumular e analisar dados dos pacientes. E a área de saúde mental tem sido uma das beneficiárias deste potencial de melhorias, proporcionando aos seus profissionais ganhos de tempo e eficiência na gestão de informações médicas. Entretanto, há relatos de problemas que estão surgindo na medida em que a utilização das tecnologias de IA se intensifica. Este quadro inclui questões referentes à gestão de informações sensíveis dos pacientes, à falta de padronização dos dados de saúde mental, prejudicando a interoperabilidade dos mesmos, o receio de que o relacionamento terapêutico paciente-profissional seja prejudicado, além da preocupação que os profissionais estão tendo pela possibilidade de serem substituídos pelas tecnologias de IA. Considerando este contexto, o presente artigo tem por objetivo identificar e analisar a dinâmica de incorporação das tecnologias de IA à área de saúde mental. Para realizar este objetivo, foi realizada uma revisão de literatura envolvendo publicações sobre o tema dos últimos seis anos. Ao final, são oferecidas algumas sugestões para desenvolvimento de futuras pesquisas que possam explorar mais possíveis soluções para os problemas identificados, ao longo do processo de adoção de novas tecnologias de IA na área de saúde mental que está em curso.
authors: Bento Alves Costa Filho; Daniel Sousa Jorge; Felipe Luiz de Morais

title: Diagnostic performance of ChatGPT for acute appendicitis compared with the Alvarado score: a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
abstract: Acute appendicitis remains the most common cause of acute abdomen and is associated with serious complications such as perforation if not diagnosed promptly. While laboratory tests and clinical findings are essential, their interpretation can be challenging and sometimes misleading. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, has shown promise in supporting clinical decision-making and enhancing diagnostic accuracy. This study aimed to evaluate the ability of ChatGPT-5 to predict the likelihood of appendicitis using clinical data, with diagnoses confirmed by histopathology and comparing it to Alvarado score which is most commonly known clinical scoring system to diagnose acute appendicitis. This retrospective comparative study evaluated the performance of ChatGPT-5 in predicting acute appendicitis across two phases. In Phase 1, the model was tested without prior context learning (i.e., without exposure to any previously labeled cases) to simulate real-world use of readily available LLMs. In Phase 2, it was re-tested after exposure to confirmed case outcomes. A structured prompting strategy was applied, incorporating patient demographics, clinical symptoms, laboratory data, and clinical context, with fixed output constraints across all cases. The dataset was divided into 70% (114 cases) for Phase 1 evaluation and 30% (48 cases) for Phase 2 validation. To address potential order leakage- a bias arising when predictions depend on case sequence rather than clinical reasoning- the cases were assessed both with and without randomization. Paired comparisons of sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy between ChatGPT-5 and the Alvarado score were performed using McNemar’s test, and Cohen’s kappa was used to assess agreement. In Phase 1, ChatGPT-5 without randomization achieved a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 81.6%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 91.6%, negative predictive value (NPV) of 100%, and overall accuracy of 93.9%, compared with the Alvarado score (sensitivity 67.1%, specificity 92.1%, PPV 94.4%, NPV 58.3%, accuracy 75.4%). In Phase 2, ChatGPT-5 without randomization reached a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 93.8%, PPV of 97.0%, NPV of 100%, and accuracy of 97.9%, comparable to the Alvarado score (sensitivity 96.9%, specificity 93.8%, PPV 96.9%, NPV 93.8%, accuracy 95.8%). Within this retrospective, surgically confirmed cohort with a high clinical suspicion of acute appendicitis, ChatGPT-5 showed high diagnostic sensitivity for excluding acute appendicitis when guided by an optimized prompt, even without prior context learning. Proper randomization of prompt data appears essential to minimize order leakage and to provide a more conservative and reliable estimate of model performance. ChatGPT-5 cannot yet be relied upon to confirm acute appendicitis, given the higher specificity of the Alvarado score, and its diagnostic sensitivity remained largely unaffected by context learning, with only a modest, non-significant gain in specificity. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation in a broader emergency-department population before any clinical implementation.
authors: Amr A. Elgharib; Moustafa I. Ghanem; Rawan S. Ibrahim; Nour Elwakeel; Ayman Shemes

title: Plasma protein glycation, oxidation and nitration markers for improved risk prediction of Type 1 diabetes mellitus
abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is characterized by hyperglycaemia caused by a deficiency of insulin resulting from autoimmune destruction of insulin-secreting beta cells of the pancreas. T1DM is caused by interaction of complex-trait genetic factors and environmental triggers such as viruses, endotoxin and possibly dietary effects. Recent studies have suggested that increased serum protein content of an advanced glycation endproduct is associated with increased risk of T1DM and also, with increased risk of cardiovascular disease in T1DM patients. The aim of this study is to quantify levels of Nε-Carboxymethyl-lysine (CML), other glycation endproducts, oxidation and nitration adducts in serum protein, in addition to related serum free adducts and amino acid metabolomics of monozygotic twins discordant for T1DM, and T1DM patients with HDL of high and low HAE, and compare these with plasma from healthy subjects. HDL apoA-1 exchange (HAE) – a measure of its ability to release lipid-poor apolipoproteinA-1, an essential step in reverse cholesterol transport. Monozygotic twins discordant for T1DM were studied from a London cohort and studies of T1DM patients with HDL of high and low HAE were based on an Oslo cohort. Major chemically-defined markers of protein damage by glycation, oxidation, and nitration were quantified in samples of plasma protein and in ultrafiltrate (glycated, oxidized and nitrated amino acids) by stable isotopic dilution analysis liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. In monozygotic twins there were increased protein glycation and oxidation markers in plasma and decreased nitration markers of plasma protein for the diabetic twin. However, increased nitration was observed in the second cohort of diabetic twins. In T1DM patients with HDL of high and low HAE, there were increased levels of glycation, oxidation and nitration of plasma protein in both patients groups with HDL of high and low HAE activity. There were changes in the amino acid metabolome in plasma of diabetic patients. This study reveals that dicarbonyl stress is a potential contributory impairment in T1DM and thereby very likely contributes to risk of CVD. Measurement of protein glycation, oxidation and nitration markers provides evidence of protein damage in healthy and patients with T1DM and also provides additional facility in the prediction for developing specific complications of metabolic disease.

title: POSTOPER ATIVE COMPLICATIONS AFTER COLORECTAL CANCER SURGERY: RISK FACTORS, IMPACT ON SURVIVAL, AND CONTEMPORARY PREVENTION STRATEGIES (A LITERATURE REVIEW)
abstract: Relevance: Postoperative complications remain major determinants of unfavorable outcomes following colorectal cancer surgery, contributing to increased mortality, reoperation rates, disease recurrence, and reduced long-term survival.The study aimed to analyze current evidence on postoperative complications after colorectal cancer surgery, identify major risk factors, evaluate their impact on long-term survival, and summarize contemporary preventive strategies.Materials and Methods: This structured literature review covered 39 publications from January 1, 2021, through July 31, 2026, including 34 original studies and 4 systematic reviews or meta-analyses; the GLOBOCAN 2022 fact sheet was used only for epidemiological context and was not counted among the included studies.Results: Reported overall postoperative morbidity ranged from 8.1% to 33.3%, while colorectal anastomotic leakage occurred in 4.7% to 15.1% of patients. Wen et al. reported postoperative infectious complications in 95/593 patients (16.0%), including wound infection, anastomotic leakage, intra-abdominal infection, pneumonia, and other infectious events. Severe complications (Clavien-Dindo grades III-V) occurred in 9.7-29.7% of patients. Significant adjusted associations included sarcopenia and postoperative complications (OR = 2.53; 95% CI: 1.45-4.42), three or more linear stapler firings and anastomotic leakage (OR = 2.71; 95% CI: 1.17-6.26), and male sex in a CT-based leakage model (OR = 3.75). In one colon cancer cohort, postoperative complications were associated with a higher adjusted risk of death (HR = 1.70; 95% CI: 1.19-2.45). Multimodal prehabilitation reduced major complications from 29.7% to 17.1%, while diverting ileostomy was associated with fewer leakage-related reoperations.Conclusion: Postoperative complications are consistently associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes following colorectal cancer surgery. Adjusted analyses identify nutritional, metabolic, patient-related, and technical factors that may support risk stratification. Multimodal prehabilitation, nutritional optimization, structured perioperative pathways, meticulous anastomotic technique, and selective diversion may reduce postoperative morbidity; however, the predominantly observational and heterogeneous evidence does not establish causality.

title: Recent Advances in Sample Preparation for Cholesterol and Oxysterol Analysis in Complex Biological Matrices
abstract: Cholesterol and oxysterols are key molecules that regulate physiological processes and participate in the occurrence and progression of various major diseases. Accurate and efficient analytical detection of these substances in complex biological matrices is critical for disease mechanism research and biomarker discovery. However, challenges including complex biological matrices, large differences in analyte abundance, susceptibility to auto‑oxidation, low ionization efficiency, and difficulty in isomer separation pose severe obstacles to reliable analysis, making sample preparation the core step for accurate quantification and valid identification. Continuous innovations have been achieved in sample preparation techniques, such as liquid-liquid extraction, solid‑phase extraction, deep eutectic solvent extraction, molecularly imprinted extraction, derivatization, as well as integrated and automated workflows. These advances improve extraction efficiency, selectivity, antioxidant protection, and throughput, while effectively reducing matrix interference and artificial oxidation. This paper systematically reviews the research progress in sample preparation for cholesterol and oxysterol analysis in complex biological matrices from 2015 to 2026, highlights the technical advantages, application scenarios, and current limitations of various pretreatment strategies, and prospects the development trends toward greening, intelligence, and high throughput.
authors: Haizhen Zhang; Longchan Liu; Haoyue Zhang; Linnan Li; Zhengtao Wang; Li Yang

title: Artificial intelligence and laboratory biomarkers in veterinary medicine: an update about machine learning applications
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence has been a revolution in human medicine in the last years. Machine learning (ML), a subset of artificial intelligence, has allowed the use of a large amount of data to search for associations of clinical significance. Although the use of ML with laboratory biomarkers in veterinary medicine is limited in comparison with the human side, the number of studies published in this field is increasing in recent years. This review addresses some basic concepts and gives a general overview of the use of ML in the area of biomarkers in veterinary medicine. It is especially focused on two species of each companion (dogs and cats) and farm (bovine and porcine) animals, and provides information about the advances made in the last years, indicating how ML using laboratory data can contribute to the diagnosis and monitoring of selected diseases and, in case of farm animals, also to better control and improve their productive performance. In addition, possible new applications such as optimizing laboratory management, refining diagnostics or improving treatment monitoring based on the experience in humans are outlined. This narrative review can contribute to a better knowledge about the possible use of ML in laboratory biomarkers in veterinary and animal sciences for current and future applications.

title: Implementation of next-generation sequencing to guide care and public health action in settings with high burden of rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis: 32 stakeholder consensus statements generated using Delphi principles
abstract: Background: Comprehensive knowledge of resistance to the novel all-oral regimens for treatment of rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (RR-TB) is important, but challenging variant detection by next-generation sequencing (NGS) in combination with variant interpretation software can diagnose resistance early. We aimed to generate a consensus on strategic issues for the implementation of NGS for routine RR-TB care. Methods: We employed a stakeholder consensus process informed by Delphi principles. First, stakeholders participated in an online survey to provide feedback on statements using a 3-point Likert scale and free text. Responses were then summarised and follow-up discussion fora with stakeholders were held to revise statements until a consensus was reached. Findings: Of the 116 invited stakeholders, 58 participated, representing RR-TB research (n=28), clinical care (n=11), diagnosis (n=5), RR-TB survivors and advocacy communities (n=5) from 14 countries in five of the six WHO regions. A consensus was rapidly reached for most statements with limited editorial changes needed. The debate mostly focused on statements covering performing sequencing at centralised facilities, acting on variants without statistical association with resistance in the WHO catalogue of mutations, strengthening WHO-endorsed regimens and the need for informed consent for the use of NGS for care and surveillance. Interpretation: The consensus-building process grounded in real-world experience from a diverse group of stakeholders generated 32 consensus statements covering five strategic domains. The blueprint generated is not a definite prescriptive framework but a document that can support policymakers when developing country-specific policies for NGS-guided precision medicine and RR-TB care. Sources of funding: This work was supported by the Global Health EDCTP3 Joint Undertaking and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation under the GenPath Africa project (101103171), the Research Foundation Flanders (FWO) Odysseus (G0F8316N) and TBM grants (T001018N).

title: Aptamer-based technologies for extracellular vesicle analysis and engineering: from isolation to functional applications
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are natural mediators of intercellular communication and hold promise for disease diagnosis and drug delivery, yet their intrinsic heterogeneity complicates isolation, molecular profiling, and targeted delivery. Aptamers, owing to their high affinity, specificity, chemical tunability, and scalable synthesis, offer a flexible molecular toolkit to address these challenges. In this review, we highlight recent progress in integrating aptamers into EV research across three interconnected domains: (1) the selection of aptamers against EV-associated surface markers; (2) the development of aptamer-based methods for EV capture and isolation; (3) the use of aptamer-functionalized EVs for targeted drug delivery and immunomodulation. We also discuss outstanding challenges, particularly the need for selection strategies that better preserve native EV epitope conformations and the rational design of multifunctional aptamer architectures. Looking forward, the convergence of aptamer technology with EV biology is expected to enable aptamer-drug conjugates and minimally invasive, dynamic liquid biopsy approaches for major diseases such as cancer, ultimately advancing early diagnosis and precision medicine.

title: Influence of Vitamin D-Based Oral Rinses on Salivary Diagnostics: Clinical and Research Considerations for Viral Detection and Oral Health
abstract: Saliva has gained increasing attention as a noninvasive diagnostic tool in both oral and systemic health. Its ease of collection, patient acceptability, and potential to reflect underlying physiological and pathological processes have supported its growing use in clinical and research settings. In the context of viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2, saliva has been explored as an alternative to conventional nasopharyngeal sampling, offering a more accessible approach to detection. However, the reliability of saliva-based diagnostics may be influenced by preanalytical factors that remain underrecognized, highlighting the importance of considering oral interventions as potential preanalytical variables in salivary diagnostics while also creating opportunities for future therapeutic applications. From a clinician-researcher perspective, particular attention must be given to the oral environment and its dynamic nature. Interventions such as oral rinsing may alter the composition of saliva and consequently affect diagnostic outcomes. Observations from clinical work suggest that while oral rinsing may reduce antigen detectability in saliva, it does not necessarily correspond to a reduction in viral RNA levels, raising important considerations regarding the interpretation of test results. These considerations are particularly relevant when saliva is used for clinical testing, as variations in oral conditions and sample preparation may influence the measured diagnostic signal. Understanding these factors may help clinicians and researchers interpret salivary findings more appropriately and recognize the limitations of test results. Further attention to standardized collection procedures and the timing of oral interventions may therefore improve consistency and support more reliable application of saliva-based diagnostics across clinical and research settings in future.
authors: Sarah M. Nizar Feteih

title: Digital Twin Applications for Predictive Maintenance, Operational Safety, and Gas-Plant Reliability
abstract: This paper develops a maturity-based digital-twin framework that ties model fidelity and data quality to specific maintenance, safety, and reliability decisions. The study responds to the problem that industrial data often remain fragmented across control, historian, maintenance, inspection, engineering, and business systems, limiting trustworthy prediction and coordinated action. It uses an integrative conceptual review of scholarly and professional literature published to date. The framework organizes eight decision functions: use-case definition, asset and data modelling, sensor-quality assessment, model calibration, state estimation, prediction and diagnosis, decision integration, lifecycle governance. It applies those functions across rotating equipment, heattransfer equipment, separation vessels, piping and valves, safety instrumented functions, plant utilities. The analysis treats uncertainty, process safety, reliability, environmental performance, resource efficiency, economics, and organizational control as connected requirements. The proposed architecture links a system definition, evidence register, model assumptions, intervention portfolio, verification plan, and learning cycle. Its central proposition is that create governed virtual representations that combine physical models, operational data, asset condition, and decision workflows when decisions preserve traceability from measured conditions to selected actions and verified outcomes. The paper offers testable propositions, an implementation roadmap, asset-specific application protocols, and a research agenda. The framework supports case-study testing and quantitative extension without claiming universal performance before field validation.

title: Scientific and methodological foundations for teaching physicochemical analysis methods in continuous chemical education: a scoping review
abstract: Background Rapid technological advancement, digitalization of analytical instrumentation, and the growing demand for interdisciplinary competence have significantly transformed the role of analytical chemistry in science and industry. These changes necessitate a systematic reconsideration of how physicochemical analysis methods are taught within continuous chemical education. Objective This scoping review aimed to map and systematize the structural components of modern analytical chemistry education, identify dominant pedagogical approaches, and conceptualize their functional interrelationships within an integrated educational framework. Design/methods The study was conducted as a scoping review in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search was performed in Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, ACS Publications, SpringerLink, and RSCI (eLIBRARY.ru), covering publications from 1975 (the earliest eligible record retrieved) to 2024. Eligible studies addressed pedagogical, curricular, or methodological aspects of teaching analytical chemistry or physicochemical analysis methods. Extracted data were analyzed using qualitative thematic synthesis and conceptual mapping to identify recurring educational components and trends. Results The analysis revealed a consistent shift from method-centered instruction toward competence-oriented and system-based educational models. The most frequently reported components included integration of theoretical principles with laboratory practice, problem-based and research-oriented learning, incorporation of digital tools and chemometrics, emphasis on metrology and data interpretation, and increasing attention to sustainability and green analytical chemistry. The evidence indicates a transition from isolated presentation of analytical techniques to structured training focused on analytical thinking, decision-making, and interpretation of complex data. Conclusions Modern analytical chemistry education is evolving toward an integrated, interdisciplinary, and competence-driven model that prioritizes conceptual understanding, information processing, and real-world problem solving. The structural framework identified in this review may support curriculum development, modernization of laboratory courses, and alignment of educational programs with contemporary scientific and industrial demands.

title: Group-Aware and Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Heart Disease Prediction Using Optimized CatBoost
abstract: Accurate and reliable heart disease prediction can support early risk assessment and improve clinical decision-making. However, repeated or duplicate observations in widely used heart disease datasets can introduce data leakage and lead to overly optimistic performance estimates. This study proposes a duplicate-aware and explainable machine learning (ML) framework for heart disease prediction. A combined dataset containing 1,328 records and 13 clinical features was systematically analyzed, resulting in 605 unique feature groups. To enable reliableA classification model which can identify a decision boundary that maximize the separation between the two outcome classes was added to SVM, one of the kernel-based classification models evaluation, the feature groups were partitioned into 484 development groups and 121 independent test groups. Six ML models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were comparatively evaluated using five-fold group-aware stratified cross-validation. CatBoost achieved the highest mean ROC-AUC among the evaluated models and was subsequently optimized using the development data. The optimized CatBoost model achieved an accuracy of 88.64%, precision of 89.92%, recall of 87.22%, F1-score of 88.55%, and ROC-AUC of 93.32% on the independent test set containing 264 records. At the unique feature-group level, the model achieved an accuracy of 86.78%, precision of 90.91%, recall of 81.97%, F1-score of 86.21%, and ROC-AUC of 93.28%. SHAP-based explainability analysis identified chest pain type, thalassemia status, ST-segment slope, number of major vessels, and resting electrocardiographic characteristics as among the most influential clinical features. The findings demonstrate that combining duplicate-aware evaluation, optimized CatBoost modeling, independent group-level testing, and SHAP-based explainability can provide a more reliable, robust, and transparent framework for heart disease prediction.

title: ATRI LIMS: a cloud-native open-source laboratory information management system for biomarker-driven Alzheimer’s disease clinical trials
abstract: Objectives: This article summarizes the architecture, design principles, and implementation strategy of the ATRI Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS), a cloud‑native, open‑source platform supporting biomarker‑driven Alzheimer's disease (AD) clinical research. The system addresses challenges associated with managing large‑scale, multimodal biomarker, and biobanking data across multisite studies. Methods: The ATRI LIMS employs a Model-View-Controller architecture implemented in Django, with Single‑Page Application interfaces built in ReactJS. A hybrid database model integrates a normalized core schema with study‑specific extensions. Deployment on Amazon Web Services incorporates multifactor authentication, encryption, and a web application firewall. Regulatory support is provided through audit trails and electronic signatures. Development relied on collaboration between informatics engineers and laboratory personnel, with user acceptance testing guiding workflow and interface refinement. Results: As of February 2026, the ATRI LIMS supports seven clinical trials and observational studies and manages more than 1.2 million biospecimens. The platform synchronizes biospecimen metadata and assay outputs with clinical datasets, improves operational efficiency through automated workflows and quality control, and facilitates compliant sample sharing for secondary research. AI‑assisted development accelerated feature delivery while maintaining code quality. Discussion: The ATRI LIMS offers a scalable, adaptable informatics framework for biomarker‑intensive AD research. Its modular design, cloud‑native architecture, and comprehensive data management capabilities support accurate specimen tracking and coordinated data integration. An open-source release is planned to enable adoption and adaptation by other research programs. Conclusions: The ATRI LIMS enhances informatics infrastructure for modern AD research by enabling scalable, efficient, and compliant biomarker and biospecimen workflow management.
authors: Gustavo Adolfo Jimenez‐Maggiora; Stefania Bruschi; Sara Abdel‐Latif; Paul S. S Aisen; Robert A. Rissman

title: The Unbearable Lightness of Prompting: A Critical Reflection on the Environmental Impact of genAI use in Design Education
abstract: Design educators are finding ways to support students in skillfully using GenAI tools in their practices while encouraging the critical scrutiny of the ethical and social issues around these technologies. However, the issue of environmental sustainability remains unaddressed. There is a lack of resources to grasp the environmental costs of genAI in education, but also, and foremost, a lack of shared practices for engaging with the issue. This article critically reflects on the energy costs of using genAI in design education, using a workshop held in 2023 with 49 students as a springboard for reflection. Through this reflection, we develop a set of five alternative stances: acceptance, shift, moderation, friction, and refusal. Each of these, and the related actions, can support a conscious use of genAI in design education. The work contributes to the field of design and HCI by bringing together ways for educators to reflect on their practices, informing the future development of educational programs around genAI.

title: THE INTEGRATION OF TECHNOLOGIES OF NUCLEAR INDUSTRY INTO HEALTH CARE: THE ORGANIZATIONAL ECONOMICAL MECHANISM
abstract: The purpose of the study is to analyze organizational economical mechanism of integration of technologies of nuclear industry into health care. The methodology is based on systemic, institutional and intersectoral approaches using statistical and structural functional analysis. It is established that in Russia, in 2015-2025 volume of radionuclide therapy procedures increased more than twofold times (from 4-5 thousand to 13-15 thousand procedures annually). The number of centers of nuclear medicine reached 18-22. The percentage of state financing made up to 60%-70%, whereas deficiency of human resources reached 20%-30%. It is established that key limitations of integration are institutional barriers, high capital intensity of projects, regional differentiation of infrastructure. The scientific novelty is in development of organizational economic mechanism of integration of technologies of nuclear industry into health care as interdisciplinary system of interaction between industrial, scientific and medical sectors. The practical significance study results is associated with possibility to apply results under improvement of mechanisms of management of high-tech medical care.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Infection Prevention: From Prediction to Protection
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), first defined by John McCarthy in 1955, refers to the science of developing intelligent machines capable of performing tasks that traditionally require human reasoning, learning, and decision-making. Since its early development in the 1960s and rapid expansion in the 2000s, AI has evolved substantially, driven by the availability of large digital health datasets, advances in machine learning, and increased computational power. In infection prevention and control (IPC), AI is emerging as a powerful tool for strengthening surveillance, improving diagnostic accuracy, predicting outbreaks, and supporting timely clinical interventions. AI-powered systems can analyze electronic health records (EHRs), laboratory results, antimicrobial prescribing patterns, microbiological data, patient demographics, and real-time hospital surveillance information to identify patients at high risk of infection and detect potential healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) at an early stage. Furthermore, AI can support antimicrobial stewardship by identifying inappropriate prescribing patterns and predicting antimicrobial resistance trends. Integration of data from wearable devices, environmental sensors, imaging systems, and unstructured clinical notes can provide continuous, real-time monitoring of infectious diseases and infection risks. AI-enabled computer vision and sensor-based technologies may also facilitate automated hand hygiene monitoring, helping healthcare facilities improve compliance with infection-control practices. Predictive models can identify emerging clusters of infection and assist public health teams in forecasting potential outbreaks, enabling earlier containment measures. Thus, AI effectively bridges prediction and protection, enhancing patient safety, healthcare quality, and operational efficiency. However, successful implementation requires high-quality data, robust validation, privacy protection, ethical governance, transparency, and recognition of the limitations of correlation-based predictions.
authors: Madhumita Das

title: Transfusion Science for Acute Surgical Emergencies
abstract: Transfusion science remains central to managing acute surgical hemorrhage. This review traces the evolution from early direct donor-to-recipient techniques to contemporary hemostatic resuscitation, noting a renewed emphasis on whole blood for severe hemorrhagic shock. Current practice employs a range of products – whole blood, red cells, plasma, platelets, cryoprecipitate, and fibrinogen concentrates – each with distinct physiologic roles and indications. We examine the development and implementation of massive transfusion protocols that prioritize early activation, multidisciplinary coordination, laboratory-guided resuscitation, and balanced product delivery to improve outcomes. Operational challenges – prehospital transfusion, austere-environment strategies (including walking blood banks), logistics, inventory management, and Rh compatibility – are addressed to highlight barriers to timely access. Finally, emerging innovations are reviewed, including improved hemorrhage-control techniques, freeze-dried plasma, cultured blood products, hemoglobin-based oxygen carriers, advanced molecular typing and universal-donor technologies, and AI-driven decision support and predictive logistics. Collectively, these advances underscore an evolving field committed to safer, more effective, and more accessible transfusion therapies across civilian, military, and resource-limited settings.

title: Primary Neoplasms of the Seminal Vesicles: A Narrative Review of Carcinoma and the Rarer Non-Epithelial and Biphasic Tumours
abstract: Primary carcinoma of the seminal vesicle is an exceptionally rare genitourinary malignancy, with evidence limited largely to case reports and small retrospective series. Diagnosis requires exclusion of more common secondary involvement from prostate, bladder, or rectal carcinoma through integration of clinical findings, imaging, histomorphology, and immunohistochemistry. Patients typically present with nonspecific symptoms and often have locally advanced disease. Computed tomography identifies retrovesical masses, while magnetic resonance imaging provides superior local staging. Core biopsy may establish the diagnosis, although definitive classification may require resection. The typical immunophenotype is CK7-positive, often with CA-125 expression, and negative for PSA, PAP, and NKX3.1; however, no marker profile is invariable. A contemporary panel including GATA3, p63/p40, uroplakin markers, CK20, p53, CD44, CDX2, and SATB2 is important for excluding urothelial and intestinal primaries. Conventional papillary adenocarcinoma is the predominant histological type, with mucinous, clear cell, squamous, and neuroendocrine variants also reported. Non-carcinomatous primary seminal vesicle neoplasms, including germ-cell tumours, sarcomas, solitary fibrous tumour, and mixed epithelial and stromal tumour, form an important differential diagnosis. Complete surgical excision with negative margins is the treatment most consistently associated with prolonged survival in the reported cases and is generally regarded as the only potentially curative option, whereas radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and hormonal therapy are selectively used for advanced or recurrent disease. International registries and collaborative molecular studies are needed to improve diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.

title: Harnessing the Power of Artificial Intelligence in the Fight against COVID-19: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the development and application of artificial intelligence (AI) across disease surveillance, epidemiological forecasting, medical imaging, prognosis, drug discovery, vaccine research, contact tracing, and public-health decision support. This review synthesizes the literature on these applications while critically examining the evidence needed for translation into clinical and public-health practice. A structured literature-search and selection framework was used to organize evidence published from the emergence of COVID-19 through the contemporary literature, with emphasis on peer-reviewed studies and recent reviews. The evidence was synthesized according to the pandemic-response pathway: early warning and surveillance; diagnosis and differential diagnosis; severity and prognosis; clinical and resource decision support; therapeutic and vaccine discovery; genomic surveillance; and privacy-preserving and responsible AI. Across these domains, AI demonstrates potential to process heterogeneous data and support time-sensitive decisions, but reported performance does not by itself establish clinical utility. Recurring limitations include small or non-representative datasets, dataset shift, limited external validation, class imbalance, information leakage, insufficient calibration and interpretability, privacy and security risks, and uncertainty about workflow integration and regulatory accountability. Recent systematic reviews also indicate that multimodal, federated, and privacy-preserving approaches remain less developed than conventional centralized models. The principal contribution of this review is a unified critical framework that links technical performance with data quality, external validation, clinical relevance, fairness, privacy, interpretability, and implementation readiness. The review therefore identifies not only where AI has been applied to COVID-19, but also the conditions required for responsible translation to clinical practice and future pandemic preparedness.

title: AI in Neuro-Oncology: An Overarching Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across neuro-oncology domains to analyze complex, high-dimensional, multimodal data. Despite major advances in the biological understanding and classification of CNS tumors, clinical outcomes for many of them remain poor, reflecting intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneity and limitations of conventional reductionist approaches. AI offers a paradigm shift to capture this heterogeneity and provide quantitative, reproducible diagnostic, predictive, and prognostic insights. This article describes a joint effort across the Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) working groups to provide an overarching review of the AI use across six key domains of neuro-oncology: neuroimaging, neuropathology, laboratory medicine, neurosurgery, drug discovery, and clinical trials. Applications closest to clinical use include imaging segmentation and quantification, AI-assisted image reconstruction, DNA methylation-based classification, and workflow optimization. Radiogenomics, WSI-based molecular prediction, AI-guided surgical targeting, liquid biopsy interpretation, AI-guided drug discovery, digital twins, and in silico trials remain promising but require stronger prospective validation. Key challenges include limited availability of large diverse datasets, variability in data acquisition and reference standards, and limited external validation. This review provides a unifying framework for understanding the role of AI across neuro-oncology and highlights key considerations for its responsible implementation, emphasizing standardization, reproducibility, multi-institutional validation, and human oversight.

title: Toward precision hernia surgery: integrating biomarkers, genomics, quantitative imaging, and artificial intelligence in abdominal wall repair
abstract: PURPOSE: Despite technical advances, the expansion of minimally invasive approaches and the development of novel biomaterials, recurrence and complications following abdominal wall hernia (AWH) repair remain frequent. This variability likely reflects anatomical and technical factors and host biological heterogeneity. Precision herniology is emerging as a translational paradigm integrating biomarkers, genetics, quantitative imaging, and artificial intelligence to refine risk stratification and therapeutic planning. METHODS: We conducted a critical narrative review with translational scope. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from January 2015 to June 2026. We prioritized adult studies across four axes: (i) biomarkers of collagen, extracellular matrix, and cellular mechanisms; (ii) genetics and susceptibility to AWH; (iii) immunonutritional markers; (iv) artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for predicting complexity and complications. RESULTS: The literature reveals convergent, albeit heterogeneous, signals indicating that host biology may contribute to variability in hernia phenotype and surgical outcomes. Alterations in collagen turnover and in the MMP-TIMP axis, fibroblast heterogeneity, inflammatory signaling, polygenic architecture related to connective tissue integrity, immunonutritional markers associated with perioperative vulnerability, and quantitative imaging metrics analyzed by AI/ML models represent biologically plausible, clinically relevant domains. CONCLUSION: Available data support the plausibility that host biological heterogeneity contributes to the formation, healing, prosthetic integration, and recurrence of AWH, thereby broadening the traditional paradigm centered predominantly on defect anatomy. The main value of this work is the critical integration of molecular and cellular biomarkers, genetics, quantitative imaging, and AI/ML into a unified conceptual framework for future precision herniology research.
authors: Bruno Amantini Messias; Guilherme Costa e Silva; Pedro Henrique de Freitas Amaral; Diogo Parente Falcão; Sérgio Roll; Jaques Waisberg

title: Microbial quality control management in industry : approaches for assessing bioburden and community composition
abstract: Microbial contamination of industrial products and processes can endanger the health and safety of consumers and workers and negatively affect businesses by causing product spoilage and decreases in process efficiency. Major microbial contamination events can result in financial losses from product recalls, unplanned production downtime, loss of sales and litigation. Effective microbial monitoring is essential for detecting the presence of microorganisms and helps businesses control and maintain product quality. This thesis first examines the challenges in achieving accurate assessments of microbial load, which is defined as the quantity of viable microorganisms within a given sample matrix (Chapter 2). Classical culture techniques remain the most widely utilized and approved methods but their major shortcomings have limited their applicability in Quality Management systems employed to control contamination throughout product processing, handling, and distribution. Issues such as the long incubation times to achieve a result, the selective bias of culture conditions on species recovery, and the inability to detect damaged or injured cells are discussed. Rapid microbiological methods (RMMs) offer increased sensitivity and accuracy, can deliver results in near real-time, and could enable more effective and proactive management of microbial contamination problems. Nevertheless, their uptake in industry has been hindered by their higher operating costs and time-consuming proof-of-equivalency studies to the reference culture methods, which are required for approval by the relevant regulatory bodies. An overview of commercially available RMMs is provided and the suitability of each method is application- and industry-dependent. An industrial case study of microbial monitoring methods was performed with Omya AG (Switzerland) the top global producer of calcium carbonate (CC) slurries (Chapter 3). CC slurries are used as manufacturing fillers in a wide range of industries including paper, paints, construction and food. High microbial loads have been shown to adversely effect slurry quality and performance and negatively impact on customers’ finished products (Schwarzentruber, 2003). Quality Assurance (QA) managers rely on culture dip slides for detecting microbial load and directing biocide treatment to manage excessive population growth. RMMs offer Omya the potential for cost savings from effective biocide management and could help QA managers uncover and remedy microbial-related product spoilage sooner. The viability-based RMM CellFacts II (CFII) (CellFacts2014 Ltd., UK) combines electrical flow impedance and viable cell specific fluorescent staining to produce an accurate, real-time measurement of the contaminating population. To improve its usability and desirability to Omya the technology was optimized by streamlining sample preparation steps, the cost per test was reduced, and data presentation and interpretation was simplified. During this study CFII showed increased sensitivity and reliability compared to dip slides and highlighted the differences in preservation efficiency and bioburden levels in slurries preserved with biocide blends or by pHstabilization. Although pH stabilizers are added to slurries during production, Omya still relies upon biocides for managing any uncontrolled microbial growth detected during product storage or upon delivery to customers. The biocide-preserved slurries that were analyzed were maintained at pH 8.5-9.0 while the pH-stabilized slurry were pH 9.5-10.0. It was hypothesized that this 1-log difference in pH impacted upon microbial community composition and it was necessary to ensure that these populations were still susceptible to post-production biocide treatments. A multifaceted approach was used to characterize the communities and assess the coverage and limitations of each method (Chapter 4). Samples were collected and microbial load was determined by plate culture and CFII, and population diversity was elucidated by the recovery of species in culture and by 16S rRNA gene analysis by Terminal-Restriction Fragment Length Polymorphism (T-RFLP) and sequencing on the Illumina MiSeq (USA). A comparison of direct and indirect DNA extraction methods was performed to observe the efficiency and differences in DNA recovery from microbial species. In addition, DNA from the viable population was selectively amplified by treating isolated microbial cells with propidium monoazide (PMA), a dye that enters non-viable cells, binds DNA and inhibits PCR amplification. Biocidepreserved slurry showed lower diversity in culture compared to pH-stabilized slurry but displayed a higher number of operational taxonomic units (OTUs) by T-RFLP and sequence analysis in the microbiome analysis platform Quantitative Insights in Microbial Ecology (QIIME). The microbial communities were significantly different with Pseudomonas spp. associated with biocide-preserved slurry and alkaliphilic Bacillus spp. dominating in pH-stabilized products. The culture media conditions were inadequate for recovering the highly abundant alkaliphilic population in pHstabilized slurry and future culture work must be optimized on alkaliphilic media. 16S rRNA gene analyses produced a more truthful representation of the community and DNA extracted from PMA-treated cells revealed changes in population structure after 48 hours of incubation and in response to biocide addition. Slurry populations are dynamic; regular sample collection at various time points is necessary to achieve accurate detection and monitoring of microbial communities.

title: Abstracts From the 2026 Health Care Systems Research Network (HCSRN) Annual Conference, Dallas, Texas
abstract: The Health Care Systems Research Network (HCSRN) comprises 18 learning health systems with integrated care delivery and embedded research units. The network's annual conference serves as a forum for research teams from member institutions to disseminate project findings, explore scientific collaborations, and share insights about population-based research practices that can measurably improve health and health care for all. The theme of this year's conference was "Scaling Learning Health Systems: Data-Driven Pathways to Better Outcomes." Abstracts presented at HCSRN 2026 are published in this issue supplement of the Journal of Patient-Centered Research and Reviews, the journal of record for HCSRN's annual conference proceedings.
authors: Health Care Systems Research Network
venue: Journal of patient-centered research and reviews

title: Intraoperative electromyography (EMG): an updated position statement by the American Society of Neurophysiological Monitoring
abstract: Electromyography (EMG) is used to assess the functional status of peripheral motor axons during surgical procedures and can help protect patients' neurological integrity intraoperatively. This is a position statement on intraoperative EMG monitoring from the American Society of Neurophysiological Monitoring (ASNM) and updates prior ASNM position statement on EMG from 2005. This position statement is endorsed by ASNM and serves as an educational service to the neurophysiological community on the recommended use of EMG as a neurophysiological monitoring tool. It presents the rationale for EMG utilization and its clinical applications. It also covers the relevant anatomy, technical methodology for setup and signal acquisition, signal interpretation, anesthesia and physiological considerations, and documentation and credentialing requirements to optimize EMG monitoring to aid in protecting the peripheral nervous system during surgery.
authors: Kent S. Rice; Stanley A. Skinner; Ernest M. Hoffman; Tatsuya Oishi; Lanjun Guo; Ronald E. Leppanen
venue: Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing

title: The Lived Experience of Chinese Patients With Somatic Symptom Disorder: An Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis
abstract: Aim To deeply explore the subjective illness experience of patients with Somatic Symptom Disorder (SSD) throughout the entire course from the initial onset of symptoms and repeated medical consultations to receiving psychological interventions. Methods Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) was adopted. Purposive sampling was used to recruit 8 patients meeting the diagnostic criteria for somatic symptom disorder in DSM-5 from the clinical psychology department of a tertiary general hospital between June 2025 and December 2025. Semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted with these patients. After verbatim transcription of interview recordings, data analysis was carried out in accordance with the six-step coding procedure of IPA. Results Four main superordinate themes emerged from data analysis: (a) Embodied processing of distress and enduring somatic imprinting; (b) An unsafe living world co-existing with Symptoms; (c) Tracing symptom origins and the journey of help‑seeking; (d) Self‑growth within the lived experience of symptom co‑existence Conclusion The underlying driving force for patients with SSD is fear of death. These individuals frequently endure intense feelings of helplessness and insecurity, yet they consistently attribute their symptoms to physical pathology. Healthcare providers may obtain medical histories from patients with SSD to assess their emotional difficulties, family-related factors, personality traits, and illness-related beliefs. Furthermore, clinicians ought to provide feedback on physical-examination findings, refrain from redundant investigations, and validate patients’ distress through empathic responding. It is essential to reframe the meaning of symptoms: draw connections between symptoms and stress- or lifestyle-related triggers; illustrate the anxiety-to-illness transition pathway, alongside the vicious cycle that sustains somatic symptom responses.
authors: Xue Y, Chen F.

title: Inspect Robots: Evaluating the Capabilities and Safety of Embodied AI
abstract: General purpose language models are increasingly able to control robotic hardware. Understanding the capabilities and safety of these models when embodied is therefore increasingly important for understanding their societal impact and risks. To this end, we introduce Inspect Robots, a modular, open-source framework for developing and running evaluations of embodied agents. Inspect Robots pairs customizable, reusable abstractions for specifying physical evaluations and analyzing their results with infrastructure that automates evaluation setup, execution and termination. We demonstrate Inspect Robots by using it to evaluate the capabilities and safety of six policies based on frontier language models. Inspect Robots has seen significant early uptake, receiving nearly 100,000 downloads in the three months since its release.
authors: Christopher Leet; Achu Menon; Sravanthi Machcha; Sabrina Zou; Aayushya Patel; Aditya Kumar Singh; Anish Kr Singh; Galaba Vamsi; Javin Ahuja; Sai Asish Yamani; Tushar Anand; Vedang Alle; Zihan Zhang; Tzu Kit Chan; Jay Chooi

title: Artificial Intelligence and Sensing Technologies for Vascular Access in Hemodialysis: A Narrative Review
abstract: Vascular access performance determines the adequacy, safety, and cost of hemodialysis. Stenosis, thrombosis, cannulation difficulty, infection, and access-related cardiac stress remain major sources of morbidity. This narrative review examines artificial intelligence and sensing technologies for vascular access care, based on PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov searches through 22 August 2026 with citation chaining. Existing reviews have examined artificial intelligence in dialysis broadly or prediction models in isolation. In this review, the vascular access itself is kept as the unit of analysis, and the evidence is followed across four connected stages: systemic risk stratification; prediction of maturation, dysfunction, and complications from clinical, ultrasound, and multimodal data; longitudinal monitoring with optical, acoustic, vibration, thermal, and pressure sensors; and procedural support with robotics and visualization technologies. Reported discrimination is high in retrospective, recording-level analyses, reaching areas under the curve of 0.99 and sample-level accuracy of 100%, but falls to approximately 0.71 in longitudinal designs that predict future events in the same patients; patient-level external validation and calibration are also rarely reported. No approach has yet been demonstrated to reduce thrombosis, prolong patency, avoid interventions, or lower cost relative to standard care in prospective multicenter studies. Deployment is further constrained by power budgets, duty cycling, and transmission bandwidth in wearable devices. Technical feasibility should not be read as clinical utility.
authors: Concetto Sessa; Elettra Lomeo; Walter Morale; Tito Gianni; Bibiana Bonerba; Giuseppe Grandaliano; Francesco Pesce

title: Neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome: a review of diagnostic and therapeutic strategies
abstract: The diagnosis and treatment of neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome (nTOS) remain challenging. Although consensus-based clinical frameworks exist, they lack robust externa validation. This study conducts a review of nTOS publications in the PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases, with a search cutoff date of December 2025. Current evidence suggests that the incidence of nTOS may be underestimated. Diagnosis should be based on a comprehensive evaluation, including medical history, systematic physical examination, ancillary examinations, diagnostic muscle block, and exclusion of other possible diseases. Treatment should be carried out in a phased manner. For mild cases, nonsurgical treatment is preferred. For patients who experience progressive neurological dysfunction, muscle atrophy, or failure of conservative treatment, timely surgery should be considered. Surgical decompression mainly involves the supraclavicular or axillary approaches. Surgical techniques include first rib resection, rib-sparing scalenectomy, pectoralis minor release, cervical rib resection. However, the optimal treatment remains controversial due to the limited availability of high-quality evidence. Future research should focus on elucidating the pathophysiology of nTOS, improving diagnostic accuracy through technological innovation, and optimizing treatment protocols through prospective multicenter studies.
authors: Guang-Yao Li; Mingqiang Xue; Jing-Wei Wang; Ke Sha

title: Chromophobe Renal Cell Carcinoma With Multimodal Imaging Features: A Case Report
abstract: Introduction: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma (chRCC) is a rare renal cell carcinoma subtype with nonspecific imaging features, making preoperative diagnosis challenging. We present a pathologically confirmed case highlighting its multimodal imaging characteristics. Methods: A 51-year-old woman with an incidentally detected left renal mass underwent contrast-enhanced CT, MRI, contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), ultrasound-guided biopsy and subsequent surgical resection with histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation. Results: CT and MRI demonstrated a solid left renal mass with enhancement persistently lower than that of the renal cortex. CEUS showed delayed iso-enhancement followed by rapid washout, consistent with a slow wash-in and fast wash-out pattern. Biopsy and postoperative histopathology with immunohistochemistry confirmed chRCC. Discussion: The concordant hypovascular findings across CEUS, CT and MRI supported suspicion of a non-clear cell RCC subtype. CEUS provided complementary real-time information on tumour perfusion. Conclusion: Combining CEUS with CT and MRI may improve the preoperative characterisation of renal masses and diagnostic confidence in suspected chRCC.
authors: Jiale Hu; Feifei Song; Shufang Xiang; Can Liu
venue: Australasian Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine

title: Evolution of Diagnostic and Surgical Standards for Thoracic Outlet Syndrome in Elite Athletes: From Case Report Insights to Modern Vascular Surgery Algorithms
abstract: Background. Thoracic Outlet Syndrome (TOS), particularly venous TOS (vTOS), is a career-threatening neurovascular condition in elite athletes. A historical case of an elite Polish skier highlighted how incomplete decompression led to premature career termination. Aim. To review the evolution of diagnostic, endovascular, and surgical strategies for athletic TOS over the past decade and propose a modernized Return-to-Play (RTP) algorithm based on SVS guidelines. Material and methods. A systematic review of PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and APCZ UMK databases (2015–2026) was performed, focusing on vTOS management, robotic resections, and ultrasound-guided blocks. Results. Published athletic cohorts demonstrate high rates of return to competitive sport following appropriate surgical decompression, although reported outcomes vary according to TOS subtype, athletic population, surgical technique, and the definition of return to play. In professional baseball players, 79% returned to the same or a higher level of competition following surgery (Chauhan et al., 2024). Minimally invasive approaches, including robotic first rib resection and VATS, may reduce surgical morbidity while providing adequate decompression in appropriately selected patients. Conclusions. Early complete surgical decompression is the current gold standard for athletes with vTOS. Incorporating robotic techniques and dynamic vascular imaging optimizes clinical outcomes and preserves athletic careers.
authors: Aleksandra Markiewicz-Zahorski; Michał Markiewicz-Zahorski; Magdalena Markiewicz-Zahorski; Julia Jaszczyńska; Filip Kęska; Zoja Goti; Zofia Łubniewska; Jan Damian; Tomasz Kałużny; Maria Michalska

title: Diagnostic performance of ChatGPT for acute appendicitis compared with the Alvarado score: a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
abstract: Acute appendicitis remains the most common cause of acute abdomen and is associated with serious complications such as perforation if not diagnosed promptly. While laboratory tests and clinical findings are essential, their interpretation can be challenging and sometimes misleading. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, has shown promise in supporting clinical decision-making and enhancing diagnostic accuracy. This study aimed to evaluate the ability of ChatGPT-5 to predict the likelihood of appendicitis using clinical data, with diagnoses confirmed by histopathology and comparing it to Alvarado score which is most commonly known clinical scoring system to diagnose acute appendicitis. This retrospective comparative study evaluated the performance of ChatGPT-5 in predicting acute appendicitis across two phases. In Phase 1, the model was tested without prior context learning (i.e., without exposure to any previously labeled cases) to simulate real-world use of readily available LLMs. In Phase 2, it was re-tested after exposure to confirmed case outcomes. A structured prompting strategy was applied, incorporating patient demographics, clinical symptoms, laboratory data, and clinical context, with fixed output constraints across all cases. The dataset was divided into 70% (114 cases) for Phase 1 evaluation and 30% (48 cases) for Phase 2 validation. To address potential order leakage- a bias arising when predictions depend on case sequence rather than clinical reasoning- the cases were assessed both with and without randomization. Paired comparisons of sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy between ChatGPT-5 and the Alvarado score were performed using McNemar’s test, and Cohen’s kappa was used to assess agreement. In Phase 1, ChatGPT-5 without randomization achieved a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 81.6%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 91.6%, negative predictive value (NPV) of 100%, and overall accuracy of 93.9%, compared with the Alvarado score (sensitivity 67.1%, specificity 92.1%, PPV 94.4%, NPV 58.3%, accuracy 75.4%). In Phase 2, ChatGPT-5 without randomization reached a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 93.8%, PPV of 97.0%, NPV of 100%, and accuracy of 97.9%, comparable to the Alvarado score (sensitivity 96.9%, specificity 93.8%, PPV 96.9%, NPV 93.8%, accuracy 95.8%). Within this retrospective, surgically confirmed cohort with a high clinical suspicion of acute appendicitis, ChatGPT-5 showed high diagnostic sensitivity for excluding acute appendicitis when guided by an optimized prompt, even without prior context learning. Proper randomization of prompt data appears essential to minimize order leakage and to provide a more conservative and reliable estimate of model performance. ChatGPT-5 cannot yet be relied upon to confirm acute appendicitis, given the higher specificity of the Alvarado score, and its diagnostic sensitivity remained largely unaffected by context learning, with only a modest, non-significant gain in specificity. These findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation in a broader emergency-department population before any clinical implementation.
authors: Amr A. Elgharib; Moustafa I. Ghanem; Rawan S. Ibrahim; Nour Elwakeel; Ayman Shemes

title: Retroperitoneal schwannoma: A rare entity with diagnostic challenges
abstract: Retroperitoneal schwannomas are rare benign tumors arising from peripheral nerve sheath cells and are often diagnosed incidentally due to their nonspecific clinical presentation. We report the case of a 37-year-old woman presenting with isolated right-sided lower back pain caused by a compressive right retroperitoneal mass. The patient underwent complete surgical excision, and definitive histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of a retroperitoneal schwannoma.
authors: Kays Chaker; Ayda Khadhar; Sadok Hmouda; Afif Limem; Inès Chelly; Yassine Nouira

title: Robotic Splenectomy for Refractory Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura
abstract: Splenectomy is a well-established surgical option for selected patients with immune thrombocytopenic purpura and persistent thrombocytopenia despite medical therapy. Although laparoscopic splenectomy remains the standard minimally invasive approach, robotic platforms may offer advantages in technically challenging cases. We present a 40-year-old woman with a 4-year history of immune thrombocytopenic purpura, obesity, Hashimoto thyroiditis, and prior sleeve gastrectomy presented with severe thrombocytopenia and abnormal uterine bleeding. After failure of medical therapy, she underwent robotic splenectomy with the da Vinci Xi robotic platform using an anterior approach. Operative time was 240 minutes, and estimated blood loss was 200 mL. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 3. Pathologic examination findings were compatible with immune thrombocytopenic purpura. Robotic splenectomy is safe and feasible in this selected challenging case and may be considered an alternative minimally invasive approach when enhanced visualization and precise hilar dissection are desirable.
authors: Fernando Revoredo Rego; Monica Uribe-León; Lucía Ronceros Salas; Carlos Alberto Wong Chu

title: All-fiber wireless auscultation garment for cardiopulmonary diagnostics
authors: Qianyi Li; Ziang Li; Xiaoyu Zhang; Hakan Akgün; Swetika Chaturvedi; Hooi Khee Teo; Kamalesh Anbalakan; David Sim; Kenneth Michael Chew Yun Chi; Kee Thai Yeo; Derek John Hausenloy; Tural Khudiyev

title: Abnormal behavior perception in elderly care scenarios based on multimodal generative adversarial networks
abstract: In view of the limitations of the existing elderly care anomaly perception methods, which mostly rely on single visual mode and shallow stitching multi-source sensing features, such as insufficient accuracy of long-time progressive anomaly recognition, easy mode collapse of multimodal training, and insufficient utilization of non visual sensing information, this paper proposes a multimodal wgan GP anomaly perception method combining CNN-LSTM spatio-temporal double branch coding. The framework integrates five kinds of heterogeneous sensor data, including vision, inertial IMU, bed pressure, physiological signs and environmental audio, and adaptively allocates the weight of each mode to complete the cross modal feature alignment based on the dual attention of space and time; The shared generator based on the fusion of spatial and temporal two-way sub generators only learns the distribution of normal behavior, and uses multimodal attention discriminator to distinguish the true and false features; Wgan GP gradient penalty and modal imbalance correction item were introduced to stabilize the confrontation training, and the weighted reconstruction error and discriminant confidence were fused to construct a joint abnormal score. Four core abnormalities, including falling, falling out of bed, long-term wandering and physiological index disorder, were identified by dynamic threshold. The experimental results show that the AUC roc of the complete model in this paper can reach 0.978 ± 0.003, the F1 score is 95.64 ± 0.47%, the false positive rate is 2.13 ± 0.24%, and the false negative rate is 3.05 ± 0.30%; Ablation experiments showed that F1 score decreased significantly after removing inertia, bed pressure or audio modes, which confirmed that such non visual modes had complementary contributions to information, and the complete model had stronger scene adaptability and engineering landing value. Not applicable.
authors: Xinbo Zhao

title: Transoral robotic surgery in otorhinolaryngology: patient perspectives and determinants of outcomes
abstract: A retrospective study in the North of the Netherlands Simple SummaryTransoral Robotic Surgery (TORS) is increasingly used for various conditions, yet its success and failure remain underexplored.In this multicenter study, we assessed 220 TORS interventions across 211 patients.Success criteria differed by condition, including tumor identification for CUP, resection margins for malignancies, and symptom improvement for benign cases like OSA and chronic lingual tonsillitis.Predictors of success varied, with factors such as patient comorbidity, tumor characteristics, and demographics playing roles.Conversely, failure predictors encompassed postoperative complications and pain, linked to patient health and demographics.These insights into TORS outcomes may aid in patient selection and counseling across different conditions, informing clinical practice and enhancing patient care.
authors: Alexandra G. L. Toppenberg

title: PsyCIDRA: A Dual-Agent Framework for Psychiatric Interviewing and Diagnostic Reasoning
abstract: Large language models show promise in clinical reasoning, but psychiatric interviewing requires guiding an evolving conversation. Their ability to carry out this interactive assessment remains less studied. We present PsyCIDRA, a dual-agent framework linking free-form psychiatric interviewing with diagnostic reasoning for expert review. Its interviewer agent uses tools to maintain working notes, load expert-written skills, and retrieve ICD-11 references to guide inquiry. Its diagnostic reasoning agent then receives the completed interview transcript and reports hypotheses alongside supporting, conflicting, and missing evidence, withholding a final hypothesis when none is sufficiently supported. Using patient profiles generated with PsyCPG, we first evaluate PsyCIDRA in simulation. Across four models on 53 evaluation cases, it achieves higher diagnostic agreement than direct prompting. On 81 held-out simulated cases, rank-1 accuracy is 60.5% versus 51.9%. In a blinded study of 101 human participants in separate arms, PsyCIDRA agrees with psychologists on whether to propose a diagnostic hypothesis in 79.6% of cases, compared with 65.4% for direct prompting. Together, these findings support the potential of LLM agents to assist psychiatric assessment through free-form dialogue. By examining diagnostic reasoning, interview quality, and safety together, this study contributes to understanding the capabilities and limitations of psychiatric interview agents.
authors: Milad Mohammadi; Fatemeh Akrami Shamsabadi; Zahra Mohseni; AmirHossein Safdarian; Malekfarhad Malek; Hadi Moradi; Hesham Faili

title: Comparative study of robot-assisted versus laparoscopic surgery for rectovestibular fistula
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare perioperative outcomes and 30-day complications between robot-assisted anorectoplasty (RAARP) and laparoscopic-assisted anorectoplasty (LAARP) for rectovestibular fistula (RVF), and exploratorily assess bowel function and operative time trends after RAARP. Comparative evidence specific to RVF remains limited. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 63 patients treated during 2019-2024. Given nonrandom treatment and differing enrollment periods, the primary analysis used the contemporaneous 2021-2024 cohort (RAARP, n = 25; LAARP, n = 23). Propensity scores were estimated by Firth bias-reduced logistic regression including calendar year, and overlap weighting estimated the average treatment effect in the overlap population. The primary outcome was total operative time. Core operative time excluded robotic docking time; for LAARP, it equaled total operative time. Thirty-day complications and Krickenbeck bowel function were analyzed exploratorily. RESULTS: RAARP was associated with longer total operative time (overlap-weighted difference, 18.00 min; 95% CI 9.90 - 26.10; P < 0.001) but shorter core operative time (- 6.81 min; 95% CI - 10.36 to - 3.26; P < 0.001). Docking time averaged 26.24±11.29 min. Postoperative length of stay did not differ significantly (- 0.53 days; 95% CI - 1.52 to 0.46; P = 0.290). Thirty-day complications did not clearly differ, and no fistula recurred. Within the RAARP group, case sequence correlated negatively with total, docking, and core operative times (Spearman ρ = - 0.987, - 0.975, and - 0.896; all P < 0.001). Among 33 patients with complete Krickenbeck assessments, soiling was less frequent after RAARP [1/12 (8.3%) vs 10/21 (47.6%); exploratory P = 0.027], but missing and non-contemporaneous data limited interpretation. CONCLUSIONS: RAARP had shorter core but longer total operative time because of robotic docking. Operative times decreased across consecutive RAARP cases, although no proficiency threshold was estimated. Functional findings remain exploratory.
authors: Ziteng Yang; Zebing Zheng; Tao Zhan; Yu Liao; Lu Huang; Chengyan Tang; Qing Du; Xia XingRong; Yuan Gong; Zeping Li; Daiwei Zhu; Zhou WanKang; Yuanmei Liu; Zhu Jin

title: Artificial intelligence in musculoskeletal surgery: Bridging innovation and evidence-based practice
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies in modern medicine, reshaping how diseases are diagnosed, treated, and monitored.In musculoskeletal (MSK) surgery, AI is rapidly progressing from research laboratories into routine clinical practice through applications in diagnostic imaging, pre-operative planning, robotic-assisted procedures, post-operative monitoring, and clinical workflow optimization.These developments have generated considerable enthusiasm because they promise greater precision, improved efficiency, and increasingly personalized patient care.However, technological innovation alone should not define clinical progress.The increasing availability of machine learning algorithms, deep learning models, computer vision, and generative AI offers unprecedented opportunities to enhance MSK practice.Nevertheless, successful implementation requires more than sophisticated algorithms.Clinical usefulness depends on robust validation, transparency, patient safety, ethical governance, and demonstrable improvements in patient outcomes.The challenge facing orthopedic surgeons is therefore not whether AI should be incorporated into practice, but how to integrate it responsibly while preserving clinical judgment, professional accountability, and evidence-based decision-making.Growing evidence suggests that successful implementation requires thoughtful integration into clinical workflows while ensuring that surgeons remain central to patient care and decision-making.[1][2][3] FROM INNOVATION TO CLINICAL PRACTICEMSK surgery has traditionally relied on the integration of patient history, physical examination, imaging, biomechanics, and surgical expertise.AI introduces an additional analytical dimension by enabling computers to identify complex patterns within large datasets that may not be readily apparent to clinicians.Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning have expanded AI applications across the entire patient journey, including diagnosis, operative planning, intraoperative navigation, rehabilitation, outcome prediction, administrative documentation, and research support.[4][5][6][7]
authors: Anchal Thakur; Yash Partap
venue: Journal of Musculoskeletal Surgery and Research

title: Gastrointestinal obstruction secondary to Rapunzel syndrome: A case report and review of the literature
abstract: Rapunzel syndrome is an extremely rare and complex manifestation of a gastric trichobezoar, characterized by a hairball mass that extends from the stomach into the small intestine. This report details a unique case of a 30-year-old female with cerebral palsy who presented with a five-month history of vomiting, a progressive decrease in oral intake leading to an inability to feed by mouth, and significant weight loss. Physical examination revealed diffuse alopecia, clinical signs of malnutrition, and a firm, mobile epigastric mass. Diagnostic imaging through computed tomography (CT) identified a large intraluminal mass extending from the gastric lumen into the jejunum, resulting in mechanical obstruction. While endoscopy visualized the mass, its significant size precluded endoscopic retrieval. Consequently, the patient underwent an exploratory laparotomy and longitudinal gastrotomy for successful extraction. The postoperative recovery was uncomplicated, and a four month follow-up demonstrated a complete resolution of symptoms and significant weight gain. In conclusion, the early clinical suspicion of Rapunzel syndrome is vital in patients with underlying psychiatric conditions or neurological impairments, to prevent life-threatening complications and ensure timely surgical intervention. In addition to the case presentation, this paper provides a review of the literature.
authors: M. Rodolfo Zambrano-Lechuga; Ivan A Ornelas-Ayala; Jose L. Galicia-Torres

title: Robotic Palpation for Spatiotemporal Arterial Pulse Quantification and Mapping Using Multilevel Microdome‐Based Soft Pressure Sensors
abstract: ABSTRACT Humanoid robots have advanced capabilities through physical and physiological examinations, but their reliance on visual information limits biological‐object assessment, underscoring the need for tactile perception. Current tactile systems primarily detect basic contact using a limited number of sensors, hindering accurate soft‐object localization and physiological signal acquisition. This study introduces a robotic palpation strategy by utilizing a fully soft‐tactile‐sensor‐integrated humanoid hand for real‐time spatiotemporal arterial pulse diagnosis. A facile fabrication technique produces an artificial pressure‐sensitive layer with multilevel microscale dome‐on‐dome (DoD) structures using eutectic gallium‐indium, achieving high‐density (>72 500 ea/cm 2 ) and large‐area (wafer‐scale >98% yield) fabrication. The DoD‐integrated pressure sensor exhibits a 7.5 × enhanced dynamic response compared with a single‐level sensing layer, enabling the simultaneous detection of subtle vibrations under high‐pressure conditions. The artificial skin is integrated into a humanoid hand, featuring 81 sensors on the fingertip and a total of 801 sensors on the hand, allowing real‐time spatiotemporal arterial pulse quantification and mapping.
authors: Seong‐Min Im; Jaehwan Jang; Byeong-Sun Park; Ji‐Won Choi; Kyeong Taek Oh; Min‐gu Kim
