title: Preoperative Planning and Risk Stratification
abstract: Complex abdominal wall reconstruction necessitates a meticulous, systematic preoperative evaluation to mitigate high rates of surgical site occurrence and recurrence. This chapter delineates an evidence-based protocol for preoperative optimization, emphasizing that surgical success is predicated on thorough preparation rather than technical prowess alone. Critical components include a comprehensive assessment of patient comorbidities, hernia characteristics, and quantified volumetric analysis via cross-sectional imaging with provocative maneuvers. Formal risk stratification, utilizing validated tools such as the Ventral Hernia Working Group grading scale, is imperative to objectively categorize patient risk and guide therapeutic decisions. A paramount focus is placed on the modification of risk factors—including tobacco use, obesity, hyperglycemia, and malnutrition—through structured interventions. This advocates for a multidisciplinary approach to optimize patient physiology prior to intervention. This rigorous preoperative paradigm enables the surgeon to rationally select the appropriate surgical technique, prosthetic material, and need for adjunct procedures, thereby individualizing care to improve postoperative outcomes.
authors: Ernesto Tartaglia
venue: Updates in surgery/Updates in surgery series

title: Indocyanine green fluorescence-guided surgery in acute settings: state-of-the art
abstract: Background: Operating in acute surgical settings is significantly different from elective surgery. One aspect is the complexity of acutely ill or injured patients with abnormal physiology, unoptimized comorbidities, and unplanned interventions. Traditional visual and tactile assessments of the surgical field anatomy and tissue viability have documented limitations. The need for integrated technology to augment such assessments is described. Indocyanine green fluorescence-guided surgery (ICG-FGS) is a promising tool, given its history, safety, low cost, and accumulated experience in elective settings for many surgeries, to help transform precision surgery into acute settings (trauma and emergency surgery). An updated review is needed based on new evidence outlining the current landscape of ICG in acute settings. Methods: We performed a comprehensive review of literature update in the last two decades through June 2026, covering PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, and published societal guidelines, including, but not limited to, the World Society of Emergency Surgery (WSES) consensus position paper and the Society of American Gastrointestinal and Endoscopic Surgeons (SAGES) review. Results: ICG is applicable across the full spectrum of acute surgical care, classified under two principal functions: anatomical mapping (biliary, ureteric, thoracic duct, and vascular structures) and perfusion assessment (bowel and mesenteric ischemia, anastomotic perfusion, pancreatic necrosis, burns, soft tissue, extremity trauma, and organ injury). Emerging and less commonly reported applications include necrotizing fasciitis debridement guidance, traumatic brain injury monitoring, penetrating abdominal trauma, gonadal torsion, fistula detection, damage control surgery, and AI-augmented quantitative fluorescence. The WSES consensus and SAGES meta-analysis provided strong prospective validation to date regarding anastomotic leakage reduction. Current gaps include the absence of standardized dosing protocols in acute settings, limited randomized data, and the subjectivity inherent to qualitative fluorescence interpretation. Conclusions: ICG fluorescence-guided surgery is a safe, low-cost, and rapidly deployable adjunct for emergency surgery. Its breadth of applicability warrants wider consideration and integration into acute surgical workflows to inform surgical decision making based specific considerations including specific indications, evidence support, equipment availability, local expertise, workflow readiness and clinical judgement. Standardized protocols, prospective trials, objective and AI-powered quantification are the research priorities to further clarify its practical role.
authors: Husham Abdelrahman; Mohamed H. Khalaf; Ibrahim Al-Hassani; Mohamed H Ahmed; Ibrahim Afifi; Fernando Antônio Campelo Spencer Netto; Ayman Ahmed El-Menyar; Hassan Al-Thani

title: Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Competence Assessment Compared with Human Examiners: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis of Agreement, Reliability, And Validity
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being used to assess clinical competence, yet its measurement performance relative to human examiners remains uncertain across professions, tasks, and assessment formats. This systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis evaluated agreement, association, reliability, validity, score differences, classification performance, and human-human benchmarking for AI-based assessment of human clinical competence. Searches identified 29 eligible reports representing 27 independent studies across medicine, dentistry, nursing, pharmacy, and paramedicine. Owing to substantial heterogeneity in measurement methods, most outcomes were synthesized narratively. Two independent studies reported Spearman correlations and were included in an exploratory random-effects meta-analysis despite differing substantially in clinical assessment context using Fisher z transformation and restricted maximum likelihood estimation. The pooled AI-human association was ρ = 0.82 (95% CI, 0.55-0.93). The two correlations were numerically similar (I² = 0%), but between-study heterogeneity could not be estimated reliably because only two studies were available. This estimate should be interpreted cautiously as a cross-context summary of association rather than a common clinical effect. Direct agreement varied markedly across studies, and favorable correlations or reliability estimates sometimes coexisted with systematic score differences or disagreement near decision thresholds. Performance appeared strongest in structured, rubric-based tasks and more variable for communication, non-technical skills, and context-dependent judgments. Human-reference quality, input equivalence, model choice, and validation design also influenced interpretability across studies. The available measurement evidence is most compatible with human-supervised formative, supplementary, second-rater, or quality-assurance applications; autonomous high-stakes use requires stronger external validation, reproducibility, and decision-level safety evidence.
authors: Abdulmohsen M Alomair

title: Application of 3D reconstruction combined with 3D printing and CBL + SP in teaching gynecologic malignant tumors
abstract: Objective The synergic effect of integrating diversified teaching methods [3D visualization technology [3D reconstruction and printing], case-based learning [CBL]. and standardized patients [SPs]] in the clinical teaching of gynecologic tumors was determined. Methods A case-control study design was proceeded in our hospital between September 2023 and March 2025 for clinical undergraduate interns and training physicians. They were divided into two groups: CBL + SP teaching mode ( n = 54); and CBL + SP + 3D teaching mode ( n = 54). A theoretical exam and a self-designed subjective questionnaire survey were used for the quantitative evaluation of teaching effectiveness. Results The average score of the CBL + SP + 3D group in the theoretical exam was significantly higher than the CBL + SP group ( P < 0.001). Students in the CBL + SP + 3D group performed significantly better than students in the CBL + SP group ( P < 0.001)in the subjective grading: learning interest, classroom participation, self-learning capacity, comprehensive analytic capacity, clinical thinking capacity, effectiveness of visual teaching aids, and simulation of clinical consultation scenarios constructed using SP. The total score of satisfactions in the CBL + SP + 3D group was significantly higher than that in the CBL + SP group ( P < 0.001). The total scores by the teachers on the students' performance in the CBL + SP + 3D group was significantly higher than that in the CBL + SP group. Conclusion The CBL + SP + 3D model established a teaching system with integration of “virtualization + material object + interaction,” which enabled significant improvement in the learning interest of students and enhanced student stereoscopic cognition of the complex anatomy of gynecologic tumors and the pathologic structures, and deepened comprehensive thinking and clinical case analysis capacity.
authors: Yaoxiang Zhong; Haikun Yang; Tingting Liu; Lvyang Li

title: A PROSPECTIVE OBSERVATIONAL STUDY ON MANAGEMENT OF ESOPHAGEAL CARCINOMA WITH MINIMALLY INVASIVE IVOR-LEWIS ESOPHAGECTOMY AND ITS OUTCOMES IN A TERTIARY CARE CENTRE IN CENTRAL INDIA
abstract: Introduction: Esophageal cancer is a life threatening malignancy with abysmal survival, even for subjects under therapeutic care.Minimally invasive surgery like minimally invasive Ivor Lewis esophagectomy, which is commonly performed for treating esophageal cancer, has a favourable impact in perioperative morbidity and enhances short term recovery compared to traditional open surgery through thoracotomy.The present study was performed to evaluate the outcomes and complications of minimally invasive Ivor-Lewis esophagectomy (MILE) for esophageal cancer. Methods and Materials:A prospective observational study of 20 patients, with histologically proven adenocarcinoma of lower esophagus and posted for minimally invasive Ivor-Lewis esophagectomy, was performed in Department of General Surgery of Government Medical College and Hospital, Nagpur for a period of 18 months (From August 2022 to January 2024).Results: In this study, predominantly patients were females (60%) in the age group of 61 -70 years, with a mean age of 64.04 ± 5.15 years.All patients experienced dysphagia (100%), and more than half also reported weight loss, odynophagia, and retrosternal pain.Approximately 40 % of patients were diabetic.Additionally, 60% of patients had hypertension, with 20% of those also having diabetes.Around half of patients were smokers (50%).Patients predominantly classified as ASA status II (60%), while the remaining 40% were classified as ASA status III.Predominantly, 60% of patients were classified under the T3 category, while the majority were classified under the N1 category (80%).Majority of patients had duration of surgery 4-5 hours (40%) with mean duration was 4.5 ± 1.72 hours.Among all patients, 40% experienced bleeding in the range of 151 to 200 mL, with a mean blood loss of 176.8 ± 40.07 mL.Among patients with complications, 10% experienced early postoperative bleeding, chyle leak, anastomotic leak, or conduit necrosis, while 60% had no complications.The most common length of stay was 6 days, experienced by 40% of patients, with a mean duration of 6.6 ± 0.97 days.Around 30% patients did not survive, while the remaining 70% survived.
authors: Dr. Kartik Sharma
venue: Indian Journal of Health Care Medical & Pharmacy Practice

title: Machine learning-based early detection of abnormal heart rate in critically ill patients: a real-world clinical dataset study with automated alert system integration
abstract: Introduction: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are a leading global health challenge, particularly in resource-constrained settings where delayed diagnosis worsens outcomes. Abnormal heart rate (tachycardia/bradycardia) is a modifiable, independent risk factor that benefits from early, automated detection. Methods: We used a large real-world dataset from Hospital Santa Maria, Lisbon (23,122 patients, January 2019-November 2021, spanning the COVID-19 period). Two operational outcome definitions were evaluated: (i) an interquartile-range (IQR)-based, patient-specific definition, used to compare four classifiers (Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors, Random Forest, Naive Bayes), and (ii) standard clinical thresholds for tachycardia/bradycardia, applied to the best-performing model. Following CRISP-DM, models were trained and evaluated with patient-grouped, walk-forward time-series cross-validation to prevent patient-level data leakage. Results: Logistic Regression was the best-performing model. Under the IQR-based definition: AUROC 0.78, recall 85.4%, precision 66.1%, F1-score 74.5%. Under the clinically standard threshold-based definition: AUROC 0.81, recall 91.7%, precision 68.8%, F1-score 78.6%. Expanded metrics (event prevalence, false-positive rate, alert burden, calibration, confidence intervals) are reported. A prototype real-time e-mail alert system was demonstrated as a feasibility proof-of-concept and reviewed informally by two cardiovascular specialists. Discussion: Recall and AUROC alone do not establish clinical utility. Key limitations include the single-centre design, substantial missingness in ethnicity/diagnosis variables, the small clinician-evaluation sample (n = 2), and pandemic-period data collection. This work is presented as a methodologically strengthened proof-of-concept, with prospective, multi-site, multi-clinician external validation identified as the necessary next step.
authors: João C. Ferreira; Luís B. Elvas

title: Thoracoscopic repair of chronic post-traumatic diaphragmatic hernia: outcomes and selection criteria
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic post-traumatic diaphragmatic hernia is a delayed consequence of missed diaphragmatic injury that presents months to years after trauma. It develops in a stable anatomical setting with mature adhesions and organ migration, creating operative conditions distinct from emergency management of acute rupture. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility and perioperative outcomes of video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery for chronic diaphragmatic hernia and to identify anatomical factors that guide selection between minimally invasive and open repair. METHODS: From January 2010 to May 2026, 21 consecutive patients underwent elective repair at a single center. Approach selection considered defect size, chronicity, adhesion extent, organ viability, and the anticipated ability to achieve tension‑free defect closure. Outcomes were described for thoracoscopic repair completed without conversion (n = 15) and open thoracotomy (n = 5). One hybrid procedure that begun thoracoscopically and proceeded with conversion under continued video guidance was reported separately. RESULTS: Thoracoscopic repair was completed in 15 patients with defects measuring 20-100 mm. Five patients underwent planned open thoracotomy for larger or more complex defects ranging from 20 to 200 mm. Thoracoscopic repair was associated with lower median blood loss (10 vs 200 mL), shorter chest tube duration (1 vs. 4 days), and shorter hospital stay (5 vs. 10 days). A 100 mm right-sided defect with hepatic herniation was repaired thoracoscopically, indicating that defect size alone does not preclude minimally invasive repair. No recurrences, conversions for hemodynamic instability, or deaths occurred during follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: In chronic diaphragmatic hernia, the absence of acute hemorrhage, instability, and visceral compromise favors minimally invasive repair. Thoracoscopic repair appeared feasible in selected patients, whereas larger or complex defects were generally managed by open reconstruction. These findings generate hypotheses and require confirmation in larger prospective studies.
authors: E. B. Topolnitskiy; Ekaterina S. Marchenko; Alex A. Volinsky

title: Salvaging the Right Middle Finger with an Abdominal Flap Following Degloving Injury and Traumatic Amputation at the DIP Joint: A Case Report
abstract: Degloving injury represents one of the most challenging forms of hand trauma. Various salvage strategies have been described in the literature, including primary reattachment of avulsed skin, reconstruction using free flaps and full-thickness skin grafts (FTSG), as well as replantation and microvascular revascularization, with the choice of technique depending on the specific characteristics and severity of the injury. However, no single reconstructive method has been universally established as the gold standard; therefore, treatment should be individualized with the primary aim of preserving tissue viability and optimizing functional outcomes. A 39-year-old man was referred from a type B hospital in Parepare, presenting with an open injury of the right middle finger following a ring avulsion injury. The injury occurred when the ring worn on the patient’s middle finger became caught on the metal handle of a pickup truck while he was stepping out of the vehicle, resulting in avulsion of the skin and subcutaneous tissue of the affected digit. At the time of injury, the patient was unaware of the detached soft tissue, and the avulsed tissue was not retrieved or brought to the hospital. The patient initially presented to a type C hospital for primary management, was subsequently referred to a type B hospital, and was finally transferred to Makassar for definitive treatment. Skin loss due to traumatic amputation. The patient underwent abdominal flap reconstruction. The results show that the salvage procedure successfully preserved the right middle finger up to the level of the middle phalanx, maintaining digit length despite residual postoperative stiffness. Initial management and available healthcare facilities play a crucial role in determining the feasibility of replantation as well as the selection of appropriate salvage reconstructive options for degloving injuries.
authors: Firda Baba; Azis Beru Gani; Akram Chalid; Berry Erida Hasbi; Hendrian Chaniago

title: Beyond the Oropharynx: TTMV ‐ HPV DNA Detection in a p16‐Positive Hypopharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract: Plasma TTMV-HPV16 DNA provided complementary molecular evidence in a p16-positive hypopharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma, while PET/CT localized the occult left pyriform sinus primary. Serial postoperative TTMV-HPV DNA assays remained undetectable through approximately 19 months of clinical and radiographic surveillance.
authors: Jacob Beiriger; Brayden J. Seliger; Silvia M. Soule; Hilary C. McCrary; Richard B. Cannon

title: Management of an Intralingual Ancient Schwannoma
abstract: Schwannomas are benign tumors arising from Schwann cells. Lingual schwannomas are exceedingly rare and usually present as painless, slow-growing masses, usually of the oral tongue or tongue base, with symptoms such as dysphagia, discomfort, and, in some cases, airway compromise. The standard of care is surgical excision via a transoral approach. In this case, we discuss an intralingual ancient schwannoma presenting with dysphagia, discomfort, and throat fullness that was subsequently excised with excellent functional outcomes.
authors: Harris Syed; Bailey Balouch; Upasana Joneja; Yekaterina Shapiro

title: Néphrectomies au Centre Hospitalier National de Pikine, Sénégal : indications, techniques chirurgicales et résultats
abstract: Purpose: To describe the indications, surgical approaches, and outcomes of nephrectomies performed at a public urology department in Senegal, in a resource-limited setting. Materials and methods: We conducted a retrospective, descriptive, single-centre study at the Urology Department of Pikine National Hospital Centre (CHNP) in Dakar, Senegal, from January 2013 to December 2023. All adults and children who underwent nephrectomy, regardless of indication or procedure type, were included. Data were collected from medical records and operative logs, including demographics, clinical presentation, imaging, indications, surgical approach and technique, early postoperative course, Clavien- Dindo-graded complications, length of stay, and histopathology. Results: Over 11 years, 36 nephrectomies were performed, representing 2.2% of all urological procedures. We analysed 34 cases. The mean age was 44.7 ± 18 years (range, 12–85), with a female predominance (70.6%, sex ratio 0.4). Flank pain was the main presenting symptom (85.3%). Computed tomography (CT) urography was the key imaging modality in 97.1% of patients. Indications were dominated by solid renal tumours (35.3%) and destroyed nonfunctioning kidneys (35.3%), mostly related to urinary lithiasis. Open surgery via a flank incision was the preferred approach (58.8%). Simple nephrectomy was the most frequent technique (50.0%). The mean hospital stay was 4.7 ± 1.8 days. The overall early complication rate was 11.8% (4/34, 95% confidence interval [CI] ≈ 3 to 28), with one postoperative death (2.9%, 95% CI ≈ 0.07 to 15). Histopathology showed 10 malignant tumours (29.4%), two benign oncocytomas (5.9%), and 13 nontumoural inflammatory lesions (38.2%). Histological results were unavailable in 26.5% of cases due to missing or unretrieved pathology reports. Conclusions: Nephrectomy was performed mainly in young adults for malignant renal tumours and lithiasis-related destroyed kidneys. Open nephrectomy remains the standard approach with seemingly acceptable morbidity and mortality.
authors: JM Randiantsalama; A Sarr; N Bihonda; Babacar Sine; Abdoulaye Ndiath; A Thiam; C Ze Ondo; A K Ndoye

title: A case report of Mirizzi syndrome type II in a patient with situs inversus totalis treated with laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
abstract: Introduction: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital condition characterized by complete mirror-image transposition of the thoracic and abdominal organs. Mirizzi syndrome is an uncommon complication of cholelithiasis that can substantially increase the technical difficulty of cholecystectomy. Importance: The coexistence of SIT and Mirizzi syndrome is exceedingly rare and presents unique challenges related to altered anatomy, operative orientation, and surgical ergonomics. Case presentation: A 30-year-old man with SIT, Kartagener syndrome, Hirschsprung disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pre-hypertension, and primary biliary dyskinesia presented with worsening abdominal pain despite prior biliary stent placement. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography demonstrated cholelithiasis with an impacted gallstone at the gallbladder neck, consistent with Mirizzi syndrome, gallbladder distention, biliary ductal dilation, and a low medial insertion of the cystic duct. Laparoscopic cholecystectomy was performed using mirrored port placement, with the surgeon positioned on the right side of the patient. Intraoperatively, an aberrant left hepatic artery was found in close association with the cystic duct and gallbladder, preventing safe attainment of the critical view of safety. A dome-down approach was therefore used to complete the operation safely. The patient recovered without complications. Clinical discussion: Published reports and a meta-analysis of laparoscopic cholecystectomy in patients with SIT demonstrate that minimally invasive management is feasible and safe despite the challenges posed by mirrored anatomy, altered ergonomics, and anatomic variation. Conclusion: Preoperative imaging, mirrored port placement, and alternative dissection strategies, such as the dome-down approach, may facilitate safe laparoscopic management of Mirizzi syndrome in patients with SIT.
authors: Amy Lo; Trista Reid; Daryhl Johnson; Steven Satterly

title: Cirugía General y del Aparato Digestivo
abstract: La cirugía del aparato digestivo constituye uno de los pilares más antiguos y dinámicos de la práctica quirúrgica. Desde las primeras laparotomías exploradoras hasta los actuales abordajes robóticos y la cirugía bariátrica metabólica, el conocimiento de la anatomía, la fisiopatología y las técnicas de imagen ha evolucionado de manera vertiginosa. Sin embargo, el vértigo tecnológico no debe hacernos olvidar los fundamentos: el diagnóstico clínico sigue siendo el primer escalón de una toma de decisiones segura y eficaz. El presente libro nace con el propósito de ofrecer una visión integrada y actualizada de la cirugía general y del aparato digestivo, centrada en los fundamentos fisiopatológicos y su aplicación directa al diagnóstico clínico‑quirúrgico. No se trata de un compendio exhaustivo de técnicas, sino de una obra que prioriza el razonamiento clínico, la indicación precisa y la prevención de complicaciones. La obra se estructura en tres grandes bloques: Fundamentos generales: principios de fisiología digestiva, semiología, métodos de imagen (ecografía, TC, RM, endoscopia) y bases de la terapéutica quirúrgica (laparotomía, laparoscopia, robótica). Se incluye un capítulo específico sobre bioseguridad y control de daños, esencial en la cirugía de urgencias. Patología por segmentos: desde el esófago hasta el recto, cada capítulo aborda la epidemiología, la clínica, los criterios diagnósticos y las opciones terapéuticas (médicas, endoscópicas y quirúrgicas) de las enfermedades más prevalentes: enfermedad por reflujo gastroesofágico, hernia hiatal, úlcera péptica, colelitiasis, pancreatitis aguda y crónica, cáncer colorrectal, enfermedad inflamatoria intestinal, apendicitis, hernia de la pared abdominal y patología hemorroidal, entre otras. Escenarios especiales: cirugía de urgencias (peritonitis, obstrucción intestinal, isquemia mesentérica), cirugía oncológica (resecciones ampliadas, metástasis hepáticas), cirugía metabólica y bariátrica, y el paciente politraumatizado con afectación abdominal. Cada capítulo está redactado por especialistas con amplia experiencia asistencial y docente, y ha sido sometido a una rigurosa revisión por pares. Se han incorporado algoritmos de decisión, tablas de estadificación y recomendaciones basadas en la evidencia (guías de la Asociación Española de Cirujanos, la American College of Surgeons y la Sociedad Europea de Cirugía Endoscópica). Un aspecto distintivo de esta obra es el énfasis en el diagnóstico clínico‑quirúrgico como competencia nuclear del cirujano general. Frente a la tentación de apoyarse exclusivamente en pruebas complementarias, recordamos que una anamnesis minuciosa y una exploración física sistemática siguen siendo la mejor herramienta para orientar la indicación quirúrgica y anticipar las complicaciones. Los capítulos incluyen recuadros de "señales de alarma" y "errores diagnósticos frecuentes" que el lector podrá aplicar directamente en la práctica diaria. El libro está dirigido a residentes de Cirugía General, a cirujanos ya especializados que deseen actualizar sus conocimientos y a médicos de atención primaria o de urgencias que necesitan reconocer cuándo derivar a un paciente quirúrgico. Cada capítulo contiene objetivos de aprendizaje, preguntas de autoevaluación y una lista de lecturas recomendadas actualizadas a 2025-2026. Agradecemos profundamente a los autores, a los revisores externos y a las instituciones que han apoyado esta iniciativa (Hospital General de Latacunga, Universidad Técnica de Ambato, y las sociedades científicas afines). Esperamos que este libro se convierta en un compañero de consulta habitual y que contribuya a mejorar la calidad del diagnóstico y el tratamiento quirúrgico de los pacientes con patología digestiva.
authors: Juan Diego Lanchi Campoverde; David Patricio Alulema Cutiopala; Adriana Cristina Cabascango Soria; Karol Dayana Rengifo Santistevan; Juan Daniel Fonseca Vaca

title: Evaluation of DeepSeek with a RAG-based knowledge base in preoperative assessment for arthroplasty to improve the decision-making accuracy of junior physicians
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing elective joint replacement are mostly elderly individuals with multiple chronic diseases. These patients have a higher risk, so preoperative assessment for joint replacement is vital for surgical safety but remains challenging for junior physicians. This study aimed to evaluate the decision-making performance of different versions of DeepSeek (Chat and R1) and their knowledge base (KB)-enhanced schemes in perioperative risk assessment and their impact on junior physicians' decision-making quality. METHODS: A total of 292 anonymized medical records from joint replacement patients were retrospectively analyzed. A professional knowledge base was constructed using 21 perioperative management guidelines and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology. The performance of four models (DeepSeek-Chat, DeepSeek-Chat + KB, DeepSeek-R1, and DeepSeek-R1 + KB) was compared in ASA scoring, RCRI scoring, surgical tolerance judgment, and risk prediction. These indicators are related to specific decisions in joint replacement surgery, including preoperative optimization before elective TKA/THA, mitigation of infection risk, planning of VTE prophylaxis, and indication for postponing elective arthroplasty, etc. Senior physicians evaluated model performance using a Likert scale. A 5 × 5 balanced Latin square crossover design was used to assess the impact of model assistance on junior physicians' clinical decision-making. RESULTS: No significant difference was found in ASA scoring accuracy (p > 0.05). For RCRI scoring and risk stratification, DeepSeek-R1 models (79.1%-79.7%) outperformed Chat models (56.5%-66.0%, p < 0.05). In surgical tolerance assessment, DeepSeek-R1 + KB showed relatively better performance, with significantly better predictive precision (p = 0.0284) and a lower missed diagnosis rate (p = 0.005) compared to the Chat models. The R1 series also showed higher predictive efficiency (87.2%-86.4% vs. 63.6%-61.8%, p < 0.05). The R1 models showed better performance than Chat models in medical comprehension, retrieval accuracy, and reasoning logic. After adjusting for physician variability and patient case mix, the DeepSeek-R1 + KB showed a statistically significant improvement over independent decision-making (OR = 1.58, p = 0.004), as well as the DeepSeek-R1 and Chat series. CONCLUSION: The DeepSeek-R1 model, with chain-of-thought reasoning, shows a marginal advantage over the Chat version in preoperative assessment for joint replacement. As a cost-effective clinical auxiliary tool, its integration with a professional knowledge base scheme can optimize the decision-making quality of junior physicians, particularly in terms of providing helpful and comprehensive decision support and providing novel insights for individualized assessment in the context of precision medicine.
authors: Haibo Wu; Mingzhuang Hou; Gongkai Chen; Zhenlin Wen; Changao Yang; Songlin Li; Xiangfei Meng; Peilai Liu; Qunshan Lu

title: Concordance of p16 status between US-guided core needle biopsy and surgical specimens in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
abstract: With the increasing prevalence of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), there is a need for efficient, minimally invasive methods to evaluate p16 status. This study aimed to assess the concordance of p16 status between ultrasound (US)-guided core needle biopsy (CNB) of cervical lymph nodes and surgical specimens, and to describe the numbers of CNB and surgical sessions required to establish the histopathologic diagnosis. This retrospective study included 39 patients diagnosed with OPSCC or head and neck squamous cell carcinoma of unknown primary (SCCUP) at a single tertiary hospital between March 2019 and March 2024. All included patients underwent US-guided CNB of cervical lymph nodes and a surgical procedure (biopsy or resection), and had evaluable p16 immunohistochemistry (IHC) results on both specimen types. The concordance rate for p16 status between US-guided CNB and surgical specimens was 100.0% (39/39; 95% CI, 91.0-100.0%; 35 p16-positive and 4 p16-negative cases). Sensitivity was 100.0% (35/35; 95% CI, 90.0-100.0%) and specificity was 100.0% (4/4; 95% CI, 39.8-100.0%). In all 39 included patients, a diagnosis of metastatic squamous cell carcinoma and an evaluable p16 result were obtained at the first CNB session. Among the 35 patients with OPSCC, 10 (28.6%) required more than 1 surgical session at the primary tumor site. No immediate complications were observed following US-guided CNB. In this cohort, US-guided CNB of cervical lymph nodes showed complete observed concordance with surgical specimens for p16 status, and a diagnosis with an evaluable p16 result was obtained at the first CNB session in all patients. Prospective, multicenter validation including more p16-negative cases is required before wider adoption.
authors: Dongjun Lee; Young Jun Choi; Joon Seon Song; Yoon Se Lee; Sae Rom Chung; Jung Hwan Baek; Jeong Hyun Lee

title: Forensic Medicine in the Modern Era: Principles, Applications, Emerging Technologies, Challenges and Future Directions
abstract: Forensic medicine is a discipline within forensic science that focuses on deceased bodies, particularly the time since death, the cause of death, the manner of death, and the mode of death. It further supports investigations by providing detailed information about the incident, including confirmation of the type of weapon used to commit the crime. Its scope goes beyond the customary forensic autopsy and encompasses medicolegal death investigation, clinical examination of living individuals, interpretation of injuries, assessment of sexual assault, forensic toxicology, identification of unknown persons, documentation of abuse, and evaluation of medical evidence for judicial proceedings. In this mini review, we will examine advanced techniques currently used in forensic medicine and how they enhance investigations, making the process easier for the investigating officer. At present, rather than relying solely on conventional approaches, investigators are increasingly adopting newer advancements such as virtual autopsy. Virtual autopsy offers valuable noninvasive documentation and can enhance the detection of skeletal and certain traumatic findings; however, the available evidence does not justify replacing conventional autopsy universally. In this review article, we will discuss all the new techniques that are useful in the field of forensic medicine and can also assist forensic investigations.
authors: Rohini Dharela; Abhijato Chatterjee; Saarsanth Philem; Davik Chaturvedi; Altamash Nomani; Manraj S. Grover
venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

title: Endobronchial Pulmonary Typical Carcinoid Tumors in Young Adults: A Three-Case Series Highlighting Obstructive Complications and Surgical Outcomes
abstract: Background: Typical pulmonary carcinoid tumors are uncommon, well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms that often arise in the central airways and may present with nonspecific obstruction-related respiratory symptoms, resulting in delayed diagnosis. We report a three-case series of endobronchial typical pulmonary carcinoid tumors in young adults, highlighting their variable obstructive complications and surgical outcomes. Methods: This retrospective case series included three consecutive patients managed at a tertiary university hospital in Syria. Clinical presentation, imaging, bronchoscopic findings, operative details, histopathology, and follow-up data were obtained from medical records. All patients had histopathologically confirmed typical pulmonary carcinoid tumors with central/endobronchial involvement and underwent definitive surgical resection. Patient identifiers were removed, and written informed consent for publication and use of accompanying images was obtained. Results: The patients were 23-35 years old and presented with different manifestations of central airway obstruction: chronic productive cough (Case 1), post-obstructive suppuration with lung abscesses (Case 2), and recurrent hemoptysis with atelectatic/post-obstructive changes (Case 3). Bronchoscopy demonstrated obstructing endobronchial lesions in all three cases, and histopathology confirmed typical carcinoid tumors with low mitotic activity and no necrosis. Case 1 underwent right middle and lower bilobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection for a large tumor staged T4N1M0. Cases 2 and 3 underwent left lower lobectomy; in Case 3, this included bronchial segment resection with primary closure and mediastinal lymph node dissection. Resection margins were negative in all cases, and mediastinal nodes were negative in Cases 2 and 3. No adjuvant therapy was administered. Follow-up showed no recurrence approximately 4.5 years after surgery in Case 1, clinical stability at one month in Case 2, and stable chest imaging at six months in Case 3. Conclusion: Endobronchial typical pulmonary carcinoid tumors in young adults can produce diverse obstruction-related complications, including chronic cough, post-obstructive suppuration, and hemoptysis with atelectatic changes. Timely airway evaluation and complete surgical resection with appropriate nodal assessment can achieve favorable outcomes, including in locally advanced disease when complete resection is feasible.
authors: Issam Alkhayer; Mohammad Alaa Aldakak; Youssef Abbas

title: Kinematic Alignment in TKA Using the Contralateral Healthy Knee as Reference: A Combined Finite Element and Clinical Analysis
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Mechanical alignment (MA) and kinematic alignment (KA) are common total knee arthroplasty (TKA) strategies. Patients with bilateral knee osteoarthritis lack a precise individualized alignment reference, whereas those with unilateral OA have a potential reference from the contralateral healthy knee. This study proposes a natural KA (NKA) strategy referencing the contralateral healthy knee and compares biomechanical and clinical outcomes of MA, KA, and NKA for TKA. METHODS: Finite element models (neutral/mild/moderate varus) were established based on three selected patients with unilateral knee OA using bilateral CT data to simulate MA/KA/NKA implantation. This exploratory biomechanical analysis was designed to identify potential patterns. Stress distribution on the femoral component, polyethylene insert, and tibia, along with contact pressure, contact area, and implant displacement, was analyzed. Additionally, a retrospective clinical study included 101 patients who underwent TKA with a minimum 1-year follow-up. Patients were divided into MA, KA, and NKA groups based on postoperative radiographic alignment. Postoperative alignment parameters, range of motion (ROM), Knee Society Score (KSS), and Forgotten Joint Score (FJS) were compared. RESULTS: Finite element analysis revealed that in the neutral and mild varus models, NKA resulted in a more balanced mediolateral biomechanical distribution, lower implant stress, and minimal component subsidence. In the moderate varus model, MA showed the most balanced mediolateral load distribution and the largest contact area. Clinical follow-up indicated that the MA group achieved lower limb alignment close to mechanical neutrality postoperatively, while the KA and NKA groups retained some physiological varus. No significant differences were observed in KSS among the three groups. However, FJS showed a statistically favorable trend in the KA and NKA groups compared with the MA group, although the clinical significance of this difference requires further investigation. CONCLUSION: The NKA strategy shows potential biomechanical advantages by optimizing stress distribution in selected neutral/mild varus models and is associated with better short-term patient-reported satisfaction than MA. NKA provides a feasible coronal alignment concept for precision TKA in patients with unilateral knee osteoarthritis without significant contralateral deformity. Long-term safety and generalizability require further validation.
authors: Lingce Kong; Wei Lin; Huijun Kang; Muchen Yu; Ming Li; Chenyue Xu; Fei Wang

title: Deep learning–based estimation of entrapment status of survivors under debris from 3D measurements for disaster medical response
abstract: Severe earthquakes, landslides, and tsunamis can cause structural collapse, trapping survivors beneath debris and limiting direct observation of the entire body. In confined spaces, voice calls, still images, and videos may be inadequate for conveying a survivor’s posture, contact with debris, and surrounding spatial conditions. We therefore developed a deep learning–based pipeline that takes a textured 3D scene mesh as input and integrates multiview, disaster-adapted human pose and shape estimation, dual-label RGB-D segmentation, scene-constrained SMPL fitting, and voxel-based geometric reasoning. The pipeline reconstructs a full-body survivor mesh, identifies candidate debris–body contact regions, and estimates the mass of load-contributing debris using a simplified geometric criterion. We evaluated the pipeline in 23 controlled entrapment cases involving clothed mannequins and representative wood and concrete blocks. Across these cases, the complete pipeline achieved a contact-region intersection-over-union of 0.391, an F1-score of 0.538, and a relative debris-mass error of 26.1%. Although these results do not establish the method’s suitability for clinical diagnosis, crush-syndrome severity assessment, or autonomous medical or rescue decision-making, they demonstrate its technical feasibility for generating preliminary situational information from 3D scene measurements.
authors: Ken Nishioka; Satoshi Kanai; Hiroaki Date; Atsushi Konno; Soichi Murakami; Toshiaki Shichinohe

title: Laparoscopic-assisted natural orifice specimen extraction subtotal colectomy for redundant colon: a retrospective parallel-cohort comparative study with reduced surgical site infections and accelerated recovery
abstract: Background Redundant colon is one of the anatomical causes of slow transit constipation (STC). When conservative management fails, surgical intervention with subtotal colectomy is indicated. This study aimed to compare the perioperative outcomes of laparoscopy-assisted natural orifice specimen extraction (LA-NOSE) subtotal colectomy with conventional laparoscopy-assisted subtotal colectomy for redundant colon. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 34 patients with redundant colon who underwent laparoscopy-assisted subtotal colectomy with cecorectal anastomosis at the Affiliated Hospital of Chengdu University between January 2009 and January 2026. Of these, 16 patients underwent LA-NOSE and 18 underwent conventional surgery with a mini-laparotomy for specimen extraction. Categorical perioperative outcomes were compared using Fisher's exact test. Results Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two groups. The LA-NOSE group showed certain advantages in postoperative recovery: sitting up within 24 h (87.5% vs. 38.9%, p = 0.005), getting out of bed within 2 days (93.8% vs. 55.6%, p = 0.019), ambulation within 3 days (100% vs. 72.2%, p = 0.046), return of gastrointestinal function within 2 days (62.5% vs. 27.8%, p = 0.045), liquid diet tolerance within 3 days (87.5% vs. 44.4%, p = 0.013), and earlier suture removal on days 6–7 (100% vs. 0%, p < 0.001). The incidence of surgical site infection (SSI) was significantly lower in the LA-NOSE group (0% vs. 27.8%, p = 0.046). Operative time, estimated blood loss, and the incidence of intestinal obstruction, anastomotic leakage, and intra-abdominal infection showed no significant differences between the groups. Conclusion LA-NOSE subtotal colectomy is a safe and feasible minimally invasive option for redundant colon, offering accelerated postoperative recovery, reduced SSI, and superior cosmetic outcomes without compromising safety. This technique adheres to the principles of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) and offers an alternative treatment option for transnatural orifice specimen extraction in benign colonic diseases.
authors: Wen-Na Liu; Li-Hao Deng

title: Seminal bradykinin, fetuin-a, pentraxin-3, and adipolin levels in infertile men with varicocele and varicocelectomy: a cross-sectional case–control study
abstract: Abstract Varicocele is characterized by abnormal dilatation of the pampiniform plexus accompanied by venous reflux and is one of the leading correctable causes of male infertility. Although several mechanisms have been proposed, the molecular pathways underlying varicocele-induced testicular dysfunction remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate seminal bradykinin, fetuin-A, pentraxin-3, and adipolin levels in infertile men with varicocele and to compare these biomarkers among patients with varicocele, patients who had undergone varicocelectomy, and controls. This cross-sectional case-control study included 90 participants: 30 infertile men with clinical varicocele, 30 patients who had undergone varicocelectomy and 30 healthy controls. Seminal bradykinin, fetuin-A, pentraxin-3, and adipolin concentrations were determined using ELISA. Sperm concentration, rapid progressive, non-progressive, and immotile sperm percentages, together with bradykinin, fetuin-A, and pentraxin-3 levels, differed significantly among the study groups. Fetuin-A and pentraxin-3 levels were significantly elevated in the varicocele group compared with healthy controls. Patients assessed approximately 3 months after varicocelectomy exhibited significantly higher bradykinin, fetuin-A, and pentraxin-3 levels than controls. No significant differences were observed among the groups regarding age, height, body weight, body mass index, abstinence duration, semen volume, slow progressive sperm percentage, or Adipolin levels. Our findings indicate that patients with varicocele and patients assessed after varicocelectomy exhibit differences in inflammatory and cellular stress-related biomarkers compared with healthy controls. The higher levels of bradykinin, fetuin-A, and pentraxin-3 observed in patients assessed after varicocelectomy may reflect differences in inflammatory and cellular stress-related profiles between the study groups; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow these findings to be interpreted as postoperative persistence or treatment-related changes. These biomarkers may provide complementary information regarding inflammatory and cellular stress-related profiles in varicocele; however, their clinical significance and utility for monitoring postoperative changes require confirmation in larger prospective longitudinal studies.
authors: Mesut Oc; Ahmet DÜNDAR; Songül Çetik Yıldız; Halit Irmak

title: Journal of Urological Surgery
abstract: The Journal of Urological Surgery is an open access, scientific, double-blind peer-reviewed journal in the field of Urooncology, Endourology, Pediatric Urology, Andrology, Reconstructive Urology, General Urology, Urogynecology and Functional Urology, Transplantation and Vascular Surgery. No fee is charged from the authors during the submission, evaluation and publication process. It is the official publication of the Society of Urological Surgery and is published quarterly (March, June, September, December).

title: THE INTEGRATION OF TECHNOLOGIES OF NUCLEAR INDUSTRY INTO HEALTH CARE: THE ORGANIZATIONAL ECONOMICAL MECHANISM
abstract: The purpose of the study is to analyze organizational economical mechanism of integration of technologies of nuclear industry into health care. The methodology is based on systemic, institutional and intersectoral approaches using statistical and structural functional analysis. It is established that in Russia, in 2015-2025 volume of radionuclide therapy procedures increased more than twofold times (from 4-5 thousand to 13-15 thousand procedures annually). The number of centers of nuclear medicine reached 18-22. The percentage of state financing made up to 60%-70%, whereas deficiency of human resources reached 20%-30%. It is established that key limitations of integration are institutional barriers, high capital intensity of projects, regional differentiation of infrastructure. The scientific novelty is in development of organizational economic mechanism of integration of technologies of nuclear industry into health care as interdisciplinary system of interaction between industrial, scientific and medical sectors. The practical significance study results is associated with possibility to apply results under improvement of mechanisms of management of high-tech medical care.
authors: T. Yu. Dzholdosheva; A. B. Mottaeva; O. V. Suzeva; V. D. Petelina
venue: Problems of Social Hygiene Public Health and History of Medicine

title: Evaluation of the Reliability and Quality of Nursing Care Plans Produced by Artificial Intelligence Models for Patients Experiencing Anaphylactic Shock: A Methodological and Exploratory Investigation
abstract: AIM: This study aimed to develop and validate a ChatGPT 4.0 and DeepSeek V3 model-supported nursing care plan for patients with anaphylactic shock. METHODS: The type of study is methodological and exploratory research. The research consists of three phases and six steps. Phase 1: Patient Scenario Development: (1) literature review and (2) scenario creation. Phase 2: Nursing Care Plan Development: (3) identification of patient care needs and (4) generation of a scenario-based nursing care plan by AI. Phase 3: Validation of the Nursing Care Plan: (5) expert review and validation of the AI-generated nursing care plan and (6) assessment of the nursing care plan's readability. ChatGPT 4.0 and DeepSeek V3 were employed to create nursing care plans. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation scale was utilized to evaluate the quality of nursing care plans. The intraclass correlation coefficient was utilized to assess the inter-rater reliability of the evaluation tool. The analysis of readability was conducted utilizing the Ateşman, the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, the Gunning Fog Index, and the Simple Measure of Gobbledygook formula. RESULTS: A notable difference emerged between the models in the Nursing Assessment section, as experts assigned higher scores to ChatGPT 4.0 (p < .005). No significant differences were found among the artificial intelligence models in other sections (p > .05). DeepSeek V3 exhibited an elevated readability level, indicated by a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 13.19, a Gunning Fog Index of 17.20, and an Simple Measure of Gobbledygook score of 9.91. CONCLUSION: Nursing care plans designed with artificial intelligence support are sufficiently readable and applicable for nurses. Cite this article as: Soylu, A., & Soylu, D. (2026). Evaluation of the reliability and quality of nursing care plans produced by artificial intelligence models for patients experiencing anaphylactic shock: a methodological and exploratory investigation. Florence Nightingale Journal of Nursing, 34, 0162, doi: 10.5152/FNJN.2026.25162.
authors: Ayşe Soylu; Dilek Soylu

title: Vaginal Mesh Revision Surgery: A Focus on Functional Outcomes
abstract: Background/Objectives: Mesh-related complications after surgery for stress urinary incontinence (SUI) and pelvic organ prolapse (POP) remain a clinical challenge, and surgical revision is often required. However, its impact on functional outcomes and continence status is incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate voiding and continence outcomes after surgical revision of vaginal synthetic mesh. Methods: This retrospective multicenter study included 55 consecutive women undergoing surgical revision of synthetic mesh for symptomatic complications after SUI or POP procedures between March 2021 and April 2025. Preoperative evaluation included clinical assessment, uroflowmetry, and selective imaging or urodynamic studies. Surgical management included mesh section, partial removal, or total removal via vaginal, abdominal, or combined approaches. The primary outcome was change in Qmax and post-void residual (PVR). Secondary outcomes included symptom resolution, changes in urgency urinary incontinence (UUI) and SUI, and postoperative complications. Results: Obstructive voiding dysfunction was the leading indication for revision (47.3%). Median Qmax increased from 13.0 to 18.0 mL/s (p = 0.0013), and median PVR decreased from 55.0 to 5.0 mL (p < 0.001). UUI improved from 56.4% to 34.5% (p = 0.017, McNemar’s exact test). Conversely, SUI increased from 20.0% to 56.4% (p < 0.001), although only 16 patients (29.1%) had clinically significant postoperative SUI, of whom 7 underwent a secondary anti-incontinence procedure. Intraoperative complications were infrequent (5.5%), while postoperative urinary tract infections occurred in 16.4%. Conclusions: Mesh revision surgery improves voiding function and reduces storage symptoms in selected patients but carries a substantial risk of recurrent or de novo SUI, underscoring the need for careful patient selection and counseling, with an acceptable safety profile in experienced centers.
authors: Rui Pedrosa; Carlos Márquez Güemez; Manuel Saavedra Centeno; Clara Velasco Balanza; Lira Pelari-Mici; Javier Casado; Luis San-José; Luis López‐Fando

title: Inguinal Hernia in a Woman: A Rare Clinical Entity – Case Report
abstract: Inguinal hernia in females is not common, and they are misdiagnosed due to atypical presentation and lower clinical suspicion as compared to males. Inguinal hernia usually presents as a groin swelling with or without pain and carries a higher risk of complications such as incarceration or strangulation. Diagnosis is primarily by clinical examination, but may need imaging support when uncertain. Surgical repair remains the definitive treatment, with both open and laparoscopic approaches. Early recognition is very important to prevent unwanted complications, which are more common in women with femoral hernias. This case report presents a patient with a right-sided inguinal hernia. A 44-year old female patient presented in outpatient surgery with a history of a lump in the right groin area for the last few months.
authors: Amir Yousaf; Raheel Ahmed

title: Development of an Electronic Archive “Rehabilitation after Soft-Tissue Lesions of the Knee Complex” for the Post-Graduate Medical and Health Professions Education
abstract: The objectives of the current article include the preservation of the scientific heritage of Bulgarian Ortho-rehabilitation school through development of an electronic archive in the field of “Orthopedic Rehabilitation of soft-tissue lesions of the knee complex”, and analysis of the efficacy of its application in the post-graduate medical and healthcare education.
authors: Radoslav Yoshinov; Borislav Yoshinov; Ivet B. Koleva
venue: Digital Presentation and Preservation of Cultural and Scientific Heritage

title: Skene’s Gland Malignancy from Imaging Diagnosis to Management: A Narrative Review
abstract: Background/Objectives: Skene’s gland malignancies are extremely rare tumors of the female paraurethral region, known almost exclusively from case reports and small case series. Their diagnosis is often delayed because symptoms are nonspecific and may mimic benign periurethral disorders, urethral diverticula, primary urethral carcinoma or anterior vaginal wall tumors. This narrative review focuses on the role of imaging, particularly pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), in the diagnosis, differential diagnosis, staging and treatment planning of Skene’s gland malignancies, distinguishing evidence from confirmed Skene’s gland cases from evidence extrapolated from female urethral carcinoma. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched on 27 September 2026 (publication years 2015–2026) and supplemented by reference-list screening; an explicit case definition was applied. Results: Of 191 records (93 after de-duplication), 17 reports of Skene’s gland malignancy were included (15 case reports or series and 2 systematic reviews); fewer than thirty cases have been published overall. Patients were mostly postmenopausal (median age about 70 years, range 45–91), presenting with an asymptomatic periurethral nodule, hematuria or vaginal bleeding, or lower urinary tract symptoms; no uniform staging system has been applied. Most tumors were prostatic-type adenocarcinomas treated by local excision alone; radiotherapy, chemotherapy or androgen deprivation were used mainly for nodal, metastatic or recurrent disease. After examination, ultrasonography can detect and characterize a paraurethral mass, whereas MRI best defines tumor epicenter, urethral, periurethral and anterior vaginal wall involvement and regional spread, and should precede cystourethroscopy and biopsy; CT and PET/CT are complementary for systemic staging. No single immunohistochemical marker establishes Skene’s gland origin. Conclusions: MRI is central to localizing and staging suspected Skene’s gland malignancy and thus to guiding biopsy and the choice between local excision and radical surgery, but most imaging recommendations are extrapolated from female urethral carcinoma and require validation in pooled multicenter data.
authors: Roxana-Denisa Capraș; Teodora Telecan; Lucas Tellier; Miana Gabriela Pop; Adriana Ioana Gaia‐Oltean

title: LAPAROSCOPIC UROLOGIC SURGERY: INITIAL EXPERIENCES IN PADANG
abstract: Introduction: Laparoscopic surgery is increasingly prevalent in urology due to improved surgical expertise. This minimally invasive procedure, popularized in the nineteenth century, offers advantages including reduced pain, less bleeding, shorter hospital stays, and improved cosmetic results compared to open surgery. Laparoscopy has expanded to various applications, including nephrectomies, pyeloplasty, ureteral stone removal, nonpalpable testes, and adrenal surgeries. Today, most urological procedures can be performed using laparoscopy, with oncological outcomes comparable to open surgery. Objective: In this retrospective study, we assess urological laparoscopic surgery results and complications in Padang, Indonesia. Material & Methods: A retrospective evaluation was conducted on patients who underwent laparoscopic surgery in Padang, Indonesia, between September 2017 and July 2023. The assessment encompassed preoperative diagnoses, laparoscopic procedure types, operation duration, hospital stays, blood loss, conversion to open surgery, and complications. Results: Of the 155 patients, 105 (67.7%) were male, with a median age of 37 years (range: 1-78). The common laparoscopic surgeries included simple nephrectomy (29%), laparoscopy undescended testis (UDT) (19.3%), renal cyst unroofing (13.5%), and radical nephrectomy (13.5%). Hospital stays ranged from 1 to 7 days, depending on the laparoscopic procedure type. Approximately 12.9% of patients required conversion to open surgery, and no major complications or fatalities were observed. Conclusion: The success and complication rates of laparoscopic surgeries in our city align with those reported in the literature. We firmly believe that technological advancements, increasing experience, and improved patient tolerance make laparoscopic surgery a secure and minimally invasive alternative to open procedures. Keywords: Laparoscopic surgery, minimally invasive surgery, urological surgery.
authors: Peri Eriad Yunir

title: Whose business is autism? Exploring the intersecting roles of developmental paediatrics and child and adolescent mental health services
abstract: This opinion article looks at how autism services for children and young people are organised within child development and child and adolescent mental health services. Although both play vital roles, their responsibilities often overlap, which can lead to delays and uncertainty for families. Rising demand, limited resources and differing pathways have added further pressure, especially since the COVID-19 pandemic. The article highlights key challenges, including age cut-offs, gaps in continuity, the need for a collaborative integrated model, the impact of stigma and the difficulties faced by children whose main needs relate to developmental delay. It argues for clearer pathways and more coordinated care.
authors: Yasser Saeed Khan; Mohamed Adil Shah Khoodoruth; Nazim Abdel Aati

title: Discourse in White Coats: Exploring Linguistic Features in Medical Communication
abstract: The aim of this qualitative descriptive research is to examine both the linguistic and discourse-level features of Medical English. The research employs a two-tiered approach: first, a linguistic analysis focusing on morphology, lexical density, syntax, and semantic evolution; second, a discourse analysis examining text organization, genre conventions, interactional patterns, and communicative practices. From a linguistic standpoint, Medical English is distinguished by its specialized terminology, extensive use of Greek and Latin roots, nominalized structures, passive constructions, and an expanding lexicon shaped by advances in numerous disciplines of Medical Sciences. At the discourse level, Medical English operates across multiple genres including clinical documentation, academic publications, and public health communication, each governed by established frameworks such as SOAP notes, IMRD structures, hedging strategies, and standardized phrasing in Medical research. As a result, Medical English has evolved beyond its traditional boundaries, emerging as dynamic and multifaceted domains of communication.
authors: Jameel Ahmad

title: Surgical and functional outcomes of pediatric pancreatic solid pseudopapillary neoplasm: A retrospective study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric pancreatic solid pseudopapillary neoplasm (SPN) is rare, but it represents a clinically important pancreatic tumor in children. The optimal operative strategy remains uncertain, particularly the balance between tumor clearance, postoperative morbidity, and preservation of pancreatic function. This study evaluated surgical, oncologic, and functional outcomes after a selective strategy incorporating parenchyma-preserving procedures. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≤16 years who underwent surgery for pathologically confirmed SPN at a tertiary hospital from January 2021 to December 2024. Clinical, imaging, operative, pathologic, postoperative, recurrence, and pancreatic functional outcomes were reviewed. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients were included; 28 were female (87.5%), and the mean age was 11.1 ± 2.1 years. Abdominal pain was the most common presentation (81.3%). The median tumor diameter was 42.5 mm (range, 19-120). Tumors were located in the pancreatic head in 15 patients (46.8%) and the body/tail in 17 (53.2%). Parenchyma-preserving procedures were performed in 19 patients (59.4%). Distal pancreatectomy was performed in 12 patients, with spleen preservation in 9. Early complications occurred in 5 patients, all with pancreatic head tumors, including one grade C pancreatic fistula that required reoperation. There was no mortality. R0 resection was achieved in 21 patients (65.6%). During a mean follow-up of 34.4 ± 9.8 months, one local recurrence occurred after R1 pancreatic head enucleation and was treated with pancreaticoduodenectomy. No clinically recognized endocrine insufficiency developed. Transient exocrine insufficiency occurred in 11 of 26 assessed patients and resolved in all. Exploratory subgroup analyses were underpowered and did not establish equivalent outcomes between operative strategies or margin groups. CONCLUSIONS: Parenchyma-preserving surgery was feasible in selected children with SPN, but pancreatic head enucleation carried fistula and margin-related concerns. These findings support selective rather than routine pancreatic preservation, with structured long-term surveillance.
authors: Hoan Manh Vu; Hien Duy Pham; Son Cong Nguyen; Nhi Yen Bui; Hoang Viet Nguyen; Nga H. Nguyen; Quang Thanh Nguyen

title: A European algorithm and strategy for management of chronic postoperative inguinal pain (EurA-CPIP)
abstract: Background Chronic postoperative inguinal pain (CPIP) is a disabling complication affecting 8%–17% of all patients after inguinal hernia repair. It is a complex pain condition with several pathophysiological mechanisms involved, including neuropathic pain, inflammation, and mechanical effects (e.g., mesh or scar tissue). Management remains inconsistent, probably due to limited high-quality evidence, heterogeneous approach, and insufficient standardisation of outcomes. This study aimed to develop EurA-CPIP, a multidisciplinary treatment algorithm and prospective data-collection platform designed to support consistent phenotyping, step-up management, and standardised outcomes across centres, creating an iterative platform for future hypothesis-driven research and multicentre trials. Methods An international multidisciplinary working group from European tertiary referral centres developed the European Algorithm and Strategy for Management of Chronic Postoperative Inguinal Pain (EurA-CPIP). Development was informed by the evidence synthesis underpinning the updated international HerniaSurge guidelines and a critical appraisal of previously published CPIP algorithms. A pragmatic step-up algorithm was designed, integrating pharmacological, interventional, surgical and supportive treatments, with prospective outcome registration and planned data-driven revision on a regular basis. Results EurA-CPIP provides a multidisciplinary algorithm with entry at multiple levels depending on prior treatment attempts. The concept is to begin and, if needed, advance from conservative measures such as systemic medication and topical therapy, to more invasive treatments such as trigger point injections, and ultrasound-guided nerve blocks; predefined investigational add-ons (radiofrequency, cryoneurolysis, botulinum toxin A) are embedded after documented block response. Multidisciplinary team review precedes escalation to more invasive interventions such as surgery. A supportive and rehabilitative coping trajectory is integrated early on. Standardised outcomes include patient-reported pain outcomes, functional impairment, psychological factors, analgesic use, and patient global impression of improvement. Conclusion EurA-CPIP is a pragmatic consensus-based strategy intended to harmonise and improve specialised CPIP care while utilising existing and developing emerging therapies. Future research should investigate pathophysiology and intervention effects within this step-up algorithm.
