title: Macro-Cybernetic Architecture of Planetary Systems: Integrating Quantum Epidemiology, Thermodynamic Hysteresis, and Dimensional Topologies
abstract: The complex interplay between microscopic pathogenic emergence, macroscopic geological events, and global sociopolitical shifts presents a significant challenge to classical, isolated scientific disciplines. This paper introduces a unified, interdisciplinary theoretical model—the Macro-Cybernetic Framework—which analyzes the terrestrial biosphere as a highly integrated computational and immunological network. By applying principles of cryptography, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and quantum mechanics to biological and sociological phenomena, this framework proposes several novel mechanisms for planetary-scale events. First, we define "Pathogenic Steganography" and "Interferometric Illumination" to explain the camouflage and subsequent systemic unmasking of pervasive parasitic architectures. Second, we introduce the concept of the "Kinetic Echo" and "Pathological Hysteresis," utilizing classical mechanics and control systems engineering (PID overshoot) to model the thermodynamic lag between the cessation of systemic biological triggers and the physical dissipation of disease, offering a new etiology for post-acute infection syndromes. Third, we propose "Quantum Epidemiology," moving beyond classical vector-based transmission models to account for the simultaneous, non-local activation of pre-distributed dormant pathogens (the biospheric botnet), heavily modulated by the "Friction of Manifestation"—a localized ecological shield comprising climatic, nutritional, and microbial variables. Furthermore, this paper models historical macroeconomic and geopolitical isolationist shifts (the Khaldunian cycle) not as independent political events, but as automated "Geopolitical Tourniquets" and network edge deletions executing planetary autoimmune responses. Finally, the framework applies wave shoaling physics to multidimensional topologies, highlighting the critical vulnerability of modern 2-dimensional transactive memory systems (digital infrastructure) to impending high-kinetic electromagnetic events. Ultimately, this comprehensive matrix provides a robust theoretical foundation for predicting epidemiological trajectories, executing comparative shield extraction via subtractive genomics, and ensuring the resilience of complex civilizational networks.
authors: Seyed Mahyar Shariatpanahi.

title: PSYCHIATRY The Case for Starting Over
abstract: AbstractPsychiatry is the only branch of medicine that still diagnoses without reference to the organ it treats. Psychiatry: The Case for Starting Over argues that this is a structural failure rather than a temporary gap. The descriptive nosology inherited from Kraepelin and formalized in the DSM achieved diagnostic reliability at the cost of validity. Its categories were assembled by committee consensus rather than grounded in mechanism, and so it cannot guide the circuit-targeted therapies now reshaping the field.The book traces this problem historically and then builds an alternative from three converging lines of work. The first is computational neural-network modeling of psychopathology, from Hopfield and Hinton through Hoffman's simulations of schizophrenia and the author's own work. The second is systems neuroscience, including large-scale networks, global workspace and integrated information theories, attractor dynamics, and small-world connectivity. The third is Friston's Free Energy Principle and predictive processing.From this synthesis the book introduces Neuroanalysis and its clinical instrument, Clinical Brain Profiling (CBP). CBP treats mental disorders as disturbances of dynamic brain-network organization and organizes them across four timescales of plasticity:•Cognizance plasticity (milliseconds) is centered on the central executive network and linked to psychosis and negative signs.•Reactive plasticity (minutes to hours) is centered on the salience network and linked to anxiety.•Adaptive plasticity (days to weeks) sits at the salience–default mode interface and is linked to depression and mania.•Developmental plasticity (lifetime) is centered on the default mode network and linked to personality disorder patterns.The book reviews the neuromodulation toolkit: ECT, DBS, TMS, tDCS/tACS, psychedelic-assisted therapy, and focused ultrasound. It then proposes an entity-matched "grammar of plasticity" for selecting, combining, and sequencing these interventions. Guiding principles include strengthening prefrontal regulation before driving motivation, opening plasticity windows before directing them, and continuous biomarker monitoring.Throughout, the author separates established science from theoretical proposal and untested hypothesis. He outlines what validation would require: prospective outcome trials, clinically feasible network measures, and a cultural shift from single-label diagnosis to multidimensional profiling. The result is a case for rebuilding psychiatry as a measurement-based, mechanism-guided clinical neuroscience.
authors: Abraham Peled

title: Neurostimulation in the treatment of psychiatric disorders: Underlying mechanisms and critical analysis of circuit-based interventions
abstract: Neurostimulation of targeted brain regions has emerged as a novel therapeutic approach to induce remission in patients with various psychiatric disorders. This strategy encompasses several modalities, including transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), deep brain stimulation (DBS), and transcranial focused ultrasound neurostimulation (tFUS), all of which aim to modulate dysfunctional neural circuits and restore activity toward physiological ranges. While the clinical efficacy of these techniques is increasingly documented, the mechanisms underlying their effects-beyond immediate changes in regional excitability-remain incompletely understood. Further, neurostimulation represents not only a technical advance, but also a conceptual shift in psychiatry, moving from interventions aimed at modulating neurotransmission or cognition toward circuit-based models of mental illness. This review surveys the current literature to clarify the mechanisms of action of neurostimulation across multiple levels of biological integration, ranging from large-scale neural circuits to cellular and subcellular processes. Subsequently, it explores innovative targets and emerging modalities that expand the scope of circuit-based interventions beyond traditional approaches. Finally, it engages in a critical epistemological reflection, addressing the conceptual challenges that accompany the translation of circuit-based models from neuroscience to clinical psychiatry.
authors: Francis Rodriguez Bambico; Antonine Nicoglou; J Relente; Alexandre Surget; Catherine Belzung

title: Artificial intelligence adoption in accounting and auditing: The technology–organisation–environment (TOE) framework perspective
abstract: Artificial intelligence technology is transforming the structure of accounting and auditing practices and reshaping the operational processes of organizations in these fields. This study aims to evaluate the factors affecting the adoption of artificial intelligence technology in accounting and auditing applications. Professionals from big four auditing firms were included in the scope of the study and semi-structured interviews were conducted. The Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework was used to understand the adoption of artificial intelligence in accounting and auditing practices at the organizational level. The study is important for a better understanding of artificial intelligence adoption at the institution level. The focus was on understanding what was happening in an organizational setting, as opposed to theoretical studies. The findings indicate that environmental factors, particularly regulatory uncertainties and market pressures, may hinder the adoption process. In contrast, organizational factors such as top management support, corporate culture, and institutional participation play a critical role in the effective implementation of AI-based technologies. While data integration and technological infrastructure pose significant technical challenges for large firms, cost constraints and limited resources emerge as key barriers for smaller organizations. In addition, legislation and regulatory pressures for companies are among the critical factors determining adoptation. Thus, in order to successfully implement artificial intelligence adoptation in accounting and auditing, it is necessary to strengthen the technological infrastructure, lead organizational change and adapt to environmental factors.
authors: Betül Şeyma ALKAN

title: Long-timescale dynamics shape visual conscious awareness
abstract: Abstract Consciousness is mostly studied as if it were composed of independent snapshots, aggregating reports over trials and experimental contexts, disregarding any temporal aspect. However, almost nothing is known about how conscious experience spontaneously fluctuates in time. To shed light on the temporal dynamics of conscious awareness, we evaluated the temporal autocorrelation of subjective visibility/confidence reports and objective performance across 20 datasets (N= 335). Two widely used measures of consciousness dissociate in temporal autocorrelation under full spatial attention: subjective measures followed an exponential decay function with long timescales (> 5s), whereas objective accuracy exhibited a slow linear decay function. But both measures share a common underlying temporal fluctuation dynamics, suggesting that the strong autocorrelation in subjective measures cannot be fully attributed to response bias or criterion shift, but might reflect a genuinely aperiodic fluctuation of conscious awareness. Causal transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) suggests that this temporal dependency of subjective measures is read out in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), where a similarly long neural timescale has been demonstrated. Together, these findings establish a temporal constraint for neural models of conscious access: candidate mechanisms should explain not only whether a stimulus becomes consciously accessible, but also how the probability of conscious access evolves over time.
authors: Zefan Zheng; Darinka Trübutschek; Yongchun Cai; Lucía Melloni

title: Neuromodulatory interventions for Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represent an escalating global public health challenge with major socioeconomic consequences. Although anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies have introduced disease-modifying treatment options for early symptomatic AD, their benefits remain modest and must be balanced against cost, monitoring burden, and safety risks. Neuromodulatory interventions have therefore emerged as promising investigational strategies that may complement existing therapeutic approaches. This narrative review evaluates current clinical and neurophysiological evidence for seven major neuromodulation approaches: 40 Hz gamma rhythm sensory stimulation, also known as gamma entrainment using sensory stimulation (GENUS), transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), focused ultrasound (FUS), deep brain stimulation (DBS), and transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM). Integrating clinical findings with mechanistic evidence, we examine synaptic plasticity, neuroinflammation, glymphatic clearance, oscillatory entrainment, and cholinergic signaling as candidate therapeutic mechanisms. A comparative matrix summarizes target specificity, invasiveness, stimulation parameters, and translational status. Finally, we discuss key barriers, including biological heterogeneity, protocol standardization, durability of benefit, caregiver burden, and the uncertain implications of continuous network stimulation for future personalized and closed-loop interventions.
authors: Ruofan Wang; Botao Zhu; Qingda Guo; Jun Steed Huang; Wandong Zhang

title: Behavioral Apathy and its Relationship with Physical Activity, Affective Attitudes, and Motor Cortex Excitability
abstract: Apathy is a multidimensional syndrome characterized by diminished motivation and reduced goal-directed behavior. Although apathy is commonly studied in neurological and psychiatric populations, it is also observed in otherwise healthy adults and may represent an important barrier to engagement in physical activity. Because physical activity requires effort, action initiation, and persistence, individuals with higher levels of behavioral apathy may be less likely to initiate and maintain active behavior. Despite growing interest in the relationship between apathy and physical activity, the behavioral and neurophysiological mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. This thesis examined the relationship between behavioral apathy, physical activity, affective attitudes toward physical activity, and motor cortex neurophysiology. Across four complementary studies, behavioral and neurophysiological pathways that may contribute to reduced physical activity in individuals with higher apathy were investigated. Study 1 is a systematic review and meta-analysis examining the association between apathy and physical activity across clinical and non-clinical populations. Study 2 examined whether intentions, explicit affective attitudes, and approach-avoidance tendencies toward physical activity mediated the relationship between behavioral apathy and physical activity in healthy adults. Study 3 is a systematic review and meta-analysis investigating the association between habitual physical activity and measures of motor cortex neurophysiology, including corticospinal excitability, intracortical inhibition, and intracortical facilitation. Study 4 used transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to examine whether behavioral apathy was associated with these neurophysiological measures in healthy adults. Across the four studies, results demonstrated that apathy is associated with physical activity, but that this association is more strongly explained by motivational and affective processes than by resting-state motor cortex neurophysiology. The systematic review and meta-analysis showed a significant negative association between apathy and physical activity, with stronger associations in older adults and individuals with Parkinson’s disease. Behavioral analyses further demonstrated that higher behavioral apathy was associated with lower physical activity, partly through weaker intentions to be physically active and less positive affective attitudes toward physical activity. Individuals with lower apathy also showed stronger tendencies to approach physical activity stimuli and avoid sedentary stimuli, although these tendencies did not mediate physical activity behavior. In contrast, the neurophysiological studies showed no reliable associations between habitual physical activity and measures of corticospinal excitability, intracortical inhibition, or facilitation. Similarly, behavioral apathy showed negligible associations with these measures, with equivalence testing indicating that any potential effects were too small to be practically meaningful. These results suggest that the relationship between apathy and physical activity is primarily linked to motivational and affective mechanisms rather than stable differences in primary motor cortex neurophysiology. Specifically, higher behavioral apathy was associated with weaker intentions to be physically active and less positive affective attitudes toward physical activity, whereas neither habitual physical activity nor behavioral apathy showed meaningful associations with resting TMS-derived measures of corticospinal excitability or intracortical circuitry. Overall, this thesis refines the understanding of how apathy contributes to physical inactivity and highlights the importance of targeting motivational processes when designing interventions aimed at increasing physical activity engagement.
authors: Ataallah Farajzadeh

title: Competency Development Strategies for Functional Entrepreneurship Development Officers in Indonesia's Ministry of MSMEs
abstract: Background: Functional Entrepreneurship Development Officers (JFPKWU) play an important role in MSME coaching; however, competency development within the newly established Ministry of MSMEs remains uneven, reactive, and lacks a position-specific competency-needs plan. This gap highlights the need to analyze competency development mechanisms and strengthening strategies. Objective: This study aims to analyze competency development strategies for JFPKWU within the Ministry of MSMEs to improve organizational performance and MSME coaching effectiveness. Methods: A qualitative case study approach was employed through in-depth interviews with nine key informants, participatory observation, and document analysis. Data were analyzed using SWOT and TOWS matrices to integrate internal conditions and external factors into strategic recommendations. Results: The findings indicate that JFPKWU competency development is influenced by three dominant factors: top management support, commitment of specialist and generalist officials, and training and development processes, supported by learning styles, organizational complexity, technology utilization, and human resource management functions. Key challenges include inconsistent leadership support, reactive training approaches, limited training participation, and the absence of position-specific competency planning. The study proposes a seven-strategy framework integrating governance strengthening, adaptive digital and hybrid learning, continuous position-based learning, practice-based collaboration, training transformation, HR optimization, and sustainable competency development. Conclusion: Effective JFPKWU competency development requires integrated strategies that align governance, learning systems, human resource management, digital transformation, and collaborative practices to strengthen organizational capacity and improve MSME coaching performance.
authors: Dendy Koswara; Firman Hadi Rivai

title: Neurophysiological and neuromuscular responses associated with the repeated bout effect following eccentric exercise in healthy adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Muscle damage severity decreases after repeated eccentric exercise bouts (the repeated bout effect [RBE]), but whether accompanying neural and neuromuscular changes contribute to protection or arise secondary to reduced damage remains unclear. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared neurophysiological and neuromuscular responses between initial and repeated eccentric bouts in healthy adults. Eight databases were searched from November 1990 to January 2025, and Hedges' g was calculated where outcomes were comparable. Given the small number of contributing studies, all pooled analyses were considered exploratory. Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. Twitch/evoked force showed recovery-compatible point estimates at 24 h (g = 1.02, 95% CI -0.03-2.06) and 48 h (g = 0.50, 95% CI 0.08-0.92). Voluntary activation findings were mixed. TMS-derived voluntary activation produced positive single-study estimates at 24 h (g = 1.10, 95% CI 0.29-1.92) and 48 h (g = 1.06, 95% CI 0.26-1.87), whereas pooled ITT-derived estimates were imprecise at 24 h (g = 0.36, 95% CI -0.92-1.63) and recovery-compatible but based on only two studies at 48 h (g = 0.44, 95% CI 0.03-0.85). M-wave/Mmax showed no consistent between-bout pattern. Corticospinal, intracortical, spinal, reticulospinal, motor-unit and EMG findings were limited, inconsistent or directionally unclear. Neural and neuromuscular changes accompany the RBE, but whether they contribute to protection or reflect reduced damage remains unresolved. Peripheral contractile outcomes showed the most consistent recovery-compatible pattern, whereas evidence concerning central activation and motor-unit behaviour remained limited or inconsistent.
authors: Oliver Hayman; Abdulrahman T Alsowail; Benjamin Griffiths; Stuart R. Gray; Glyn Howatson; Ken Nosaka; Stuart Goodall; Ashlyn K. Frazer; Dawson J. Kidgell

title: Gelişmekte Olan Ekonomi KOBİ’lerinde Üretken Yapay Zekâ Entegrasyonu ve Yönetsel Karar Verme Kalitesi: İstanbul’dan PLS-SEM, NCA ve fsQCA ile Bulgular
abstract: Policy across the emerging world presses small and medium-sized enterprises toward generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), yet enthusiasm has run ahead of firm evidence that channeling managerial reasoning through such tools sharpens the decisions firms actually make. The distinction anchoring the analysis is between holding access to GenAI and weaving it substantively into how managers think; the latter, the depth of integration into managerial cognition, is modeled here as the conduit translating enabling conditions into decision quality within emerging-economy SMEs. Responses from 312 owner-managers and senior managers of Istanbul SMEs are examined through an integrated TOE-TAM lens joining PLS-SEM with Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). Depth of integration drives decision quality (β = 0.612) and process innovation performance (β = 0.574) alike. Top management support and perceived usefulness behave as necessary conditions, each carrying an empirical floor (42% and 38%) beneath which high decision quality never materializes, while three sufficient configurations reach that outcome by separate routes.
authors: Haldun TURAN

title: Digital and Organizational Capabilities for Sustainable Business Performance: The Moderating Role of Top Management Support
abstract: Digital investment does not automatically generate sustainable outcomes; firms require organizational capabilities, analytical decision routines, and supportive leadership conditions to translate technology into economic, environmental, and social value. Drawing on the dynamic capabilities view and contingency theory, this study examines how digital transformation capability, innovation capability, and data-driven decision making are associated with sustainable business performance and whether top management support moderates the relationship between digital transformation capability and sustainable business performance. Survey data obtained from managerial informants representing distinct large Slovenian companies were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that digital transformation capability, innovation capability, and data-driven decision making each showed a positive and statistically significant association with sustainable business performance. The interaction between digital transformation capability and top management support was also positive and statistically significant, indicating that the relationship becomes stronger as management support increases, although the magnitude of this amplification was modest. The study advances a differentiated capability-deployment perspective by distinguishing digitally enabled reconfiguration, innovation execution, and analytical decision routines and by identifying top management support as an amplifying condition.
authors: Katja Crnogaj; Maja Rožman

title: Integration of Top Management Support into the Delone– McLean Model to Enhance Accounting Information Systems Success
abstract: Purpose: This study aims to ascertain how system, information, and service quality and Top Management Support affect accounting information system effectiveness.Methodology: Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) was used as an analysis tool in this quantitative study. The data collection method used was saturated sampling. Data were collected through a questionnaire distributed to 60 respondents with a research sample, namely the director of finance, internal supervisory unit, head of the accounting section, head of the financial planning and evaluation section, and head of the finance section at type B general and special hospitals in Makassar City.Results: The results of the study show that information quality and Top Management Support significantly affect the effectiveness of the accounting information system. The effectiveness of accounting information systems is not significantly impacted by system and service quality.Conclusions: Based on the findings that show that not all factors exert a significant influence or reinforce each other, organizations need to apply a selective approach in the management of accounting information systems.Limitations: The number of available populations is limited and the number of samples successfully collected is small, so the results of the study tend to have a narrow scope and are less representative of real conditions in the fieldContributions: This research provides important insights for organizations, such as hospitals, to optimize the use of information technology to support accounting processes.
authors: Istianah Istianah; Grace Theresia Pontoh; Aini Indrijawati
venue: International Journal of Financial Accounting and Management

title: Adoption Of Business Intelligence Systems in Small and Medium Enterprises: An Integrated TAM-TOE Perspective
abstract: This study investigates the factors influencing the adoption of business intelligence (BI) systems among small and medium enterprises (SMEs). By integrating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) with the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework, this research proposes a comprehensive model that was empirically tested using data collected from 312 SME managers across multiple industries in Indonesia. A quantitative approach was employed using an online survey instrument, and the data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling with Partial Least Squares (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that perceived usefulness, organizational readiness, and competitive pressure are the strongest predictors of BI adoption intention among SMEs. Interestingly, perceived ease of use has a weaker effect than expected, suggesting that SME managers prioritize strategic value over usability when considering BI adoption. Furthermore, top management support positively moderates the relationship between organizational readiness and BI adoption intention. This study extends the theoretical understanding of technology adoption in resource-constrained settings and provides practical recommendations for BI vendors and policymakers targeting the SME market.
authors: Dorris Yadewani; Hendrik Permana; Marjohan .; Salamiah Muhd Kulal
venue: International Journal of Digital Entrepreneurship and Business

title: Determinants influencing digital twin adoption decision in food supply chains
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs) are increasingly recognised as a promising solution for food supply chains (FSCs). However, existing DT research has focused mainly on conceptual development, technical applications, and pilot implementations, providing limited empirical evidence on the determinants influencing firms' adoption decisions. Thus, this study examines the determinants of DT adoption decisions in FSCs. Drawing on Diffusion of Innovation theory and the technology-organisation-environment (TOE) framework, the study develops a research model explaining how TOE factors shape firms' adoption decisions. Survey data from 260 respondents in food and technology-related firms across Western economies are analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Results show that compatibility, technology readiness, top management support, competitive pressure, and market uncertainty significantly influence the DT adoption decision, while complexity negatively affects adoption. Findings indicate that the DT adoption decision in FSCs is shaped not only by perceived technological characteristics but also by organisational support and external environmental pressures.
authors: Ying Huang; Abhijeet Ghadge; Nicky Yates
venue: International Journal of Logistics Research and Applications

title: Top Management Support and Technology Infrastructure in Maintaining the Success of Electronic Medical Records
abstract: The implementation of Electronic Medical Records (EMR) is an essential part of hospital digital transformation aimed at improving the quality, efficiency, and accountability of healthcare services. The success of EMR implementation is not solely determined by system readiness, but is also strongly influenced by top management support and the readiness of technological infrastructure. This study aims to analyze the role of top management support and technological infrastructure readiness in maintaining the successful use of EMR at Ratu Aji Putri Botung Regional General Hospital, Penajam Paser Utara Regency. This research employed a qualitative approach using a case study method. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation. The study involved seven informants consisting of hospital leaders, administrative managers, information technology personnel, and healthcare workers as direct users of the EMR system. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive qualitative techniques through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The results indicate that top management support plays a significant role in maintaining the success of EMR implementation through policy formulation, budget allocation, usage monitoring, as well as training and assistance for users. In addition, the readiness of technological infrastructure has generally supported the use of EMR, although limitations remain in terms of device distribution, network stability, and system development. Overall, the success of EMR implementation at Ratu Aji Putri Botung Regional General Hospital is influenced by the synergy between leadership commitment and sustainable technological infrastructure readiness.
authors: Mamik Hidayati; Sadly Abdul Djabar; Nurmadhani Fitri Suyuthi

title: Systematic Literature Review: The Effect of Green Financing, Green Fintech, and Green Investment on Customer Loyalty with Top Management Support as a Moderation Variable
abstract: This study aims to analyze the contribution of green financing, green fintech, and green investment to the loyalty of banking customers, by placing top management support as a moderation variable. Using the Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method, this study examines various international scientific articles published in 2020–2026 through the stages of identification, screening, inclusion selection, and narrative synthesis analysis. The results of the research show that green financing, technology, and investment have a positive effect on binding customer loyalty because it is effective in boosting the bank's image, trust, and commitment to environmental sustainability. Specifically, green financing builds a reputation through funding environmentally friendly projects, green fintech optimizes consumer experience through efficient digital services, and green investment strengthens the allure of banks in the eyes of investors and the public. Furthermore, top management involvement is proving crucial in strengthening the execution of this strategy through policy legitimacy, resource allocation, and the formation of a sustainable organizational culture. As a result, success in maintaining long-term customer loyalty does not only rely on the adoption of green innovations, but also depends on how strong the commitment shown by the company's top leadership is strong
authors: Kastriyana Kastriyana; Muhammad Iqbal Fasa; Anas Malik
venue: INTERDISIPLIN Journal of Qualitative and Quantitative Research

title: Decision-making styles, organizational ıinnovativeness, and change fatigue in healthcare
abstract: Introduction and Objective: Decision-making styles, organizational innovativeness, and change fatigue are three interrelated variables in healthcare management. This study aimed to explore health managers' experiences and perceptions of these variables and identify the individual, organizational, and contextual factors shaping their dynamics. Materials and Methods: Semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted with 15 health managers from private healthcare institutions in Istanbul, Turkey, representing lower, middle, and upper management equally. Data were collected between April–October 2025 and analyzed through thematic analysis. Findings and Conclusions: Three main themes emerged: (1) Reasons for resistance to change and innovation (13 sub-themes including habitual resistance, staff turnover, and change fatigue from unplanned changes); (2) Facilitators of change and innovation (13 sub-themes including top management support, digitalization, and ownership capacity); (3) The influence of decision-making styles (7 sub-themes including inclusive decision-making, evidence-based rationality, and crisis-induced necessity). Inclusive and evidence-based styles were positively associated with innovativeness; change fatigue adversely affected both innovativeness and decision-making.Participatory and evidence-based decision-making styles are positively associated with organizational innovativeness and may mitigate change fatigue. These findings carry actionable implications for health managers and policymakers.
authors: Funda Topak; Ramazan Özgür ÇATAR

title: Understanding Internet of Everything adoption in manufacturing SMEs: Insights from the technology-organization-environment model
abstract: Adoption of the Internet of Everything (IoE) refers to how individuals, organizations, or industries implement and integrate IoE technologies into their operations, services, or daily practices. It involves using connected devices (as in IoT) and the intelligent coordination of people, processes, data, and things to create a unified digital ecosystem. This research examines the determinants of Internet of Everything (IoE) adoption within technological, organizational, and environmental contexts, conceptualizing IoE adoption as the dependent variable. A quantitative methodology was employed, with data collected from 169 organizational respondents and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The study investigates six independent variables: perceived usefulness, perceived cost, top management support, organizational readiness, government regulation support, and market competitive pressure. The Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) theory served as the underpinning theory. The empirical findings reveal that perceived usefulness, top management support, and organizational readiness significantly influence IoE adoption. However, perceived cost, government regulation support, and market competitive pressure do not demonstrate significant effects. These results suggest that internal organizational factors, particularly leadership commitment and readiness, are more pivotal in driving IoE adoption than external pressures or financial considerations. This study contributes to the growing body of literature on digital transformation by offering a nuanced understanding of adoption dynamics in emerging technological ecosystems. Practitioners are encouraged to strengthen organizational preparedness and engage top management early in the adoption process to enhance the success of IoE initiatives.
authors: Muhamad Irham Ibrahim; Nur Azimah Ahmad; Hasnizam Shaari

title: Challenges of implementing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems in Bangladesh
abstract: Goal: This study examines why Bangladeshi companies struggle to adopt ERP systems, looking at organizational, technical, and human hurdles. By combining the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Critical Success Factors (CSF) frameworks, it shows how user acceptance and organizational readiness directly drive ERP success. Methodology: A sequential exploratory mixed-method design was used. First, a PRISMA-guided literature review mapped out key ERP challenges to shape the survey. Questionnaires were then gathered from 30 professionals across multiple Bangladeshi sectors with hands-on ERP experience. Finally, the data was analyzed using descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, one-sample t-tests, and Cohen’s d to evaluate reliability, significance, and practical effect size. Results: Cronbach’s alpha was 0.560, indicating moderate internal consistency. All seven ERP challenges were statistical significant. Budget limitations, lack of training and support, shortage of skilled personnel and maintenance costs demonstrated strong practical effects, whereas data migration, employee resistance and weak top management support also emerged as significant barriers. Limitations: The study is exploratory, cross-sectional, and based on a small sample. Practical implications: Organizations should focus on training, budgeting, skilled teams, leadership support, change management, and data governance. Originality/Value: The study adds Bangladesh-based ERP evidence using an integrated TAM-CSF perspective.
authors: Muhammad Abdus Samad; Jonayed Abdullah; Kulsuma Begum Rumina; Mostafijur Rahman; MD. Mohibullah Sabbir
venue: Brazilian Journal of Operations & Production Management

title: Knowledge Sharing Behavior among Vietnamese Academics: The Dominant Roles of Organizational Culture and Leadership
abstract: Background/ problem: While knowledge sharing is vital for academic innovation and institutional performance, its behavioral determinants in emerging higher education systems remain inconclusive, particularly regarding the assumed facilitating role of information technology (IT). Objective/ purpose: Grounded primarily in social exchange theory, this study investigates the effects of organizational culture, top management support, and personality traits on knowledge sharing behavior among university lecturers, while also examining the moderating role of IT. Design and Methodology: A cross-sectional quantitative survey was administered to 185 academic staff across universities in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and multigroup analysis (MGA). Results: The model explains 56.0% of the variance in knowledge sharing behavior (R2 = .56). Organizational culture (β = .42, p < .001, f 2 = .34) and top management support (β = .38, p < .001, f 2 = .32) emerged as dominant drivers with medium-to-large effect sizes. Extraversion exerted a significant positive impact (β = .32, p < .001, f 2 = .20), whereas introversion exhibited a small negative effect (β = -.11, p = .03, f 2 = .03). Conversely, IT had neither a significant direct effect (β = .09, p = .07, f 2 = .02) nor a moderating effect on organizational relationships. MGA revealed no significant gender differences. Conclusion and Implications: Findings demonstrate that knowledge sharing is fundamentally a socially embedded behavioral process. Technological infrastructure cannot substitute for interpersonal trust, collaborative norms, and supportive leadership in fostering academic knowledge exchange.
authors: Bao-Huy Dinh; Ngoc-Thin Chau

title: BIM-Supported green building adoption in the construction industry
abstract: The construction industry is under growing pressure to embrace digital technologies that advance sustainable infrastructure and support the transition toward smart cities. Building Information Modeling (BIM) has emerged as a key enabler of green building practices, yet its adoption across construction organizations remains uneven and the factors shaping this adoption are not fully understood. This study investigates the determinants influencing BIM-supported green building adoption and examines its contribution to smart and sustainable city development. Drawing on the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework and Diffusion of Innovation (DOI) theory, an integrated model was developed to assess the effects of technological competence, top management support, organizational readiness, external support, environmental sustainability orientation, and relative advantage on BIM-supported green building adoption. Survey data were collected from 389 construction professionals, including architects, engineers, project managers, and BIM coordinators, and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS. The results reveal that technological competence (β = 0.399), top management support (β = 0.378), and relative advantage (β = 0.317) are the strongest drivers of BIM-supported green building adoption, while environmental sustainability orientation, external support, and organizational readiness exert smaller but significant positive effects. More broadly, these determinants of BIM-supported green building adoption are relevant to the wider goal of smart and sustainable city development, given the role of green buildings in enabling data-driven design, lifecycle performance analysis, and environmentally responsible urban decision-making. This study extends technology adoption research by integrating TOE and DOI perspectives within a sustainability-driven construction context offers practical guidance for construction firms and policymakers operating in similar rapidly developing, sustainability-focused markets.
authors: Khaled A. Alrasheed; Abdulaziz Alotaibi; Abdullah O. Baarimah; Aawag Moshen Alawag; Hamad Almujibah; Madhusudhan Bangalore Ramu

title: Factors Influencing Industry 4.0 Adoption among Small and Medium Enterprises in Southeast Vietnam: An Integrated Technology-Organization-Environment-Resource-Based View-Diffusion of Innovation Framework
abstract: The Industry 4.0 paradigm transforms how firms manufacture products, create value in digitalized markets, and sustain competitive advantage; nevertheless, the use of fourth industrial revolution technology among Vietnamese SMEs is confined. This work investigates the determinants of Industry 4.0 adoption for SMEs in Southeast Vietnam based on the integrated framework of the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) model, the Resource-Based View (RBV), and the Diffusion of Innovation (DOI) theory. A sequential mixed-methods design was utilized. After refining and validating the measurement scales using qualitative inquiry and pilot studies, data were collected from 416 SME executives and analyzed with PLS-SEM. The findings suggest that external support plays the largest role for the Industry 4.0 adoption process, followed by support from top management, risk-taking culture, financial capability, human resource capability, competitive pressure, and perceived relative advantage. Conversely, technological complexity is detrimental to the technology adoption process. The culture of risk-taking acts as a mediator between organizational resources and technology adoption, while impacts of support from leadership and risk-taking culture are heightened in contexts of market turbulence. Theoretically, it contributes to the TOE literature by combining RBV and DOI perspectives, highlighting how organizational resources are converted into adoption outcomes through a risk-taking organisational culture. Practically, it provides policy-makers, industrial associations and SME managers with insights into promoting the accelerated digital transformation and stronger implementation of Industry 4.0.
authors: Pham Quang van; Vo Thanh Thu
venue: International Review of Management and Marketing

title: The role of emotional intelligence and empathy as personal resources in enhancing employee performance in the IT industry: a job demands-resources perspective
abstract: This study investigates the relationships among Organisational Ethics (ETH), Interpersonal Relationships (IR), Job Autonomy (AUT), Support from Top Management (STM), Job Demands, Job Resources, Emotional Intelligence (EI) and Empathy (EMP) and Employee Performance (EP) within the IT (Information Technology) Industry through the JD-R (Job Demands-Resources) theory. This study examines how organisational and job-related factors are associated with Job demands and Job resources which are subsequently associated with Emotional Intelligence, Empathy and Employee Performance. Given the limitations from the previous empirical studies on EI and EMP as personal resources in IT industry context, this research aims to fill this gap by investigating the association of these personal resources with EP with a special focus on the IT industry. A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured questionnaire administered through a survey among IT employees working in different management and technical positions in Bengaluru, India. Around 318 valid responses were collected and analysed using SPSS and Jamovi. Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) was used to analyse the relationships among the constructs. The findings indicate that Emotional Intelligence and Empathy are significantly positively associated with Employee Performance in the IT industry. Further, the significant association of Job demands and Job resources with EI and EMP indicates the significance of workplace conditions in shaping employees’ emotional capabilities. This study applies the JD-R framework to examine EI and EMP as personal resources connecting job characteristics with employee performance outcomes in the IT industry. These research findings contribute to the literature of EP by providing practical insights for the IT industry seeking to enhance employee performance by developing emotional competencies and creating a supportive work culture.
authors: V. Lakshmi Voleti; Meenakshi Verma

title: Транскраниальная магнитная стимуляция в сочетании с когнитивной провокацией и интегративной психотерапией улучшает отказ от курения
abstract: Введение. Применение транскраниальной магнитной стимуляции (рТМС) с предварительной когнитивной провокацией в сочетании с интегративной психотерапией формируют надежную стратегию совладания у лиц с синдромом табачной зависимости. Цель. Повысить эффективность лечения лиц с синдромом зависимости от табака путем комплексного воздействия на физический и психологический компоненты патологического влечения. Материалы и методы. В основную группу вошли 60 респондентов с диагнозом по МКБ 10: F 17.2 – синдром зависимости от табака, мужского и женского пола, в возрасте 18–44 года, проходивших курс комплексного лечения с применением высокочастотной рТМС на левую дорсолатеральную префронтальную кору и медиальную префронтальную кору с предварительной когнитивной провокацией в сочетании с интегративной психотерапией. Результаты. Метод лечения лиц с синдромом зависимости от табака, с использованием транскраниальной магнитной стимуляции и интегративной психотерапии прошли 60 человек. Средний возраст составил 32,5±12,3 года. Процедуры транскраниальной магнитной стимуляции проводились с частотой до 2 раз в неделю: от 5 до 9 процедур прошли 78% человек, 10 процедур 16% человек, остальные 2% до 3 процедур и 4% до 15 сеансов. Сеансы интегративной психотерапии в индивидуальном формате проводились с частотой до 2 раз в неделю прошли 60 человек: от 5 до 9 процедур прошли 53% человек, 10 процедур 45% человек, и 3% до 12 сеансов. Полностью прекратили употребление табака 48 (76%) человека, остальные 16 (24%) человек находились в состоянии контролируемого приема и готовности к отказу. Отмечено снижение тревожности после курса лечения: ситуативной тревожности (с 51,5±12,3 до 40,7±10,0 баллов, p<0,001), личностной тревожности (с 50,4±14,2 до 45,9±10,0 баллов, p=0,021), усиление внутреннего локуса контроля в сферах достижений, неудач и профессиональной деятельности, развитие адаптивных копинг-стратегий (принятие ответственности и планирование), уменьшение отрицания проблемы и повышение готовности к активным действиям по отказу от курения. Заключение. Нормализация уровня тревожности после проведения транскраниальной магнитной стимуляции и интегративной психотерапии зависимых от табака лиц подтверждает снижение эмоционального дистресса и ослабление одного из основных триггеров курения – стресс-индуцированной тяги, повышение стрессоустойчивости и способности к саморегуляции в провоцирующих курение ситуациях. Активация схемы зависимости путем когнитивной провокации делает ее более поддающейся модуляции, где рТМС может открыть «окно пластичности», и поведенческое вмешательство интегративной психотерапии может быть более эффективным. Полученные данные демонстрируют высокую клиническую эффективность разработанного метода лечения, основанного на использовании интегративной психотерапии и транскраниальной магнитной стимуляции у зависимых от табака лиц. Introduction. The use of transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) with preliminary cognitive provocation in combination with integrative psychotherapy forms a reliable coping strategy in individuals with tobacco dependence syndrome. Purpose. To improve the effectiveness of treatment for individuals with tobacco dependence syndrome through a comprehensive approach to the physical and psychological components of pathological craving. Materials and methods. The study group included 60 respondents with an ICD-10 diagnosis of F17.2 – tobacco dependence syndrome, male and female, aged 18–44 years, who underwent a course of comprehensive treatment using high-frequency rTMS to the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and medial prefrontal cortex with preliminary cognitive provocation in combination with integrative psychotherapy. Results. A total of 60 people underwent a treatment method for tobacco dependence syndrome using transcranial magnetic stimulation and integrative psychotherapy. The average age was 32.5±12.3 years. Transcranial magnetic stimulation procedures were performed up to twice a week: 78% of people underwent 5 to 9 procedures, 16% of people underwent 10 procedures, the remaining 2% up to 3 procedures, and 4% up to 15 sessions. 60 people underwent individual integrative psychotherapy sessions up to twice a week: 53% of people underwent 5 to 9 procedures, 45% of people underwent 10 procedures, and 3% up to 12 sessions. 48 (76%) people completely quit smoking, the remaining 16 (24%) people were in a state of controlled use and readiness to quit. A decrease in anxiety was noted after the course of treatment: situational anxiety (from 51.5±12.3 to 40.7±10.0 points, p<0.001), personal anxiety (from 50.4±14.2 to 45.9±10.0 points, p=0.021), strengthening of the internal locus of control in the areas of achievements, failures and professional activity, development of adaptive coping strategies (acceptance of responsibility and planning), reduction of denial of the problem and increased readiness for active steps to quit smoking. Conclusion. The obtained data demonstrate the high clinical efficacy of the developed treatment method based on the use of integrative psychotherapy and transcranial magnetic stimulation in persons with tobacco dependence.
authors: И.В. Григорьева; М.И. Тукало; Ю.М. Каминская

title: Motor cortex pain compensation is modifiable: allostatic load degrades its analgesic efficiency and rehabilitation restores it
abstract: The primary motor cortex is a critical hub for pain control, yet its few identified regulatory mechanisms - intracortical inhibition and oscillatory markers - predict symptoms inconsistently. The prevailing view holds that pain results from reduced inhibition, a fixed deficit, rather than from resistance to inhibition that rehabilitation can reverse. Here we show that motor cortex pain compensation is instead a modifiable state whose analgesic efficiency depends on allostatic load. In a fibromyalgia trial and a knee osteoarthritis cohort assessed with parallel EEG and transcranial magnetic stimulation, a signature combining central theta asymmetry and intracortical inhibition was unrelated or inversely related to symptom burden under low allostatic load but positively related to it under high load in fibromyalgia, and its protective association was attenuated under high load in osteoarthritis - the same signal carrying different clinical meaning. A burden-adjusted index modelled on the homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance was elevated under high load, predicted improvement after rehabilitation beyond baseline severity, and fell in responders but not in non-responders; in both cohorts the neurophysiological component itself recalibrated with response. Motor cortex compensation is thus degraded by allostatic load and restored by rehabilitation.
authors: Felipe Fregni; Marta Imamura; Lucas Camargo; Kevin Pacheco‐Barrios; Anna Lepesteur Gianlorenco; Linamara Rizzo Battistella; Wolnei Caumo

title: Connectome guided approaches to cognitive rehabilitation after stroke
abstract: Abstract Stroke is among the major causes of disability around the world, and cognitive deficits remain one of the most disabling and consistently overlooked consequences. Standard rehabilitative techniques often struggle to promote the neural reorganization needed to foster long-lasting improvement in patients’ cognitive skills because they do not account for patients’ personal network-level pathology. Connectome refers to the complete set of structural and functional connections within the brain and offers a groundbreaking tool for understanding cognitive impairment following strokes and guiding treatment. This narrative review highlights how current research demonstrates the role stroke plays in disrupting large-scale cognitive networks, namely the default mode network, the frontoparietal network, and the salience network. We then discuss how connectome analysis may help tailor personalized therapy by aiding decision-making, allowing clinicians to target specific brain areas when applying treatments such as transcranial magnetic stimulation, tDCS, neurofeedback, brain-computer interface technologies, virtual reality, and behavior-based interventions (language training, attention training). We further clarify which observations are well-established and where the field still relies on emerging data to inform predictions regarding the efficacy of different interventions. Limitations in predictive modeling of stroke-related connectomic alterations will be highlighted (reproducibility issues, limited sample sizes, and lack of consensus on image-acquisition protocols). It outlines the process for translating knowledge into practice. Potential future avenues for research include serial neuroimaging, machine learning, omics biomarkers, and behavioral targets. Connectomics is not an intervention but represents the scientific basis needed for making interventions more efficient.

title: Corticospinal tract structure and descending motor output following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: an exploratory multimodal neuroimaging assessment
abstract: Background: Functional and structural differences in the central nervous system, including higher motor cortex activation, lower corticospinal excitability, and smaller corticospinal tract volume have been proposed as potential contributors to persistent quadriceps strength deficits following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR). However, prior work has largely examined these differences using isolated single modality neuroimaging approaches, limiting integration across brain activation, corticospinal excitability, and neural structure. Therefore, our primary aim was to compare neurophysiological and neurostructural outcomes between individuals with ACLR and uninjured individuals (CON) and to explore whether corticospinal tract (CST) volume conditioned the association between (1) cortical activation and corticospinal excitability and (2) corticospinal excitability and quadriceps strength. Methods: Nineteen right-foot dominant individuals, including 10 with a history of unilateral ACLR and 9 CON participated in the current study. Brain activation in primary motor cortex while performing a supine knee flexion-extension task, CST volume, and corticospinal excitability was measured by functional magnetic resonance imaging, diffusion tensor imaging, and transcranial magnetic stimulation, respectively. Group comparison and correlation analyses were conducted to evaluate the difference in quadriceps strength, brain activation, CST volume, and corticospinal excitability between the two groups and to measure association between these variables for each group, respectively. Exploratory moderation analyses were conducted to evaluate association between motor cortex activation, corticospinal excitability and MVIC, while determining whether this association is moderated by the structural volume of the CST. Results: Compared with controls, ACLR participants demonstrated higher active motor threshold, lower motor evoked potential (MEP) amplitude, and lower CST volume. CST volume was positively associated with MEP amplitude in the ACLR group. Exploratory moderation analyses yielded nominal interaction effects suggesting that CST volume may condition the relationships between task-related primary motor cortex activation and MEP amplitude, and between MEP amplitude and quadriceps strength in the ACLR group. Comparable interaction effects were not statistically detectable in controls. Conclusion: Individuals with ACLR demonstrated neurophysiological and neurostructural differences despite comparable quadriceps strength. Exploratory findings raise the hypothesis that CST volume may influence cross-modal relationships among brain activation, corticospinal excitability, and quadriceps strength after ACLR, highlighting the potential value of integrating structural and functional measures when evaluating the descending motor system. These findings provide a foundation for larger longitudinal investigations examining how CST structure interacts with neurophysiological function and motor recovery following ACLR.

title: Simulation-based optimization of look up tables for TMS ASM operation at the Large Binocular Telescope
abstract: Gravity and temperature induced deformations in extremely large telescopes are commonly compensated using look up tables (LUTs). At the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT), the existing LUTs were derived from focal plane aberration minimization and do not explicitly enforce geometric constraints required for metrology operation. They also do not account for rapid environmental variations or long-term structural evolution. We present a simulation-based framework that integrates the Telescope Metrology System into the control strategy to redesign the LUTs. A sequential optical model of the LBT was used to reproduce the active optics loop and to evaluate the sensitivity of wavefront error and pointing to Adaptive Secondary Mirror rigid body motions. The optimized LUTs will be validated through dedicated on sky tests to assess their suitability for routine operation.
authors: Byeongjoon Jeong; Luca Rosignoli; Heejoo Choi; John M. Hill; Brandon Mechtley; Olga Kühn; Gabriele Rodeghiero; C. Veillet; J. Chu

title: Reorienting TMS treatments for fear memories and posttraumatic stress disorder. The emerging potential of the anterior prefrontal cortex
abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is characterized by re-experiencing trauma through vivid and involuntary intrusions, avoidance of cues that could trigger traumatic memories, and alterations in mood and cognition. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) offers a promising approach to modulating activity and functional coupling within neural circuits underlying these processes. To date, TMS studies in fear-conditioning research and PTSD have mainly focused on dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) and ventromedial (vmPFC)-connected or broader medial-prefrontal (mPFC) targets, yielding encouraging but heterogeneous effects on posttraumatic symptoms. In parallel, emerging evidence has implicated the anterior prefrontal cortex (aPFC; Brodmann area 10) in threat- and trauma-related processes, including memory retrieval, higher-order control of defensive responding, adaptive strategy selection, and resilience. Whereas the dlPFC and vmPFC have been incorporated into mechanistic models of fear regulation, the aPFC has received limited attention in theoretical frameworks of fear and PTSD. Here, we review TMS studies organized around dlPFC, vmPFC-connected or mPFC, and aPFC neuroanatomical targets, integrating evidence from experimental and clinical research. Based on the hierarchical model of prefrontal organization, we argue that these regions represent potential TMS targets or circuit nodes, but likely act on partially distinct mechanisms. The vmPFC appears primarily involved in early automatic downregulation of defensive responses; the dlPFC may support cognitive control strategies such as reappraisal; and the aPFC may enable a supraordinate influence over higher-order representations and avoidance-related circuitry, as well as flexible selection of emotion-regulation strategies. We conclude that integrating the aPFC into this framework may guide next-generation, mechanistically-informed TMS treatments for PTSD.
authors: Alba Chiara La Pastina; Eugenio Manassero; Benedetto Sacchetti

title: NESTApp: A GUI-Based MATLAB Application for Auditable TMS-EEG Preprocessing with EEGLAB
abstract: Abstract Electroencephalography (EEG) preprocessing determines signal quality and interpretation, particularly for transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with EEG (TMS-EEG), where recordings are affected by large and complex stimulation-related artifacts. Several preprocessing approaches have been developed, but substantial variability remains in how pipelines are implemented, documented, and evaluated across recordings, limiting reproducibility and comparability across studies. We developed NESTApp, a MATLAB-based graphical interface built on EEGLAB, to provide an accessible and reproducible framework for implementing and evaluating TMS-EEG preprocessing pipelines. Rather than prescribing a specific pipeline, NESTApp allows users to construct and consistently apply customisable workflows incorporating established EEGLAB and TMS-EEG processing tools, while automatically documenting processing decisions and parameters. Integrated quality-control procedures track data removal and flag recordings based on user-defined criteria, facilitating systematic evaluation across participants. The application also supports group-level visualisation and export of processed TMS-EEG measures for subsequent analyses. Applied to 29 recordings from 16 participants, NESTApp processed 27 and identified those requiring further inspection. By integrating pipeline implementation, documentation, quality control, and group-level evaluation within a single interface, NESTApp provides a transparent framework for TMS-EEG preprocessing that may improve reproducibility, facilitate consistent processing across cohorts, and lower technical barriers to the implementation of established preprocessing approaches.

title: Spinal Recurrent Inhibition Shapes the Dynamics of TMS-induced Motor-Evoked Potentials: A Computational Modeling Study
abstract: Abstract Motor-evoked potentials (MEPs) recorded via surface electromyography (EMG) from peripheral muscles following transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) of the motor cortex reflect the integrity of the entire corticospinal pathway and are widely used in both basic neuroscience and clinical practice. However, the relative contributions of spinal and peripheral mechanisms to the observed MEP waveform remain poorly understood, partly because computational models that capture individual MEP characteristics are lacking. Here, we present a biologically plausible and computationally efficient model of the descending motor pathway, spanning the spinal cord and hand muscles, that can be fitted to individual MEP waveforms across a range of TMS intensities. The model successfully reproduces individual MEP waveforms, accounting for approximately 90% of the observed variance in waveforms across 10 healthy participants. Crucially, we demonstrate that recurrent inhibition of Renshaw cells in the spinal cord is indispensable for reproducing the fine temporal structure of MEP waveforms, even when input-output curve fitting appears adequate without it. Beyond waveform reproduction, the fitted model provides interpretable estimates of latent neural dynamics and subject-specific pathway parameters, including motor neuron size distribution, synaptic receptor balance, axonal conduction delay, and hand muscle refractoriness, that are consistent with known biological ranges. These results suggest that individual MEP waveforms, when analyzed using a biologically grounded model, carry substantially more information about spinal and peripheral motor pathway integrity than conventional amplitude-based measures alone.
authors: Vincent S.C. Chien; Eleonora Bernasconi; Erik Müller; Peng Wang; Madeleine M. Lowery; Jérémy Liegey; Karen Wendt; Jacinta O’Shea; Timothy Denison; Jaroslav Hlinka; Thomas R. Knösche; Konstantin Weise; HELMUT J. SCHMIDT

title: Causal evidence for the role of dorsolateral prefrontal cortex in the implementation of cognitive control adjustments
abstract: Abstract Cognitive control processes enable us to use recent contextual information to flexibly adapt to current task demands. This ability to adapt control processes is exhibited in response conflict tasks. In these tasks, participants must respond to a relevant piece of information while overcoming the tendency to respond to task-irrelevant information that cues an automatic or habitual response. Control demands can be updated in these tasks via two separate routes. Both errors and conflict between task-irrelevant and task-relevant information affect performance on subsequent trials. A body of work has implicated dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) in implementing these control adjustments. However, this work has primarily relied on correlational techniques or focused on a single index of control adaptation. Here, we combine inhibitory transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) over DLPFC with computational modeling of behavior to test the causal role of DLPFC in control adaptation. We show that inhibitory TMS to DLPFC reduces the effect of previous trial conflict, and committing an error on the previous trial further reduces adaptive effects. This result provides causal evidence for DLPFC playing a general role in implementing trial-to-trial control adjustments.

title: Cognitive state dependent enhancement of cognitive control with transcranial magnetic stimulation
abstract: Abstract Background Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is an effective treatment for major depressive disorder (MDD), yet variability of therapeutic responses remains high. A key contributor to this variability may be state-dependent effects of brain stimulation, where activity in underlying circuits can shape the propagation of TMS-evoked activity. Thus, constraining the target circuits’ state by engaging cognition may make TMS’ effects more consistent. Objective We tested whether TMS’ effects on cognitive control, a transdiagnostic construct implicated across psychiatric disorders and a putative mediator of TMS efficacy, are state-dependent. Methods Participants (N = 25) completed a context-dependent behavioural assay of cognitive control before and after we delivered rTMS to the prefrontal cortex (PFC). During rTMS, participants performed either the cognitive control task (active-state TMS), or performed a context-independent perceptual task (control-state TMS). We assessed changes in downstream behavioural metrics of circuit function, as well as neural indices of cognitive control measured from electroencephalography (EEG). Results rTMS enhanced downstream readouts of cognitive control only when stimulation was delivered concurrent with the cognitive control task. Similarly, only active-state TMS modulated theta band oscillatory activity, which is thought to be a marker of cognitive control engagement Conclusion These findings demonstrate that TMS’ effects on cognitive control are state-dependent, in which endogenous engagement of PFC-anchored networks can shape the magnitude and functional relevance of TMS-induced plasticity. Considering cognitive states during TMS may therefore offer a framework to enhance and/or accelerate TMS’ therapeutic effects.
authors: Aaron N. McInnes; Victoria L Pipia; Kiyana L Maynard; Güldamla Kalender; Alik S. Widge

title: Accelerated TMS is associated with changes of subgenual cingulate–default mode network coupling in depression: an observational 7 Tesla fMRI study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation (aTMS) is an effective treatment for depression, but its neurobiological mechanisms of action remain to be elucidated. This study used high-resolution 7-Tesla MRI to investigate changes in resting-state functional connectivity (rs-FC) of the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC) following a treatment series of aTMS. We hypothesized a decrease in sgACC rs-FC with key cortical regions of the default mode network (DMN), reflecting a downregulation of a network that is overactive in depression. METHODS: Twenty-two patients with current depression underwent 7-Tesla MRI scans before and after a two-week aTMS treatment series (24,000 pulses) targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Fourteen healthy participants were also scanned twice as a control group. Longitudinal changes in sgACC seed-based rs-FC were compared between groups. Furthermore, group differences were assessed at baseline and at follow-up. Exploratory correlations between longitudinal changes in sgACC rs-FC, depression severity, mindfulness, and affect were also evaluated. RESULTS: There was a reduction in rs-FC between the sgACC and bilateral precunei, and between sgACC and left frontal pole in patients receiving aTMS. At baseline, patients had increased rs‑FC between the sgACC and a cluster including the left precuneus and a cluster in the right superior frontal gyrus. Exploratory correlations suggest an association between sgACC-precunei rs-FC changes and mindfulness (p = 0.008, uncorrected for multiple comparisons), while no associations were found with depression severity or affect. CONCLUSIONS: Treatment with aTMS is associated with a reduction in rs‑FC between the sgACC and the DMN. Exploratory correlations with mindfulness warrant replication in larger, independent samples.
authors: Tobias Bracht; Pascal Borel; Stefan Dendorfer; Leila Maria Soravia; Kristina Adorjan; Sebastian Walther; Andrea Federspiel; Roland Wiest; Gianluca Andri Florineth; Niklaus Denier

title: Heterogeneity and Ontogeny of Mouse Thymic Macrophages Reveal a Requirement for Csf1r-Expressing Myeloid Cells During Early T Cell Development
abstract: Thymic macrophages (TMs) maintain tissue homeostasis by clearing the large numbers of apoptotic cells generated during T cell development, but how TM heterogeneity relates to their developmental origin and role in thymocyte maturation remains incompletely understood. Using complementary flow-cytometric, single-cell transcriptomic, and genetic approaches, we resolved two major TM populations corresponding to TIMD4+ cortical and CX3CR1+ medullary/cortico-medullary macrophages. TIMD4+ VCAM1+ TMs displayed a prominent efferocytosis and apoptotic-cell-clearance program, whereas TIMD4− VCAM1+ TMs were enriched for antigen-presentation and interferon-response pathways. Fate mapping revealed unequal progenitor contributions to these populations, and CCR2 deficiency selectively reduced TIMD4− VCAM1+ TMs and thymic monocytes, supporting ongoing input from circulating precursors. Exploratory pseudotime analysis further identified a transcriptional continuum from Ly6c2+ Ccr2+ monocytes toward macrophage states. Using MaFIA fetal thymic organ cultures, AP20187-mediated depletion of Csf1r-expressing myeloid cells reduced CD4+CD8+ thymocyte differentiation and produced a coordinated accumulation of DN3 cells, loss of DN4 cells, and reduction in CD27 expression. These convergent changes identify the DN3-to-DN4 transition as a developmental stage that requires an intact Csf1r-expressing myeloid compartment, and establish a functional connection between the thymic myeloid niche and early αβ T cell development. Together, our study refines the phenotypic and developmental organization of mouse TMs and reveals a previously under-appreciated requirement for myeloid-cell support during progression through the β-selection checkpoint.
authors: Helen Wang; Vinothkumar Rajan; Anthony Wong; Slava Epelman; Juan Carlos Zúñiga‐Pflücker

title: Precision cognitive neurorehabilitation: dose, adaptivity, digital therapeutics and implementation
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cognitive deficits are determinants of long-term disability and socio-professional reintegration across neurological disorders, including stroke, traumatic brain injury, multiple sclerosis, and neurodegenerative diseases. Despite evidence supporting cognitive neurorehabilitation, its implementation remains heterogeneous, and therapeutic parameters are insufficiently defined. AREAS COVERED: The authors reviewed the published literature from PubMed and Google Scholar from 1 January 2015 to 30 June 2026, supplemented by seminal publications. Clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and observational and proof-of-concept studies were prioritized. This brief narrative review examines restorative and compensatory cognitive neurorehabilitation for deficits of attention, executive functions, language and disorders of consciousness in people after stroke and traumatic brain injury (TBI), older adults, and those with neurological and neurodegenerative conditions, including multiple sclerosis, Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. Emphasis is placed on dose, frequency, adaptivity, personalization, and digital and technology-assisted interventions. Methodological challenges include heterogeneity of protocols, limited use of active control conditions, insufficient long-term follow-up, and the gap between cognitive test improvements and meaningful effects on participation. EXPERT OPINION: Advancing cognitive neurorehabilitation requires precision-driven approaches integrating digital therapeutics with clinical frameworks. Large-scale pragmatic trials, meaningful endpoints, and implementation strategies across the continuum of care will be essential to transform cognitive neurorehabilitation into a component of neurological practice.
authors: Florian W. Sander; Etienne Sallard; Mauro Silva; Laurence Schneider; Karin Diserens; Christophe E. Graf; Andrea Serino; Arseny A. Sokolov

title: A New Current Fingerprinting Sensing Method for Adaptive Protection of PV-Integrated Distribution Networks
abstract: Grid-following photovoltaic (PV) inverters inject fault currents whose magnitude and phase are set by the control mode active during the disturbance, so directional overcurrent relay (DOCR) settings coordinated for one inverter response can miscoordinate after a mode change. This paper proposes a communication-free adaptive protection scheme built on local sensing. A voltage-adaptive current fingerprinting classifier uses local positive sequence measurements to detect current-limiting (CL), active current priority (ACP) and reactive current priority (RCP) operation, as well as momentary cessation (MC) and asymmetrical faults. The classifier activates the relay setting group prepared offline for the detected mode. With pickup currents fixed, the coordination sub-problem is shown to be a linear program (LP), so every setting group is computed at its exact global optimum. Where the grid code droop law makes ACP and RCP indistinguishable by angle, the classifier declares the ambiguity and activates a group that is feasible for both. Under a class-0.5 instrument transformer noise model, the group placed in service is coordination-valid in 99.8% of cases and the expected residual miscoordination is 3.0×10-5 s, 0.01% of the 0.30 s margin. On the CIGRE medium-voltage benchmark, the scheme satisfies the margin in all operating modes for three-phase, line-to-line (LL) and single-line-to-ground (SLG) faults. The same fault types are then verified at three fault locations on a practical Egyptian 11 kV feeder model, where the sensing layer is confirmed on an electromagnetic transient (EMT) model and the scheme removes the violations of single-setting coordination using an estimated 4 kB of relay memory.
