title: Gait Speed in Spinal Muscular Atrophy: A Key Vital Sign Linked to Strength and Fatigability
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction/Aims Gait Speed (GS), a valid and reliable indicator of function and health in multiple populations, has not been explored in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). The purpose of this study was to characterize GS and gait speed reserves (GSR), and explore associations with strength and fatigability in SMA and healthy controls (HC). Methods Data were collected from ambulatory individuals with SMA ( n = 14) and controls (HC) ( n = 10). Using custom‐engineered instrumented insoles, stride velocity (SV) was collected during the Six‐Minute Walk Test (6MWT) and 10‐m walk/run (10MWR). Three GS variables were identified; SV50th Centile 6MWT (SV50C 6MWT ), 10MWR SV, and SV95th Centile 6MWT (SV95C 6MWT ). Gait speed reserve (GSR) was calculated from 10MWR and SV50C 6MWT . Repeated measures analysis of variance assessed differences in GS and GSR across groups. Spearman's Rho was used to assess associations between speed variables and clinical assessments. Results All speed variables were different within HC ( p < 0.001) and SMA ( p = 0.002). There was a significant Group × Speed interaction ( p < 0.001) with greater differences in HC. GSR was lower in SMA ( p < 0.001, d = 2.42). In SMA, thigh strength was associated with all three GS variables and inversely associated with fatigability ( p < 0.05). In HC, associations between GS and strength or fatigability were not observed. GSR was not associated with strength, fatigability, or GS in either group. Discussion GS is diminished in SMA and correlated with strength and fatigability. While reduced in SMA, GSR was not associated with GS, strength, or function. GS is a key vital sign of health and may be a useful biomarker in SMA.
authors: Carly Magun; Ton T. H. Duong; Cara H. Kanner; Rafael S. Rodriguez-Torres; Elizabeth R. Harding; Sally Dunaway Young; Rabia Farooquee; Constance de Monts; Amy Pasternak; Maria A. Fragala-Pinkham; Damiano Zanotto; Jacqueline Montes

title: Metal Hypersensitivity Reactions Following Spinal Implants
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metal hypersensitivity reactions are infrequently reported but clinically significant after spinal implant surgery. Clinical presentation can mimic infection or mechanical failure, making diagnosis difficult. Evidence to guide diagnosis and management is largely limited to short case series and case reports. The purpose of this study was to systematically review the clinical presentation, diagnostic methods, and outcomes of metal hypersensitivity associated with spinal implants. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus from inception through June 22, 2026, in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Title and abstract screening, full-text review, and data extraction were performed independently by 2 reviewers with conflicts resolved by a third reviewer. Eligible studies included adult patients with suspected or confirmed metal hypersensitivity following spinal implant surgery that reported patient-level clinical outcomes. RESULTS: Fifteen studies with a total of 19 patients met inclusion criteria (53% female, 42% male, and 5% not reported). The median patient age was 47 years (range, 19-69). Twelve procedures (63%) were fusion-based, while 7 (37%) were motion preserving, including disk arthroplasty and artificial facet replacement systems. Common clinical presentations included persistent pain, with 8 patients (42%) exhibiting dermatologic manifestations. Metal hypersensitivity was immunologically confirmed by positive patch testing and/or lymphocyte transformation testing in 11 patients (58%), while 8 (42%) were diagnosed clinically. Onset of symptoms ranged from immediately postoperatively to 15 years after implantation. Eighteen patients underwent removal or revision with clinical improvement in 14 of 16 with a reported outcome (88%). CONCLUSION: Metal hypersensitivity reactions following spinal implants are infrequently reported but may present either immediately or in a delayed manner with symptoms that mimic more common postoperative complications, such as infection or pseudarthrosis, or may present with dermatologic manifestations. In cases where other etiologies are ruled out, hardware removal was frequently, though not invariably, associated with clinical improvement, which was reported narratively rather than by validated outcome measures. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic Level V. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.
authors: Joseph Abbo; Jacob Thomas; Christian Stipho; Erik Nakken; Rakesh Patel; Joshua David Piche; IIyas Aleem

title: The trigger-timing framework for long COVID: using symptom triggers and temporal patterns to guide mechanistic stratification and treatment planning
abstract: Long COVID is characterized by substantial clinical heterogeneity, with similar symptoms often arising from different underlying physiological mechanisms. Fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, palpitations, dyspnea, gastrointestinal symptoms, sleep disruption, and exertional intolerance may each reflect autonomic dysfunction, mitochondrial or bioenergetic impairment, endothelial or microvascular dysfunction, mast cell or histamine-mediated signaling, gut dysbiosis, neuroendocrine dysregulation, or interactions among these domains. Symptom-based classification alone may therefore be insufficient for identifying dominant mechanisms or guiding treatment selection. This manuscript proposes the trigger-timing framework as a clinically accessible, hypothesis-generating method for translating patient-reported symptom behavior into mechanism-informed interpretation. The framework is based on the premise that common daily stressors, including upright posture, temperature exposure, physical or cognitive exertion, meals, emotional stress, sleep disruption, alcohol exposure, and intercurrent illness, function as real-world physiologic probes. The timing of symptom worsening after these stressors provides additional information because immediate, short-delay, same-day, delayed, cumulative, and circadian responses may reflect different response kinetics. The framework integrates four core clinical dimensions: the trigger that provokes symptom worsening, the timing of symptom onset, the symptom pattern that emerges, and the relief or recovery pattern that follows. Immediate worsening with standing, heat exposure, meals, or upright exertion, especially when relieved by lying down, supports an autonomic or circulatory pattern. Delayed worsening after physical or cognitive exertion supports impaired recovery physiology and post-exertional malaise. Meal-related symptoms may suggest autonomic, metabolic, gastrointestinal, or mast cell-related physiology depending on timing and accompanying symptoms. Circadian or persistent patterns may suggest neuroendocrine, sleep-related, autonomic, or inflammatory rhythm instability. This framework is intended as a companion operational framework to a mechanism-anchored network model of Long COVID. It may help guide targeted diagnostic evaluation, treatment prioritization, sequencing decisions, longitudinal tracking, and research cohort enrichment. The model remains conceptual and requires prospective validation to determine whether trigger-timing patterns correlate with objective physiological measures, predict differential treatment response, and improve outcomes compared with symptom-based stratification alone.
authors: Robert Groysman

title: Translational maturity of artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography varies across cardiovascular diseases
abstract: Electrocardiography is a widely available and low-cost cardiovascular test, and artificial intelligence-enabled electrocardiography (AI-ECG) can identify latent electrical phenotypes beyond conventional interpretation. However, high retrospective discrimination does not necessarily translate into clinically reliable or actionable benefit. This critical narrative review evaluates the translational maturity of AI-ECG across arrhythmias, acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, valvular heart disease, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Web of Science were searched from January 1, 2022, through July 10, 2026, with earlier landmark studies added by backward citation tracking. Seventy-seven publications informed the review. Evidence was appraised using five clinically oriented criteria: intended use, reference-standard reliability, external validation and transportability, clinical actionability, and effects on workflow or patient outcomes. AI-ECG has progressed furthest in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction triage and reduced-left-ventricular-ejection-fraction screening, where prospective or randomized studies have demonstrated workflow or diagnostic-yield benefits, whereas acute myocardial infarction rule-out has reached prospective multicenter diagnostic validation. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy screening has also advanced through international validation and prospective implementation. By contrast, occlusion myocardial infarction detection, prediction of occult or future atrial fibrillation, valvular heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, long-term heart-failure prediction, and cardiac amyloidosis remain primarily validation-stage or risk-enrichment applications. Across domains, broader adoption is constrained by label quality, calibration, transportability, operating-threshold selection, and limited patient-outcome evidence. AI-ECG is therefore best positioned as clinician-supervised decision support linked to explicit downstream testing and care pathways.
authors: Huanhuan Chen; Jingjuan Huang; Xumin Hou

title: Effects of eyelash extensions on the ocular surface: a systematic review of clinical outcomes and adverse events
abstract: Topic To synthesise evidence on ocular surface outcomes, symptoms and adverse events associated with semi-permanent eyelash extensions. Clinical relevance Eyelash extensions are applied beside the ocular surface; their clinical effects and associated complications warrant assessment. Methods PubMed, Ovid, CINAHL and Scopus were searched to 3 September 2026 without date or language restrictions for primary human studies reporting extension-specific ocular or periocular outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and appraised studies using adapted Newcastle-Ottawa and Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Findings were synthesised narratively owing to heterogeneity. The review followed PRISMA 2020 and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420261383757). Results Nineteen studies were included: two prospective studies, five cross-sectional studies, four case series and eight case reports. In one prospective study, corneal staining peaked at one hour and tear-film stability was lowest at one week after application. A matched comparator study found between-group differences in tear break-up time and clinical signs. One removal study showed improvement in symptomatic users. Four self-report studies included 845 users; symptom prevalence ranged from 26.8% to 97.5%, reflecting different samples and methods. Reported adverse events included keratoconjunctivitis, contact dermatitis, bacterial keratitis and eyelid leukoderma. Conclusion Eyelash extensions are associated with ocular surface disturbance and diverse adverse events, involving exposures beyond the adhesive. Small uncontrolled studies, self-reported surveys and case-level evidence limit certainty and prevent population-risk estimation. The findings support clinical enquiry about extension use in patients with unexplained ocular surface or perioperative symptoms.
authors: Minnan Al-Khafaji; Hussain Al-Hilali; Stephen Ong

title: Conceptualizing cognition and behaviour across amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia
abstract: Cognitive and behavioral dysfunction in frontotemporal dementia (FTD) evolves along a clinical continuum from a clinically silent stage of disease, through a prodromal period, often referred to as mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and/or mild behavioral impairment (MBI), and into a clinically manifest stage recognized by the syndromes of behavioral variant FTD and primary progressive aphasia (PPA). Similar cognitive and behavioral manifestations of varying severity are also encountered in individuals with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Notwithstanding this phenotypic overlap as well as a degree of shared genetic risk and underlying pathology, the approach to phenotypic characterization and description meaningfully differs between the ALS and FTD communities. The problem is particularly evident within the ALS community when describing impairment in the prodromal vs. clinically manifest disease stages. Pertinent considerations include the nature of cognitive and behavioral assessments, the nosology used to describe symptoms identified including those encompassed by the terms 'behavioral' and 'neuropsychiatric', the operationalized criteria that define prodromal syndromes and clinically manifest disease, and the extent to which these criteria rely on longitudinal (vs. cross-sectional) data. A multi-stakeholder workshop, held in London, Ontario (May 12-14, 2025), brought together neurologists, psychiatrists, neuropsychologists, neuropathologists, neuroscientists, and neurogeneticists studying ALS and FTD, to promote inter-disciplinary dialogue and to define a research agenda that might be jointly tackled to address these critical issues. A new nosology for classifying frontotemporal-related behavioral and neuropsychiatric dysfunction, which could be used to support empirical evidence collection, is proposed alongside a list of cognitive, language, behavioral and neuropsychiatric symptoms to be considered in the evaluation of individuals with ALS. Research priorities for each of the ALS and FTD communities, as well as initiatives that should be undertaken jointly, are highlighted. The long-term goal is to harmonize approaches to phenotypic characterization, the nosology used to describe symptoms, and the criteria used to define landmark stages along the clinical continua of the motor neuron and frontotemporal axes irrespective of clinical stage.
authors: Michael G Benatar; Edward D. Huey; Chiadi U. Onyike; Caroline A. McHutchison; Maria Carmela Tartaglia; Megan S. Barker; Sharon Abrahams; Joke De Vocht; Emma Rhodes; Yolande A.L. title: The Management of Type 1 Diabetes in Adults. The Updated 2026 Consensus Report by the American Diabetes Association (ADA) and the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD)
abstract: This 2026 consensus report from the European Association for the Study of Diabetes (EASD) and the American Diabetes Association (ADA) builds on the 2021 consensus report to provide guidance for managing type 1 diabetes in adults. Reflecting the rapid advances in the field, this update places particular emphasis on the integration of new technologies, while all sections have been revised to incorporate novel therapies, including interventions to delay the onset of stage 3 type 1 diabetes. It also broadens its scope to screening for long-term diabetes complications, and the management of obesity and cardiovascular risk factors. Psychosocial care and diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) remain key elements. The report was developed using the Accurate Consensus Reporting Document (ACCORD) framework. The guidance aligns with current ADA Standards of Care and relevant EASD and ADA documents and aims to support clinicians globally in delivering high-quality, personalised care for adults with type 1 diabetes, with recommendations that can be adapted across diverse healthcare systems and resource settings.

title: The Role of TP53 Genetic Mutation in Breast Cancer Pathogenesis
abstract: Objective: To review the role of TP53 genetic mutations in breast cancer Study Design: Case-control studyPlace and Duration of Study: This study was conducted at the Marjan Teaching Hospital in Babylon, from 1st December 2023 to 30th June 2025. Methods: This case-control was conducted at Marjan Teaching Hospital in Babylon and 200 subject were enrolled, 100 patients with breast cancer and 100 healthy undivided were recruited. Subjects were selected at after theextraction of DNA the genotype of rs17878362 C/T and rs1042522 G/C was done using TaqMan-based Real-time PCR technique. Results: The significant was noted in cancer antigen 15-3 level between the two group where it was 45.22±4.32U/ml in cases and 22.24±2.10U/ml in control (p=0.001).as for the polymorphism rs17878362. There was a statically significant difference in the frequency of CC 29% and CT 58% genotypes as well as in T alleles between cases and control (p=0.001), also similar result were obtained for the polymorphism rs1042522 .the frequencies of GG 38%; GC 62% genotypes and C alleles were statistically significantly more in the cancer group (P=0.001). The highest risk was found for TT genotype of rs17878362 which had the OR equal to 3.11. Discrepancies from Hardy- Weinberg Equilibrium were detected in the cases of breast cancer group in both genetic polymorphism (p=0.001). Conclusion: The strong correlation between TP53 gene polymorphism rs17878362 and rs1042522 and high cancer incidence. These variants seem to affect the function of TP53 protein in terms of programmed cell death, causing genomic instability which is associated with developing of tumors. Thus, they might serve as important markers for cancer predicant and treatment.

title: Faradaically Resilient Triphase Wedge‐Shaped Nanowire Arrays for Robust Bioanalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Gas‐containing triphase interfaces are attractive for oxygen‐mediated electrochemical systems, yet faradaic stress‐induced electrowetting remains unresolved in triphase biointerfaces. This work presents faradaically resilient wedge‐shaped copper nanowire arrays (W‐CuNWAs) that stabilize oxygen‐enriched triphase interfaces during sustained and repeated electrochemical operations. In contrast with conventional passive liquid‐repellent nanostructures, W‐CuNWAs employ co‐programmed structural–wettability anisotropy to reconcile wettable charge‐transfer regions with gas‐retaining regions within a single nanoarchitecture. Compared to cylindrical CuNWAs, W‐CuNWAs introduce shape‐encoded wetting barriers that increase capillary breakthrough pressure by 2.85‐fold and pin the contact line at the upper edge. Across 3 h of continuous bias, 500 potential cycles, repeated impedance perturbations, and cathodic electrodeposition of a high‐surface‐energy co‐catalyst, W‐CuNWAs retain stable wettability and electrochemical responses with only 0.88 kΩ mass‐transport‐resistance drift, whereas cylindrical counterparts undergo electrolyte infiltration and structural failure. The retained atmosphere‐connected gas phase enables Pt/W‐CuNWAs to achieve 1.65‐fold higher oxygen‐reduction current, 8.96‐fold lower oxygen mass‐transfer resistance, and 2.96‐fold faster current stabilization than cylindrical counterparts. Integration with an FeOOH/BiVO 4 photoanode enables near‐drift‐free, unbiased photoelectrochemical operation over 8.42 h of repeated cathodic cycling, and reliable detection of Alzheimer's neurofilament light chain in clinical plasma. This work establishes shape‐encoded faradaic electrowetting resistance as a design principle for operationally stable, oxygen‐mediated triphase nanoarchitectures in bioanalysis.
authors: Hayeon Kim; Hyeok Lim; Sung Hyun Park; Jaejin Kim; Joonseok Lee; Kayoung Kim

title: The effect of low-temperature-induced immune activation in elderly idiopathic facial palsy: the association between Th1/Th2 imbalance and facial nerve inflammation
abstract: The pathogenesis of idiopathic facial palsy in the elderly has not been fully elucidated. Recent studies have shown that exposure to low temperatures may participate in the pathological process through immune-mediated pathways. This article reviews that cold stimulation can disrupt the Th1/Th2 immune balance, manifested as reduced secretion of Th1-type cytokines and upregulation of Th2-type cytokines, thereby inducing peripheral inflammatory responses around the facial nerve, leading to nerve edema, demyelination, and conduction dysfunction. Due to the immune aging characteristics of the elderly population, including the reduction of the initial T cell pool, the imbalance of pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory factor ratios, and the decline in regulatory T cell function, they are more sensitive to the immune dysregulation induced by low temperatures and have a significantly increased risk of facial palsy. Clinical and animal experimental evidence supports this mechanism, suggesting that the serum IL-4/IFN-γ ratio may serve as a prognostic marker. Future multi-center studies are needed to verify the effectiveness of targeted immune regulation intervention through the Th2 pathway and explore the application value of low-temperature warning and individualized warming strategies in the prevention of facial palsy in the elderly.
authors: Xing Tang; Ziqin Ji; Xueling Xiao; Tongtong Zhu; Shoujen Lan; Yeayin Yen; Xin Shao; Shune Tan; Chao Wang; Jicheng Zhang

title: Hydrogel Microneedles for Perioperative Applications: Drug Delivery, Biosensing, and Theranostic Translation
abstract: Abstract: Hydrogel microneedles provide access across the skin barrier for drug delivery and interstitial-fluid sampling. Their perioperative use depends on whether that access remains reliable during skin preparation, surgical positioning, and changes in tissue perfusion. This narrative review examines how material design affects delivered dose, measurement accuracy, and clinical feasibility. Human sampling studies establish feasibility for selected measurements; most therapeutic and integrated sensing applications remain at the preclinical stage or have been investigated in other clinical settings. The review distinguishes these findings from evidence in surgical patients. Particular attention is given to insertion and adhesion on disinfected or compromised skin, the relationship between interstitial and plasma measurements, and drug exposure after delivery is interrupted. Short-duration superficial procedures and observational drug or wound-adjacent monitoring offer focused questions for initial studies with standard care maintained. Progress toward treatment requires validation of the complete product, including sterilization, batch consistency, shelf life, and safeguards against uncontrolled release. Clinical studies should report failed applications and adverse events alongside patient outcomes. Autonomous anesthetic administration remains a development goal whose safety cannot be inferred from separate demonstrations of sensing and drug release. Keywords: hydrogel microneedles, perioperative applications, drug delivery, interstitial fluid, therapeutic drug monitoring, theranostics
authors: Yue Qi; Cong Wang; Jinyue Chen; Dalong Wu

title: Effect of neurodegenerative comorbidities on the risk of revision of knee joint replacements
abstract: Background: As populations age, both joint arthroplasty procedures and neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's disease (PD) are increasingly common. While general risk factors for knee prosthesis failure are well known, the specific impact of PD on implant survival is less clear. Motor symptoms of PD—rigidity, bradykinesia, postural instability—could impair joint function and raise complication risks. Understanding this relationship is crucial for optimizing care in these patients. Aim: This study investigated whether patients with preoperative PD have a greater risk of revision after total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Secondary aims included determining causes of failure, comparing outcomes with total hip arthroplasty (THA), and assessing biomechanical factors through computer modeling. Materials and Methods: A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted using the Emilia-Romagna Joint Replacement Registry (RIPO) and administrative databases. Patients with PD who underwent TKA from 2003–2018 were compared to matched controls without neurodegenerative diseases. The primary endpoint was revision for any reason. Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and multivariate Cox regression were applied. THA outcomes were analyzed in parallel, and biomechanical modeling was performed to simulate joint forces in PD. Results: Of 52,573 TKAs, 551 were in PD patients. The revision rate was significantly higher in the PD group (8.4% vs. 3.5%), with a 2.7-fold increased risk (HR 2.7; 95% CI 2.1–3.7). Septic loosening and implant dislocation were more common in PD patients, while aseptic loosening rates were similar. For THA, long-term revision rates did not differ, but PD patients had more early complications, notably periprosthetic fractures. Biomechanical modeling showed no significant differences in joint loading. Conclusions: Parkinson’s disease independently increases the risk of TKA failure, primarily due to systemic frailty, infection, trauma and not mechanical overload. Tailored perioperative and multidisciplinary approaches are needed to improve outcomes in this population.
authors: Alessandro Panciera
venue: AMS Dottorato Institutional Doctoral Theses Repository (University of Bologna)

title: Applying artificial intelligence to the hypertension care cascade: Opportunities and challenges
abstract: In the United States, hypertension control curves have plateaued below what is achievable and acceptable. The persistence of suboptimal disease control—despite a robust clinical armamentarium—suggests failure points between guideline-directed and real-world care. This manuscript examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to address the public health challenges undermining hypertension control. Using the hypertension care cascade (which comprises diagnosis, awareness, treatment, and control) as a guiding framework, we synthesize current evidence and identify promising applications of AI-enabled tools and technologies at each stage of the cascade. AI, indeed, offers a plausible pathway for addressing some of the most pernicious forces undermining sustained, scalable hypertension control; however, it is not without risks and limitations. Its deployment must, therefore, be paired with a comprehensive governance structure that safeguards patients and prioritizes safety, equity, and accountability. With these safeguards in place, AI holds promise for bridging hypertension's operational gaps and improving population health.
authors: Matthew E. Berman; Mateen H. Abbasi; Roman Pati; Thomas Wyskowski; Divij Satapathy; Jay Tamirisa; Faraan O. Rahim; Jared W. Magnani
venue: American Heart Journal Plus Cardiology Research and Practice

title: Gene Therapy Approaches for Rare Genetic Diseases: Current Advances, Challenges and Future Perspectives
abstract: Rare genetic diseases are a highly heterogeneous group of disorders affecting a small number of patients but collectively pose a significant global health burden. Current treatments offer clinical benefits but often fail to correct molecular defects, reach tissues, avoid immunity, or eliminate repeated dosing. These limitations are especially pronounced in cases of molecularly heterogeneous rare diseases affecting small patient populations with anatomically inaccessible tissues. Gene therapy helps to address such limitations by targeting the causal gene or transcript. In this chapter, we examine the molecular basis of rare genetic diseases, major delivery platforms, genome editing technologies, and representative clinical applications. The adeno-associated virus and lentiviral vector systems are important viral vectors, as they have higher transduction efficiency, while lipid nanoparticles, polymer-based carriers, and physical methods provide scalable and possibly engraftable strategies. Gene addition, disruption, and precise sequence correction can be accomplished using CRISPR–Cas nucleases, base editors, and prime editors, but the challenges of delivery, immunogenicity, off-target activity, and manufacturing are significant. Diseases and disorders such as spinal muscular atrophy, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, and hemophilia B are examples of how disease mechanism, target tissue, durability, and safety impact therapeutic designs and clinical translation strategies. The future of gene therapy for rare diseases depends on the widespread adoption of patient-specific designs, expedited approval pathways with regulatory agencies, and standardized manufacturing processes. Expanding newborn screening for early diagnosis, capid and promoter engineering with high tissue specificity, improving immunosuppression protocols, and establishing long-term follow-up registries are of critical importance.
authors: Mert Polat; Selin Akad Dinçer; Yunus Kasım Terzi

title: Evolution of evidence-based medicine: toward digital evidence ecosystems and artificial intelligence
abstract: Evidence-based medicine (EBM) has transformed clinical decision-making by integrating the best available research evidence with clinical expertise and patients’ values and preferences. Over the past three decades, EBM has evolved from the critical appraisal of individual studies into a broader framework encompassing evidence synthesis, clinical practice guidelines, assessment of evidence certainty, research transparency, and shared decision-making. Despite these advances, contemporary EBM faces important challenges, including the rapidly increasing volume of research, delays in evidence synthesis and implementation, limited applicability of randomized controlled trials to heterogeneous real-world populations, and difficulties in individualizing population-level evidence. Emerging approaches—including real-world evidence, living evidence, learning health systems, precision medicine, and artificial intelligence (AI)—offer opportunities to address these limitations. Together, these approaches may enable a transition from static to continuously updated evidence, from population-average to more personalized evidence, and from a linear evidence pipeline to a learning evidence ecosystem in which clinical practice both uses and generates evidence. AI may further accelerate evidence retrieval, synthesis, updating, and individualized decision support, while introducing challenges related to reliability, bias, transparency, reproducibility, and accountability. Next-generation EBM should therefore be conceptualized not as a replacement for traditional EBM but as its evolution into a digitally connected, continuously learning evidence ecosystem. In the AI era, the foundational principles of EBM—source verification, critical appraisal, uncertainty assessment, integration of patient preferences, and accountable human judgment—will become increasingly important.
authors: Soo Young Kim

title: Measurement-Error-Aware Causal Distributed-Lag Quantile Modeling of Indoor Air Pollution and Short-Term Lung-Function Deterioration
abstract: Low-cost indoor air-quality sensors could support personalized asthma prevention, but their nonlinear measurement error, delayed exposure effects, time-varying confounding, and heterogeneous lower-tail responses limit risk estimation. We present CAUSALQUANT-ASTHMA, a measurement-error-aware causal quantile distributed-lag framework for short-horizon peak expiratory flow analysis. Sparse reference measurements train a nonlinear calibration model; stabilized sequential generalized-propensity weights address measured exposure assignment; and a susceptibility-modulated, smooth, noncrossing quantile model estimates lag-specific and sustained-exposure contrasts. Because no authorized cohort simultaneously provided dense indoor sensing, reference co-location, and outcome-compatible longitudinal data, evaluation used five semi-synthetic panels with known counterfactual truth, 150 patients and 12,600 patient-days per realization. Across eight methods, CAUSALQUANT achieved a dose-response integrated absolute error of 0.304 plus or minus 0.094, improving 24.2 percent over the strongest measurement-error and propensity-weighted baseline. It also obtained the lowest overall pinball loss, 1.065, while maintaining zero quantile crossings and 78.1 percent coverage for the nominal 80 percent interval. Sensor calibration reduced held-out exposure RMSE by 33.7 percent. Stress tests quantified degradation under sensor noise, missing personal measurements, and hidden confounding. These findings establish methodological feasibility and reproducibility, not clinical effectiveness; prospective, governance-approved external validation is required before patient-level interpretation or deployment.
authors: Shayma Alkobaisi; Anas Ali

abstract: lzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline and memory impairment, posing a significant global healthcare burden. Early diagnosis remains challenging due to reliance on late-stage clinical symptoms, by which time irreversible neuronal damage has already occurred.
authors: Anup Kumar Chakraborty
venue: International Journal of Pharmaceutical and Biological Archive

title: Changes in modifiable dementia risk factors and subjective cognitive decline in mid and later life
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Exposure to modifiable dementia risk factors (MDRFs) contributes substantially to dementia risk across the life course. Less is known about persistence and changes in these factors during mid- and later life and how they relate to early neurophysiological changes associated with dementia. This study examined rates and changes in MDRFs over two years and their associations with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) among older adults. DESIGN: Cohort study. SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Participants were 2370 adults aged 55-92 years (M = 68.54, SD = 7.15; 56.5% female) who completed the 2018 and 2020 waves of a longitudinal survey of ageing in New Zealand. MEASUREMENTS: Self-reported hypertension, diabetes, hearing impairment, vision impairment, current smoking, hazardous alcohol use, physical inactivity, depression, and loneliness were classified into four categories across waves: stable absence, reduction, onset, and stable presence. SCD was assessed in 2020. Logistic regression models were used to examine associations between MDRF categories and SCD. RESULTS: Survey-weighted responses indicated 8.6% of older adults experienced SCD. Diabetes, hearing impairment, current vision impairment, stable presence of physical inactivity, depression, and current loneliness were associated with increased odds of SCD. CONCLUSIONS: Both the onset and reduction of psychosocial and sensory MDRFs in mid- and later life have measurable implications for subjective cognitive outcomes in a general population sample. Prevention and reduction of diabetes, sensory loss, physical inactivity, depression, and social isolation represent meaningful targets for supporting cognitive well-being among older adults.
authors: Joanne Allen; Michelle Kelly; Gill Livingston; Christine V Stephens; Fiona Alpass

title: From shōnen to seinen to Studio Ghibli: attraction to anime and manga, and their relation to mental health and social outcomes
abstract: Abstract Aim Interest in anime and manga can be very diverse (from action-packed stories to romantic tales to works by the famous Studio Ghibli). Our aim was to examine the association of interest in manga and anime (and specifically certain genres) with mental health, social disconnectedness, and subjective well-being outcomes. Subject and methods We used data from a sample of the general adult population in Germany ( N = 2591, mean age 47 years, 50.6% female). Outcomes were quantified using psychometrically sound tools (e.g., Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9] or Satisfaction with Life Scale [SWLS]). General interest in manga and anime and also interest in certain genres (among those who were interested) served as key independent variables. Results A general interest in manga and anime was consistently associated with poor mental health and social disconnectedness (compared with the absence of such interest), whereas it was generally not associated with subjective well-being outcomes. Among those who were interested, while most interest in specific manga genres was only partly or not significantly associated with the outcomes, interest in manga from Studio Ghibli was associated with better mental health and less social withdrawal. Moreover, an interest in anime from Studio Ghibli was associated with several favorable outcomes (better mental health, social connectedness, and higher ikigai levels). Conclusion While a general interest in anime and manga was consistently associated with poorer mental health and social disconnectedness, certain genres were associated with favorable outcomes among those who were interested in them. Further differentiated research is needed to better understand the psychosocial outcomes of anime and manga passion.
authors: André Hajek; Hans‐Helmut König

title: Application and prospects of veterinary diagnostic techniques in laboratory monkeys
abstract: -threaten animal welfare and colony security, while also elevating zoonotic transmission risks and compromising the reliability of research data. The diversity, complexity, and clinically insidious nature of diseases in laboratory monkeys impose stringent demands on veterinary diagnostic capabilities. This review summarizes the current status and recent advances in mainstream veterinary diagnostic techniques applied to laboratory monkey disease surveillance. We analyze the specific applications, strengths, and limitations of molecular, immunological, imaging, and conventional microbiological methods for detecting major viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens of laboratory monkeys, covering quantitative PCR (qPCR), CRISPR-based assays, ELISA, IFA/IHC, and other established platforms. By comparing these techniques across sensitivity, specificity, cost-effectiveness, and operational feasibility, we delineate their suitability for distinct use cases: high-precision laboratory testing, large-scale colony screening, and point-of-care clinical diagnosis. Current veterinary diagnostic assays for laboratory monkeys achieve robust analytical performance. In several studies, qPCR delivers 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity for B virus detection, digital PCR (dPCR) attains a limit of detection as low as 45 copies/ml for monkeypox virus; and CRISPR/Cas-based assays have demonstrated 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity in clinical validation cohorts. Building on these advances, we further identify practical bottlenecks in diagnostic deployment and propose targeted countermeasures. Finally, we explore emerging trends and application prospects for point-of-care testing, multiplex pathogen detection, and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis, which collectively support the development of accurate, efficient, and intelligent disease diagnostics for laboratory monkeys. This work aims to provide a theoretical and practical reference for clinical practice and scientific research focused on laboratory monkey disease prevention and control.
authors: Zhengjia Zhang; Diangang Han; Qiujiang Wei; Xuewei Fu; Yongqing Yan; Dandan Li; JIGE XIN

title: Plasma immune signatures associate with neurodegeneration in frontotemporal lobar degeneration
abstract: Abstract Frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) encompasses clinically and biologically heterogeneous syndromes that are unlikely to be captured by a single blood biomarker. Although plasma neurofilament light (NfL) chain reflects neuroaxonal injury, multiplex profiling may identify complementary inflammatory, vascular and proteostatic processes relevant to clinical phenotype and progression. We characterised plasma CNS-related and inflammatory proteomic signatures across FTLD-related clinical syndromes and tested their associations with neuroaxonal injury, clinical severity, regional brain atrophy and survival. Plasma samples from 177 participants with behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), primary progressive aphasia (PPA), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) or corticobasal syndrome (CBS) and 67 healthy controls were analysed using the high-sensitivity nucleic acid-linked immuno-sandwich assay (NULISA) platform. We quantified 130 CNS-related and 250 inflammation-related proteins. Differential expression and multivariate classification analyses were complemented by hierarchical clustering, penalised regression and survival analyses. Canonical correlation analysis tested multivariate associations between disease-associated proteins and regional MRI brain volumes. Sixty-one CNS-related and 61 inflammation-related proteins differed between participants with FTLD-related syndromes and controls after false-discovery-rate correction. NfL was the strongest individual discriminator between all patients and controls, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.91. In exploratory full-cohort models, the multivariate CNS signature achieved an area under the curve of 0.93, compared with 0.82 for the multivariate inflammation signature. However, inflammatory proteins provided stronger discrimination for selected syndrome comparisons, including PPA versus PSP. Among inflammation-related proteins, SPP1 and CD276 showed the strongest positive associations with NfL. Higher CD276 and SPP1 were associated with increased mortality, whereas higher amyloid-β42 was associated with lower mortality. A multivariate protein signature weighted towards tumour necrosis factor and immune signalling was associated with lower regional brain volumes across predominantly frontotemporal and limbic regions (canonical correlation 0.43; permutation p=0.018). Plasma multiplex proteomics identified complementary dimensions of neuroaxonal injury and immune dysregulation across frontotemporal lobar degeneration-related syndromes. CNS-related proteins, particularly NfL, predominantly captured case-control neurodegeneration, whereas inflammatory signatures provided additional information about syndrome heterogeneity, structural brain changes and survival. SPP1, CD276 and broader immune-related signatures are candidates for independent biomarker validation and mechanistic investigation.
authors: Meira van Schaik; Kei Onn Lai; Noah Lorenz Shapiro; Alexander Jäck; Julia Goddard; Harry Crook; Roosmarijn Frohn; Peter Simon Jones; Sean YW Tan; Owen Swann; Rachel Mulvaney; Amanda Heslegrave; Henrik Zetterberg; Matthias Brendel; Kamen A. Tsvetanov; James Benedict Rowe; Maura Malpetti

title: Real-Time SpO2 Estimation from Chest Reflectance Photoplethysmography: Algorithm Development and Clinical Validation Against Arterial SaO2
abstract: Peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) estimation using photoplethysmography (PPG) is typically based on the pulsatile components of red and infrared (IR) PPG signals acquired from peripheral sites, such as the finger or earlobe. Although these sites provide strong PPG signals, they are less suitable for integrated monitoring with electrocardiography (ECG), including arrhythmia detection. Simultaneous acquisition of PPG and ECG from a chest-worn device may therefore enable continuous and integrated physiological monitoring. However, chest PPG is characterized by lower perfusion and greater susceptibility to respiratory and motion artifacts, making reliable extraction of pulsatile red and IR components challenging. In this study, we developed and clinically evaluated a real-time SpO2 estimation algorithm based on chest reflectance PPG. Green PPG, which provides a relatively distinct pulsatile waveform under low-perfusion conditions, was used for beat detection. A heart-rate-adaptive analysis window, normalized cross-correlation-based signal quality assessment, and least-squares estimation of the AC amplitude ratio were combined to calculate the red-to-IR ratio of ratios, from which SpO2 was estimated using a calibration equation. Algorithm performance was evaluated against reference arterial oxygen saturation (SaO2) measured using a blood gas analyzer. The proposed method achieved an accuracy root mean square of 2.91% relative to the reference SaO2. These results support the technical feasibility of chest reflectance PPG-based SpO2 estimation and its accuracy under controlled desaturation conditions.
authors: WooYong Lee; 신재연; MiHye Song; Mi-Kyung Song; Kyung Mi Kim; Gyu‐Jeong Noh; Sung Pil Cho

title: ECG parameters in episodes of neonatal hyper- and hypoglycemia: an observational study
abstract: Introduction: Abnormal glucose concentrations are common in the neonatal period and may entail long-term consequences. They are currently detected invasively through spot-measurements, contribute to blood loss and are painful depending on the sampling route. We hypothesized that hypo- and hyperglycemia may be associated with changes in neonatal electrocardiogram (ECG), such as PR interval, QRS duration, and ST segment durations. Methods: We analyzed ECG parameters and categorized blood glucose measurements [hypo-, normo-, hyperglycemia (locally defined as >180 mg/dL)] using generalized linear mixed-effects models. Potential ECG predictors of blood glucose abnormalities were first identified in univariable models and then entered into a multivariable model to assess associations, adjusting for postmenstrual age and time between two consecutive measurements. The direction and magnitude of observed associations were assessed in leave-one-subject-out sensitivity analyses. Results: 959 paired measurements (32 hypoglycemia, 714 normoglycemia, 213 hyperglycemia) from 15 neonates were analyzed. In the multivariable model, PR interval was significantly associated with hypo- and hyperglycemia. QRS duration was associated with hyperglycemia, whereas ST segment duration was related to hypoglycemia. All associations remained significant after adjustment for postmenstrual age and time between two consecutive measurements. Within the constraints of the limited sample size, the leave-one-subject-out sensitivity analysis suggested that the direction and magnitude of effect sizes were largely consistent across iterations. However, statistical significance was sensitive to single-subject exclusions, particularly for the PR interval in hypoglycemia. Intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.65 for hyperglycemia and 0.41 for hypoglycemia, indicating relevant intra-individual clustering. Discussion: The findings of this hypothesis-generating study in 15 individual infants suggest that cardiac electrophysiology may provide information about blood glucose abnormalities in the neonatal period. Especially findings on hypoglycemia remain exploratory due to the limited sample size. ECG parameters may serve as candidate features for non-invasive prediction of hypo- and hyperglycemia in critically ill neonates.
authors: Lena Olivier; J Strunk; Camelia Lauterbach Oprea; André Stollenwerk; Sina Wedding; Thorsten Orlikowsky; Mark Schoberer

title: Visually similar prints expose a benchmark validity gap in computational art history
authors: Jiongming Fang

title: 55th Child Neurology Society Annual Meeting
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Pediatric concussion care is rapidly evolving, leading to significant shifts in clinical recommendations.We updated clinical recommendations, tools, and algorithms within the Living Guideline for Pediatric Concussion using peer-reviewed evidence, while integrating patient engagement and expanding scope to priority populations and emerging areas.METHODS: 4041 papers published through 2025 were critically assessed, aligned with current clinical recommendations, and coded with EppiReviewer.An interactive living evidence gap map generated using EPPI-vis was shared with 45 expert panel members and consensus voting informed updates.This was repeated every six months and includes ongoing input from individuals with lived experience.RESULTS: Recommendation updates include aerobic exercise to treat concussion, guidance on screen time, return to school, mental health, and early interventions to facilitate recovery and reduce the risk of persisting symptoms after concussion.The strength of evidence varies, with more high quality (level 1-2) studies supporting initial medical management (131) and prolonged symptoms (57), while telemedicine (3) and interpersonal violence (0) remain limited, reflecting emerging areas of research.The Living Guideline Evidence Map includes 1511 publicly accessible records published from 2013 -2025.Guideline recommendations, tools, evidence maps, and details of the consensus process are freely shared on pedsconcussion.com,with over 989,000 total engagements.CONCLUSIONS: Evaluation and synthesis of evidence coupled with commitment and collaboration from leaders in the field is essential for developing and sustaining evidencebased clinical guidelines.The creation and regular updating of the Living Guideline for Pediatric Concussion provide a mechanism for continually advancing pediatric postconcussion knowledge and care.

title: Perceived occupational HIV risk, stigma, and discriminatory attitudes among healthcare professionals in Jeddah and Riyadh, Saudi Arabia: a comparative cross-sectional study
abstract: Background Even with the presence of institutional policies, training programs, and various interventions, stigma associated with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) still obstructs fair access to healthcare services. In Saudi Arabia, there is a scarcity of research focusing on the regional variations among healthcare workers regarding their Fear of HIV Infection/Perceived Occupational Risk, their attitudes towards individuals living with HIV (PLHIV), and the stigma and discrimination they observe. Aim This research aimed to compare these aspects among healthcare professionals in Riyadh and Jeddah. Methods This study employed a comparative cross-sectional design involving 466 healthcare workers, including doctors, nurses, and allied health professionals, from selected healthcare facilities in Riyadh and Jeddah. Data collection was carried out using a validated, self-administered questionnaire that evaluated Fear of HIV Infection/Perceived Occupational Risk, attitudes towards PLHIV, observed stigma and discrimination, infection-control practices, the healthcare facility environment, and institutional policies. Descriptive statistics, comparisons between groups, and multiple regression analyses were utilized to explore regional differences and factors influencing attitudes towards PLHIV. Results In Riyadh, participants tended to be older and possess more experience than those in Jeddah. Specifically, 39.7% of individuals from Riyadh were between 30 and 39 years old, while 55.0% of those from Jeddah were aged 20 to 29. Additionally, those in Riyadh were more likely to have extensive professional experience and prior training related to HIV. Both groups showed moderate levels of fear regarding HIV infection and perceived occupational risk, along with similar levels of support from institutional policies. Differences between regions were noted in terms of observed stigma and discrimination, with Riyadh scoring higher, and in infection-control practices, where Jeddah had slightly better scores. Multivariable regression analysis revealed minimal evidence that factors such as region, previous HIV-related training, fear of HIV infection, perceived occupational risk, or health facility policies independently influenced attitudes toward people living with HIV (R 2 = 0.006, p = 0.596). Conclusion In both areas, healthcare workers exhibited moderate levels of fear regarding HIV infection and perceived occupational risks. However, misconceptions and discriminatory attitudes towards people living with HIV (PLHIV) were still apparent. These results highlight the necessity of ongoing, evidence-based HIV education, initiatives to reduce stigma, and enhanced institutional support systems to foster compassionate and fair treatment of individuals with HIV in Saudi Arabia.
authors: Amal Ibrahim Khalil; Seham Ahmed Mohamed El-Gamal; Sitah S Alshutwi; Waad Alsulami; Hanaa M. Abo Shereda

title: Recent advances and challenges in electronic nose technology for agricultural commodities and food quality assessment
abstract: Traditional methods for analyzing agricultural produce and food quality, such as chromatography and sensory evaluation, are often expensive, time consuming, and require skilled professionals, making them hard to implement for rapid and large-scale testing. The advent of Electronic nose (E-Nose) technology presents a promising alternative by emulating the human olfactory system through sensor arrays that identify volatile compounds and produce distinctive response patterns. This review examines the principles, evolution, and applications of E-nose systems for assessing the quality of food and agricultural products across diverse categories, including fish, meat, dairy products, tea, coffee, and edible oils. These systems provide non-destructive and smart analytical solutions for modern food-processing industries. Their role in identifying contamination, freshness assessment, authenticity, and monitoring fermentation plays a crucial role in modern food processing. Recent advancements integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies have significantly enhanced the efficacy of E-nose systems, enabling superior pattern recognition, data interpretation, and precise prediction capabilities. This enables objective and accurate quality assessment. Despite these advantages, the widespread adoption of this technology is hindered due to sensor drift, low sensitivity, high initial costs, and the difficulty of processing such complex data. Future research should focus on enhancing sensor stability, formulating resilient data analytics models, and decreasing system costs to facilitate scalability. Overall, E-nose technology has potential to transform food-quality assessment by providing the food industry with rapid, non-destructive, and intelligent analytical methods.
authors: R V Maneysha; Vakalapudi Sanjani; Kirthika Suresh

title: Hip Mobility Is Associated with Isokinetic Hip Adduction Torque in Recreationally Active Females: An Exploratory Study
abstract: This exploratory study examined whether trunk and hip mobility are associated with isokinetic hip torque in recreationally active females. Twenty-two women completed standing isokinetic hip testing at 60°·s⁻¹, yielding peak torque (PT; normalised to body mass), time to peak torque, and joint angle at peak torque for hip flexion–extension and abduction–adduction. Segmental (lumbar, thoracic, hip) and global mobility indices, composites of active range of motion, were quantified with inertial measurement units. Ninety-six Spearman correlations were computed with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) control; regression models were fitted post hoc. Two associations survived FDR correction: dominant hip adduction PT was related to hip mobility (r = .70, 95% CI .36 to .87) and to global mobility (r = .66, 95% CI .34 to .84). A segmental model accounted for 49% of the variance (adjusted R² = .485), with hip mobility the only stable predictor (β = 0.57, 95% CI 0.13 to 1.00). Sensitivity analyses indicated that this finding was robust to the construction of the indices and was carried mainly by hip flexion range of motion, which is unrelated to the fixed testing excursion. A side-matched analysis weakened the dominant-side association (r = .57). Associations of global mobility with the timing and angle of non-dominant adduction torque did not survive correction. The global index contains the hip index (r = .85), so the two are not independent constructs. Hip mobility is associated with hip adduction torque magnitude; the findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, preferably longitudinal studies.
authors: Şeyma Tuba Acar; Büşra Yücelsoy; Enda Francis Whyte; Cengiz Ölmez
venue: Research in Sport Education and Sciences

title: Oculomics using artificial intelligence derived retinal biomarkers for cardiovascular health
abstract: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from retinal vascular morphology, structural and perfusion imaging, retinal aging, metabolomics, and artificial intelligence models linking retinal biomarkers with cardiovascular risk factors, subclinical disease, clinical events, and cardiorenal and metabolic outcomes. These biomarkers may complement conventional risk assessment, but clinical utility is unproven and integration into cardiovascular digital twins remains conceptual. Prospective validation, standardized acquisition, interoperability, interpretability, and equitable evaluation are required before implementation.
authors: Harshal A. Sanghvi; Gurnoor Gill; Jay Patel; Minali Prasad; Najah A. Khan; Vimal Sarup; Shailesh Gupta; Kushagra Katariya; Sanjeev P. Bhavnani

title: Comparative study of zero degree and ambient plate temperature of submerged arc welded IS 2062 grade B steel for application in cold region
abstract: Submerged Arc Welding (SAW) is widely used in the fabrication of structural steel components; however, its performance under cold-region conditions remains insufficiently explored. This study presents a comparative investigation of SAW performed on IS 2062 Grade B steel plates maintained at ambient temperature and 0 °C, with the objective of assessing the feasibility of welding without preheating for cold-region applications. Welding trials were conducted in a bead-on-plate configuration, and the influence of arc voltage, travel speed, wire feed rate, and electrode stick-out was systematically evaluated using a Taguchi L16 orthogonal array. A total of 32 welded specimens, comprising 16 welds at ambient temperature and 16 welds at 0 °C, were produced and characterized through weld bead geometry measurements, microhardness testing, and optical microscopy. The results demonstrated that sound and defect-free welds could be successfully produced at both plate temperatures without the need for preheating. Comparative analysis revealed that welding at 0 °C increased heat dissipation from the weld zone, resulting in reduced weld penetration and reinforcement height compared with ambient-temperature welding. However, bead width showed only minor variations between the two temperature conditions. Microhardness measurements indicated that the 0 °C plate temperature significantly enhanced hardness, particularly within the heat-affected zone (HAZ), where an average increase of approximately 36% was observed relative to ambient-temperature welds. The reinforcement region exhibited a hardness increase of about 7.7%, while the weld metal hardness remained largely unaffected. Microstructural evaluation showed that ferrite and pearlite were the dominant phases in both welding conditions. Nevertheless, the higher cooling rate associated with the 0 °C plate temperature promoted grain refinement and reduced grain coarsening in the HAZ compared with ambient-temperature welding. Finally, the comparative study confirms that SAW of IS 2062 Grade B steel at 0 °C can achieve weld quality comparable to that obtained under ambient conditions while offering improved hardness and refined microstructural characteristics. These findings highlight the potential of SAW without preheating for structural steel fabrication and repair operations in cold-region environments.
authors: Abhijit Bhowmik; Raman Kumar; M. Arun; Ankush Mehta; Valentin Romanovski; Jeewan Singh; Rajender Kumar; Nagaraj Ashok; Abdulaziz N. Alhazaa

title: AI-driven strategies for sustainable cultural tourism marketing: a case study approach to visitor engagement and environmental impact
abstract: Introduction While artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionized real-time personalization in destination marketing, its strategic deployment to mitigate the negative externalities of cultural overtourism remains undertheorized. Methods Grounded in the Tourism 4.0 paradigm, this paper addresses this gap by introducing the AI–Sustainability–Engagement Nexus (ASEN) framework; a novel conceptual model integrating the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) paradigm with the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). To evaluate the model's structural propositions, we conduct an institutional multi-case desk study of secondary data from eight globally significant cultural heritage sites (e.g., The Louvre, The Palace Museum, Dunhuang Mogao Grottoes, and Machu Picchu). Results The findings suggest that AI-driven smart demarketing and spatial-temporal flow optimization is associated with alleviating localized overcrowding and carbon footprints in the cases where such effects are directly evidenced. Discussion Crucially, the analysis indicates that sustainability returns are not incidental byproducts of marketing efficiencies; rather, they require explicit environmental design parameters and robust institutional governance architectures. The paper concludes with an actionable, agenda-setting framework for destination management organizations (DMOs) to balance economic demands with heritage preservation.
authors: Muhammad Daood; Hongyun Tian; Dan Tshiswaka Dan; Reagan Kapilya; Saba Batool Wadhar

title: Lifefulness - feasibility and acceptability of a self-guided digital intervention promoting mental health among older adults in Sweden
abstract: Background: The number and proportion of older adults (≥65 years) is increasing worldwide, already exceeding 20% in Sweden. The growing number of older adults with concurrent physical and mental health issues, pose a major challenge for healthcare, rendering a critical need for low-cost, easily accessible behavioural interventions. Methods: This single-group feasibility trial evaluated a transdiagnostic digital self-help intervention, "Lifefulness", specifically adapted for older adults and designed to promote behaviour change and mental health. Content was based on cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and healthy ageing principles. Older adults were recruited from the community (age range 65-85) and were assigned to the six week intervention, which included three brief phone interviews focusing on program adherence. Outcomes included program use and acceptability as well as preliminary effects on quality of life and mental health outcomes. Results: A total of 73 individuals were included. Program utility was high on average, with 72% of participants engaging with the intervention daily or several times a week. The average time spent on the three interviews was 33 min per participant. The program was associated with favourable changes in various mental health symptoms and higher ratings of quality of life and the participants reported high satisfaction and credibility. Conclusions: These findings support the feasibility and resource-efficiency of a digital self-help intervention for older adults. The intervention warrants further testing in a randomized trial with long-term follow-up assessments of both outcomes and healthcare consumption.
authors: Martin Kraepelien; Karin Romberg; Neda Agahi; Nitya Jayaram‐Lindström; Amit Chakrabarti; Arun Kandasamy; Indranil Saha; Christopher Sundström

title: AI Agents for Multimodal Oncology Diagnosis: Toward Transparent and Traceable Clinical Decision Support
abstract: Cancer diagnosis depends on data from radiology, digital pathology, molecular profiling, laboratory testing, and longitudinal clinical records. AI performs well in selected tasks, but most systems remain narrow and disconnected from the iterative reasoning required in oncology. This Viewpoint defines an AI agent as a feedback-driven system that maintains task state, selects among governed tools, observes results, and revises its plan under explicit safety constraints. This definition separates agents from multimodal foundation models, retrieval-augmented generation, and fixed workflow automation. We organize the discussion across multimodal data collection, preprocessing, fusion and representation learning, and diagnostic decision support. We distinguished agent-level evidence, component- or infrastructure-level evidence, and prospective propositions throughout. Clinical translation will require resilient failure handling, guideline version control, prospective evaluation, computational and workflow feasibility, and clinician authority over final decisions. The near-term opportunity is therefore transparent and traceable clinical decision support rather than autonomous cancer diagnosis.
authors: Liuyang Yang; Liyu Shan; Xiangmei Yao; Renbin Zhao; Zengzheng Li; Shuai Feng; Yajie Wang

title: Irish giants: from myth to medicine
abstract: The archetype of the 'Irish giant' in folklore appears to be rooted in historical individuals afflicted by pituitary gigantism. This review compiles and critically assesses the veracity of historical accounts, primarily from the late 17th to the early 20th century, for a group of individuals with gigantism that had Irish origins. Clinical and, in some cases, osteological data (e.g., Charles Byrne, Cornelius Magrath, and Patrick Cotter) confirm a diagnosis of pituitary gigantism, a rare disease that is caused by excess growth hormone secretion from a pituitary adenoma. In the pre-scientific era, the effects of the unopposed hormone excess resulted in extreme tall stature, debilitating morbidity, and usually premature death. This aligns with our modern understanding of the potential severity of hormonal excess and tumour growth in pituitary gigantism. The high concentration of cases in Ulster is explained by a founder germline pathogenic variant (c.910 C > T, p.(R304*)) in the AIP gene, that was identified in multiple contemporary families, later in the skeleton of Charles Byrne and most recently, among the Irish diaspora. Estimated to have arisen around 2500 years ago, this variant established a direct medical explanation for a regional phenomenon. In this review we provide a detailed compilation of historical Irish giants and discuss the evidence linking myth and folklore to the modern medical reality of pituitary gigantism as a rare, severe genetic disease.
authors: Wouter W. de Herder; Paul Benjamin Loughrey; Márta Korbonits; Adrian Daly

title: EMERGING BLOOD-BASED BIOMARKERS IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE: FOCUS ON TAU, NFL, AND GFAP
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterised by progressive neurological disorder marked by the gradual decline of memory and cognitive abilities, affecting daily functioning and quality of life, imposing a leading socioeconomic disruption and healthcare burden.For the effective interventions, treatment and management, early diagnosis is important though conventional techniques like imaging and cerebrospinal fluid tests are invasive and costly.The inclusion of blood-based biomarkers provides a transformative approach for the early detection and disease monitoring.The purpose of this review is to critically evaluate the emerging evidence on Tau181, Tau217, NfL, and GFAP, aiming to delineate their role in reshaping future strategies for detection, monitoring, and intervention.Tau 217, among the tau isoforms biomarkers, demonstrated as a superior candidate with regards to diagnostic accuracy and stronger co-relation with Amyloid Positron Emission Tomography and disease progression, while compared to Tau 181.As the frontrunner biomarker, Tau 217 has emerged for AD with NfL and GFAP that provide precious complementary insights.Axonal degeneration is reflected by NfL while astrocytic activation is indicated by GFAP.Both serve as complementary markers.Combined multi-marker panels integrating these biomarkers enhanced sensitivity and specificity for AD detection.Therefore, these blood-based biomarkers provide a potential and revolutionary AD diagnosis and management by enabling non-invasive, early, and precise disease characterization.
authors: Sakina Turabi
venue: Indian Journal of Health Care Medical & Pharmacy Practice

title: Gender Differences in Visual Attention and Stated Preferences during Evaluation of Battery Electric Vehicles: An Exploratory Eye-Tracking Study
abstract: In this exploratory study were examined the gender differences in visual attention and stated preferences during the evaluation of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) using eye-tracking. Thirty-two participants (18 men, 14 women) viewed static images of the ten top-selling BEVs in Slovakia while eye movements were recorded across four predefined Areas of Interest (AOIs). Vehicle design attracted the greatest absolute dwell time in both groups. No gender difference reached conventional statistical significance (all p > 0.05), yet medium effect sizes were obtained for brand (d = 0.69), acceleration (d = 0.67), vehicle equipment (d = 0.60) and trunk capacity (d = 0.53), all rated higher by women, whereas men more often cited driving range as the main reason for model choice. The findings are hypothesis-generating and motivate confirmatory research with larger, purposively balanced samples.
authors: Viktória Cvacho; Radovan Madleňák; Alessandro Pagano; Edward Kozłowski
venue: Communications - Scientific letters of the University of Zilina

title: Beyond responsiveness: Differentiated associations among product features, psychological needs, perceived enjoyment, and continuance intention toward AI learning devices
abstract: As large language models are increasingly embedded in dedicated learning tablets, educational robots, and other physical AI learning devices (AILDs), sustaining learners' engagement beyond initial adoption has become a broader challenge for educational technology research and design. Although the technical capabilities of such devices continue to advance, the factors associated with continued use remain poorly understood. Drawing on the Stimulus-Organism-Response framework and Self-Determination Theory, this study examines associations among perceived personalization, interactivity, response timeliness, friendliness, autonomy, competence, relatedness, perceived enjoyment, and continuance intention. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 726 first-year senior high school students with experience using AILDs and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Effect sizes varied substantially across the estimated associations. The association between relatedness and perceived enjoyment had the largest effect size (f2 = 0.266), whereas the remaining effect sizes were small or negligible. Two theoretically informative expected associations were not supported: perceived personalization with autonomy and response timeliness with relatedness. The model explained 47.0% of the variance in continuance intention and 50.7% in perceived enjoyment. Perceived friendliness showed the largest feature-need association with relatedness, whereas response timeliness was associated with autonomy and competence but not with relatedness. Autonomy and competence showed statistically significant direct and indirect associations with continuance intention, whereas relatedness showed a statistically significant indirect association involving perceived enjoyment but no significant direct association with continuance intention. Perceived enjoyment was positively associated with continuance intention and was involved in statistically significant indirect associations for all three psychological needs. These findings reveal differentiated feature-need and need-intention association patterns in physical AI educational hardware and suggest that design attention may usefully extend beyond responsiveness to relational and enjoyable interaction. Because the data are cross-sectional, these association patterns should not be interpreted as evidence of temporal or causal relationships.
authors: Gang Ren; Xuezhen Wu; Gang Wang; Yinuo Ye; Zhihuang Huang; Tianyang Huang

title: Transport–Reaction–Signal Coupling in Lateral Flow Assays for Next‐Generation Point‐of‐Care Diagnostics
abstract: Lateral flow assays (LFAs) remain central to point-of-care diagnostics because they combine low cost, portability, and operational simplicity. Emerging diagnostic demands, including low-abundance biomarkers, complex sample matrices, quantitative readout, and multiplexed analysis, increasingly expose limitations that cannot be solved by signal-label enhancement alone. This Review examines recent LFA advances through a three-phase framework that couples porous-material mass transfer, interfacial reaction engineering, and signal transduction. The framework clarifies how membrane and flow design regulate analyte delivery and residence time, how antibody orientation, reaction amplification, and hook-effect mitigation improve capture efficiency and dynamic range, and how advanced nanolabels, integrated readers, multiplexed formats, and AI/ML-supported design and analysis expand performance across the assay workflow. By distinguishing intrinsic performance gains from strategies that transfer complexity to reagents, devices, or software, this Review provides design principles for sensitive, quantitative, and translation-oriented LFA systems.
authors: Yan Pan; Yuewei Li; Chao Mi; Zhengwen Yang; Lana McClements; Steven James Langford; Jiayan Liao

title: Artificial intelligence in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: A short narrative review of diagnostic and therapeutic implications
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and may progress from steatosis to metabolic dysfunctionassociated steatohepatitis, fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma.Insulin resistance, obesity, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, and impaired autophagy contribute to its pathogenesis.Early diagnosis, monitoring of disease progression, and assessment of therapeutic response remain important clinical challenges.Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning may improve disease prediction by integrating laboratory, metabolic, imaging, histological, and molecular data.Natural language processing and deep-learning approaches applied to radiological imaging and digital histopathology may support automated quantification of steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, while AI-assisted multi-omics analysis may identify molecular signatures relevant to disease stratification.Current evidence is strongest for retrospective case identification, imaging-based classification, and quantitative digital pathology; therapeutic selection and monitoring remain largely investigational.AI should therefore be viewed as a decision-support technology rather than a replacement for clinical judgment.
authors: Mona Mohamed Ibrahim Abdalla; Fabian Amalraj Davamani; Nabil A. S. Eid

title: Association between trusted sources of information and COVID-19 protective behaviors: results from a longitudinal survey of adults living in New York City during the pandemic
abstract: Introduction: For the public to adopt health promoting behaviors widely, there has to be sufficient trust in the institutions that disseminate information on protective behaviors. However, when members of the public lose trust in formal information sources, many seek information from informal information sources. Identifying trusted informal messengers is key to restore trust and effectively promote public health. Methods: We conducted repeat surveys with young adults and older adults living in New York City public housing to assess who they consider a trusted source of COVID-19 information, as well as their protective behavior practices across a period of five weeks. We then examined the association between trusted sources and participant behavior. Results: Participants in both age groups showed the highest trust in doctors or healthcare providers. Associations with protective behavior existed across multiple information sources, but strongest associations for both age groups were seen in relation to trusting one's faith leader for information. Discussion: Although other sources of information were more frequently cited as trustworthy by participants, trust in one's faith leader was the strongest predictor of protective behavior practices.
authors: Emily Gill; Lorna E. Thorpe; Donna Shelley; Natasha J. Williams

title: A Multimodal Therapist-Supervised Robotic Gait-Training Platform with Phase-Synchronized Infrared Thermal Biofeedback: A Concept-Level Technical and Translational Healthcare Framework
abstract: , an investigational fixed robotic gait-training platform combining a treadmill-synchronized lower-limb exoskeleton, dynamic body-weight support, phase-synchronized infrared-A (IR-A) thermal biofeedback, directional acoustic feedback, a semi-immersive display, camera-derived body representation, and artificial intelligence (AI)-supported therapist guidance. The architecture is defined through subsystem interfaces, implementation status, operational states, explicit risk controls, and a staged validation roadmap. No human participants, patient-level data, bench datasets, or statistical analyses were involved; subsystem factory checks did not characterize integrated performance. The installed exoskeleton has four actuated sagittal axes at the hips and knees, with in-series load cells supplying interaction-force inputs for contingent ipsilateral IR-A cueing under reduced guidance. The integrated AI module combines rule constraints with a case-based design, but has no trained statistical model or clinical cohort database; the therapist retains parameter-setting authority. Live video and avatar modes are implemented, whereas independent thermal monitoring and structured recommendation audit trails remain planned. Trigger thresholds, sampling rates, end-to-end latency, exposure limits, and fault responses remain undocumented or unverified. The contribution is a conceptual integration framework that distinguishes implemented functions, declared specifications, and unverified requirements. Independent mechanical, thermal, software, and human-factors validation, followed by appropriately authorized human studies, is required to establish safety, usability, technical reproducibility, and any incremental rehabilitation benefit. The optional thermal branch requires particular safeguards for impaired thermal sensation and cannot be assumed to add clinical value beyond robotic gait training alone.
