title: Payment models and reimbursement challenges for remote patient monitoring: a scoping review
abstract: Objective To map provider payment models and reimbursement policies for remote patient monitoring (RPM) across settings, and describe barriers, facilitators, and economic or operational consequences. Introduction RPM use is growing, yet reimbursement remains unsettled. Fragmented policies and misaligned payment incentives may limit scale-up and sustainability. Inclusion criteria Peer-reviewed sources on providers, payers or RPM recipients reported an RPM payment model, reimbursement policy or gap plus economic, operational or implementation findings. Grey sources provided RPM-specific payment, policy or coverage mechanics. Methods A JBI-aligned scoping review used database and four-strand grey-literature searches, dual independent title and abstract screening, Excel charting, ATLAS.ti coding, and MMAT appraisal of peer-reviewed studies to support interpretive caution. Results Fifty-six sources were included (34 peer-reviewed; 22 grey). Among peer-reviewed studies, fee-for-service predominated, often using management windows aligned with review frequency. Episode payments and shared-savings were less common and programme-specific. Across both source types, common barriers included coverage uncertainty, administrative workload, and misaligned incentives, while facilitators included value-oriented elements and transition funding. Economic findings were mixed, and utilisation outcomes were often unreported. Sources emphasised clear eligibility, supervision and frequency rules, brief documentation, and responsibility for devices, platforms, and connectivity. Three cross-cutting mechanisms concerned incentives and money flow, rules and billing gates, and workflow and workload. Conclusions Based on recurring patterns in the evidence, we propose prospective evaluation of a substitutive fee-for-service management window aligned with review frequency. Bundles and shared-savings may suit longitudinal monitoring but require attribution and data infrastructure. Public Interest Summary Remote patient monitoring lets clinicians track health between visits using data sent from home. We reviewed 56 sources to see how these services are paid for and what makes them easier or harder to run. Among peer-reviewed studies, fee-for-service was the most frequently reported payment model, often through monthly payments covering monitoring and review. Fewer studies described fixed-period payments or shared-savings contracts. Common hurdles were unclear rules, heavy paperwork, and incentives that do not align, for example when clinics pay while savings appear elsewhere. Helpful features were clear eligibility, short checklists, and temporary funds to start services. Our main takeaway: match payment to how monitoring works over time. One option for future evaluation is a monthly “management window” that replaces some clinic visits and states who pays for equipment and platforms. Other models may also be considered as data sharing improves. This may support more sustainable remote care.
authors: Kay Duit; Petra J. Porte; Kees Ahaus; Maureen Rutten‐van Mölken

title: A systematic review of non-contact medical IoT systems for physiological biomarker monitoring
abstract: Introduction Non-contact medical Internet of Things systems measure physiological biomarkers such as heart rate (HR), respiration rate (RR), temperature, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and blood pressure (BP) without physical contact with the patient. These systems combine sensing modalities including cameras, radar, Wi-Fi, acoustic, and infrared sensors with signal processing and learning algorithms to deliver comfortable, non-invasive monitoring. Prior reviews have largely examined individual sensing modalities or signal processing techniques in isolation, leaving cross-modality system architecture and privacy-preserving design underexamined. Methods We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines and analyzed 88 recent studies of non-contact monitoring systems. Studies were characterized by sensing modality, system architecture, target physiological parameter, validation setting, and reported performance. We additionally assessed each study for methodological quality and examined the extent to which privacy-preserving mechanisms were incorporated into system design. Results Radar and vision-based systems dominate the corpus, together accounting for approximately three-quarters of included studies, while sound, Wi-Fi, embedded sensor, and mixed-modality designs remain at an earlier stage of validation. Research effort is heavily concentrated on two parameters: RR appears in 83% of studies and HR in 67%, while no other parameter exceeds 11%. BP, SpO₂, and temperature therefore remain largely unaddressed by contactless methods. Heterogeneous reporting metrics across studies prevent direct statistical comparison of performance between modalities. Discussion The findings indicate that modality selection should be driven by deployment context rather than headline accuracy. Radar suits wards and intensive care units where patients are covered or moving, vision and sound suit structured clinical spaces with stable conditions, embedded sensor designs suit eldercare beds and chairs, and mixed radar and vision systems suit precision-critical settings such as neonatal and postoperative monitoring. Persistent challenges include signal reliability in uncontrolled environments, limited benchmarking due to the absence of standardized datasets, privacy and ethical concerns, and poor integration with existing healthcare infrastructure. Building on these insights, we propose a conceptual federated, edge-based learning framework, presented as a design proposal for future implementation rather than a validated system, and outline research directions to accelerate clinical translation.
authors: Bithi Banik; Saptanil Ghose; Ahnaf Hasnain Nahiun; Yuan Lin; Andrii Shalaginov; Debasish Ghose

title: A review of older adults’ acceptance of health monitoring tools: application status, theoretical acceptance models, and user-related and context-level influencing factors
abstract: Health monitoring tools enable real-time, accurate monitoring of physiological data in older adults, offering timely alerts and feedback that facilitate early detection of health problems and prompt intervention. However, adoption and use of these tools among older adults remains limited, significantly constraining their practical effectiveness. This narrative review examines the factors influencing older adults’ acceptance of health monitoring tools by synthesizing 49 studies, comprising 40 studies classified as core evidence and 9 as supplementary contextual evidence. Relevant literature was identified through a snowballing approach, beginning with key articles and tracing their reference lists and citing articles. Findings were synthesized through a thematic approach. Among the theoretical models identified in this review, the Technology Acceptance Model and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology are the most frequently applied, whereas the Senior Technology Acceptance Model, despite its specific relevance, has not been applied to health monitoring tool acceptance in any study included in this review. Key influencing factors can be grouped into two categories: user-related factors, such as demographic, health-related, and psychological characteristics; and tool- and context-level factors, such as privacy and security of monitoring data, interaction experience and ease of use, device appearance and invasiveness, and economic costs associated with pricing and technology access. Enhancing acceptance may require a comprehensive approach encompassing targeted health education and digital skills training, optimized user interfaces and privacy safeguards, multi-tiered financial subsidies, and the development of innovative theoretical models tailored to the older adult population.
authors: Qi Zhang; Zhang Yongqin

title: Bedside data to clinical foresight: the emerging role of nurses in AI-enabled predictive care and early patient deterioration detection
abstract: Early recognition of patient deterioration remains a cornerstone of high-quality nursing care and is essential for preventing avoidable morbidity, mortality, and unplanned intensive care admissions. Despite advances in physiological monitoring, delays in recognizing subtle clinical changes continue to contribute to adverse patient outcomes. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology capable of integrating large volumes of clinical, physiological, laboratory, and electronic health record (EHR) data to generate predictive insights that support timely clinical decision-making. AI-enabled predictive care systems, including machine learning algorithms, deep learning models, wearable sensor analytics, and early warning systems, provide nurses with opportunities to identify high-risk patients before overt clinical deterioration occurs. Rather than replacing nurses, these technologies augment clinical judgment by facilitating continuous risk assessment, prioritization of care, and proactive intervention. This narrative review explores the evolving role of nurses in AI-enabled predictive care and early patient deterioration detection. It examines the integration of bedside clinical observations with AI-driven predictive analytics, highlights current applications across acute and critical care settings, and discusses implications for nursing education, leadership, ethical practice, and interdisciplinary collaboration. The review also addresses challenges related to algorithmic bias, explainability, data quality, digital literacy, and governance while identifying future opportunities for human-centered AI implementation. Strengthening nurses' competencies in digital health and AI is essential for maximizing patient safety and ensuring equitable, evidence-based care in increasingly technology-enabled healthcare environments.
authors: R. Sheeba; N. Murugananandan; Tamilselvan; Tanusri Mandal; Israel Jeba Prab D.; Jamunarani P.; N Ilakkiya; N Padmapriya; Nithin Manly S.; Golda Sahaya Rani R.; J. Sathya Shenbega Priya; Mohammed Umar
venue: International Journal of Research in Medical Sciences

title: A review of machine learning and the internet of things for remote patient monitoring covering advances challenges and opportunities
abstract: As Machine Learning (ML) and the Internet of Things (IoT) have matured, their convergence has placed Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) at the centre of personalized, cost-effective care. The present work reviews progress in ML and IoT based RPM, covering how ML is applied within RPM, the principal ML models employed, the IoT infrastructures that underpin it, the use of RPM across different patient populations, the challenges that arise, and the directions the field may take. After a PRISMA-guided screening of work indexed in Springer, IEEE, MDPI, ACM, and Elsevier, 101 peer-reviewed studies published from 2020 onward were retained for a qualitative (narrative) synthesis structured around five research questions. The review is narrative in form yet is carried out under a structured and transparent protocol. Within the studies examined, RPM was reported to enable real-time monitoring, cut the number of in-person hospital visits, and reduce the cost of patient-centred care, while IoT- and ML-based designs that built in privacy-preserving techniques strengthened data security; across these studies, deep learning and hybrid ML models often reported higher predictive accuracy than conventional approaches, though typically on particular datasets and at greater computational cost. Across the ten systems compared here, the eight that reported a single determinate figure gave accuracies with a median of 94.5% (range 92% to 98%) and latencies with a median of 265 ms (range 120 ms to 350 ms), and not one of them was evaluated at a site other than the one where it was developed, so these numbers describe individual study conditions rather than performance at population level. Among the obstacles that surface repeatedly are patient adherence, interoperability, scalability, and the protection of data. On balance, the body of evidence gathered here suggests that RPM built on ML and IoT can make monitoring safer, more flexible, and more anticipatory; reaching that level across whole populations, however, will call for sturdier systems, broader patient participation, and thorough clinical validation.
authors: Sumitra Singar; Raghuveer Singh Dhaka; Manmohan Sharma

title: Renegotiating autonomy and safety: disentangling tensions emerging for older adults living with smart monitoring systems
abstract: Smart monitoring systems (SMS) are increasingly deployed in community-based care to empower older adults to live safely and independently. However, existing research largely treats monitoring as a process in which continuous data collection and real-time alerts are intended to translate into improved outcomes. What remains underexplored is how older adults experience monitoring and how it shapes their behavior over time. In this qualitative longitudinal study, 21 older adults are accompanied from SMS installation for more than one year, with individual semi-structured interviews conducted across four data collection phases. Findings reveal that older adults actively anticipate how the system interprets their behavior, producing three responses: reactance, that is, disengaging from devices to reclaim autonomy over safety; preemptive behavior, for instance, restructuring daily routines to avoid triggering alerts constraining their autonomy and safety; and performative compliance, that is, managing behavior to satisfy caregivers rather than personal needs, leading to a loss of autonomy. These constitute autonomy-safety value tensions: a technology designed to advance both values instead produces conditions under which protecting one systematically undermines the other. To this end, this study provides empirical insights into unintended consequences and a conceptual model explaining how value tensions emerge, with implications for practitioners and caregivers.
authors: Laura Madeleine Detels; Mingsong Zhai; Zhao Cai; Manuel Trenz

title: INTELLIGENT INTRUSION DETECTION USING MACHINE LEARNING FOR SECURE DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE
abstract: The growing interconnectivity of digital infrastructure has increased exposure to cyber threats and strengthened the need for effective intrusion detection. Machine-learning techniques offer promising capabilities for recognizing malicious network behavior from structured traffic observations. However, differences in the representation of benign and attack traffic can affect the development and interpretation of intelligent detection systems. This study characterized the dataset and examined the distribution of legitimate and malicious network traffic, with particular attention to major intrusion groups and less frequently represented attack categories. A secondary descriptive analysis of the original CIC-IDS2017 network-flow dataset was conducted. Dataset structure, traffic attributes, class labels, and traffic-category distributions were systematically examined. Network observations were organized into benign traffic and broader intrusion groups to describe their relative representation. The analysis identified substantial variation across traffic categories. Legitimate network communication represented the largest component, whereas malicious observations comprised multiple attack types with different levels of occurrence. Denial-of-service-related activities represented a major portion of intrusion traffic, while port scanning, brute-force, web-based, botnet, infiltration, and other attack categories contributed additional security-relevant observations. Several specialized attack classes were sparsely represented, demonstrating notable class imbalance. These findings indicate that CIC-IDS2017 provides a diverse foundation for machine-learning-oriented intrusion-detection research. The observed traffic diversity supports analysis of multiple malicious behaviors, while class imbalance highlights the importance of appropriate evaluation strategies and careful interpretation of future predictive models. The study provides a structured basis for subsequent intelligent cybersecurity research and model development.
authors: Mohammad Majharul Islam Jabed; Bhanu Pratap Singh

title: Financial fraud detection model based on dual-layer knowledge graph
abstract: Corporate financial fraud is becoming increasingly complex and covert, necessitating the development of intelligent identification frameworks that combine accuracy and interpretability. This study proposes a detection method based on a two-layer knowledge graph. A two-layer structure is constructed, combining cross-layer path mining and rule vector discrimination to achieve end-to-end closed-loop detection. Experiments show that the method maintains stable performance as the enterprise scales up. In a sample of 700 enterprises, the method achieves an accuracy of 94.2%, a precision of 92.7%, a recall of 93.5%, an F1 score of 93.1%, an AUC of 0.95, and an MCC of 0.88. In a multi-enterprise scenario in the manufacturing industry, the detection accuracy reaches a maximum of 97%, AUC 0.975, and rule trigger rate 87%. After 100 iterations of rule mining, approximately 390 high-quality rules are retained, with an average support exceeding 0.069. This method demonstrates significant advantages and provides a practical intelligent framework for enterprise auditing and supervision.
authors: Ying Jiang

title: A four-coil magnetic levitation force sensor system for contactless horizontal force perturbations measurement
abstract: Accurate measurement of small horizontal forces under finite vertical loading remains challenging because conventional contact-based methods can be affected by friction, support interference, contact deformation, and force coupling. This study presents a four-coil magnetic levitation sensor system for contactless estimation of the magnitude of a static horizontal force applied along a predefined axis. Four coil–permanent magnet pairs levitate a rigid platform, while the applied force is inferred from the change in the average steady-state coil current caused by lateral coil–magnet misalignment. A magnetic force model describes the coupling among coil current, vertical air gap, lateral displacement, and restoring force, and an experimental calibration is used to convert the current response into applied force. Static calibration was performed using known horizontal loads, followed by independent validation using loads not included in the calibration. The resulting current–force relationship was nonlinear but repeatable, with discrepancies of approximately 3.5–4.1% over the tested range. The horizontal displacement presented in the analysis was inferred from the static magnetic-force equilibrium, whereas the vertical air gap was measured using four laser displacement sensors. Power consumption tests and a lumped parameter vibration analysis of the designed prototype were also used to identify practical limitations related to scaling, thermal drift, vibration, and sensor bandwidth. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using the coil current as a contactless sensing output for static force magnitude estimation under controlled vertical loading.
authors: Yuxin Yang; William S.P. Robertson; Azadeh Jafari; Maziar Arjomandi

title: An Integrated Visual–Textual Approach for Accurate Phishing Detection on Social Media Platforms
abstract: The rapid rise of phishing attacks on social media platforms highlights an urgent and growing cybersecurity challenge in today’s digitally connected world. As millions of users rely on these platforms for communication, business, and information sharing, cybercriminals increasingly exploit them to distribute deceptive links, fake advertisements, and fraudulent messages designed to steal sensitive data such as login credentials, financial information, and personal identities. The sophistication of these attacks—often leveraging social engineering techniques, impersonation of trusted entities, and AI-generated content—makes them difficult for users to recognize and avoid. Consequently, there is a critical need for robust and intelligent detection systems capable of reliably identifying malicious content in real time. Such systems should incorporate advanced machine learning models, behavioral analysis, and continuous adaptation to emerging attack patterns in order to effectively mitigate risks, protect users, and maintain trust in social media ecosystems. This paper proposes a multimodal phishing detection framework that integrates visual indicators (e.g., logos and page imagery) with textual signals (e.g., URL structure and phishing-related keywords). Our contributions are threefold: (i) a feature fusion strategy that combines visual and textual cues, (ii) the construction of a comprehensive dataset using feature extraction and natural language processing (NLP), and (iii) a comparative evaluation of multiple machine learning models. We extract 27 discriminative URL features and evaluate Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Naı̈ve Bayes. Random Forest achieves the best performance, reaching 98.6% accuracy with a false positive rate of 0.01, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed multimodal approach for phishing detection on social media.
authors: Ala’ S Mughaid; Andaleep Shdeifat; Abedalmuhdi Almomany; Mohammad Kharabsheh; Shadi Mahmoud Faleh AlZu’bi

title: Interactive Industrial Metaverse Platform based on Digital Twin and Extended Reality for Real-time Process Monitoring
abstract: The transition toward Industry 4.0 and the emerging Industry 5.0 paradigm highlights the need for real-time integration of heterogeneous machines, human-machine collaboration, and interoperable data flows. Modern factories frequently combine advanced machines with legacy systems, leading to inconsistent data structures and limited process visibility. To address these challenges, a DT-XR-based industrial metaverse framework was developed to enable standardized data acquisition, cloud-centered information management, and immersive visualization across diverse manufacturing environments. The framework provides a multilayer architecture that consolidates heterogeneous controller and sensor data into a unified structure, processes them on edge devices, stores them as cloud-based time-series records, and delivers them to digital twin and XR interfaces for real-time monitoring. This approach supports the cyber-physical integration emphasized in Industry 4.0 and the human-centered decision-making prioritized in Industry 5.0. The framework was validated through two case studies. In a hybrid additive-subtractive testbed, heterogeneous controller data and sensor signals were synchronized within a digital twin with an end-to-end latency of approximately 33.00ms. In an industry-scale blow molding system operating with PLC-based legacy machine, standardized data management and AR-based visualization of heater temperatures, mold timing, environmental conditions, and inline states were achieved, with an average round-trip latency of approximately 1040.92ms. These results demonstrate that the proposed DT-XR framework enhances interoperability, process transparency, and operator-centered decision-making, and shows strong potential for scaling to larger production systems and future Industry 5.0 applications. © 2026 The Authors. venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Machine Learning Detection of Revenue Leakage From Clinical Coding, Claims, and Reimbursement Discrepancies
abstract: Healthcare revenue cycles increasingly depend on accurate clinical documentation, coding, claims processing, and reimbursement, yet their complexity creates substantial opportunities for revenue leakage. Coding inaccuracies, incomplete documentation, claim denials, underpayments, contractual inconsistencies, and reimbursement discrepancies can reduce healthcare organizations’ financial performance while increasing administrative burden. Conventional audit approaches are often retrospective, rule-based, and resource-intensive, limiting their ability to identify complex or evolving patterns across large volumes of clinical and financial data. This study examines a machine learning framework for detecting revenue leakage by integrating clinical coding, claims, payment, denial, and reimbursement information. The framework applies supervised and anomaly-detection techniques to identify discrepancies between expected and received reimbursement, coding irregularities, recurrent denial patterns, and financially significant claim anomalies. Predictive features incorporate diagnosis and procedure codes, billed charges, payer characteristics, reimbursement amounts, denial reasons, and historical payment behavior. Model performance can be evaluated using precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and financial recovery indicators. The proposed approach supports risk-based claim prioritization, earlier identification of revenue loss, targeted auditing, and data-driven revenue-cycle management across healthcare reimbursement systems.
authors: Jine Laner
venue: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews

title: Diabetic retinopathy detection models: Transition from conventional to deep learning approaches and a hybrid model
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic and common disease all over the world that has many side effects. One of the main side effects of this disease is diabetic retinopathy (DR), which if not diagnosed and treated in time, causes low vision and eventually blindness. Early diagnosis of this disease prevents the occurrence of complications of it. As artificial intelligence and deep learning technologies progress, various models for diagnosing medical images like fundus images in diabetic retinopathy became available. Due to the increase in the prevalence of DR, we propose a hybrid method with VGG-16 deep learning model and a hand-crafted feature extraction technique, namely Principal Component Analysis, for the classification of DR. To achieve this goal, two well-known datasets, namely APTOS 2019 and Messidor-2, are considered. On each of the datasets, two hand-crafted models, namely Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Local Binary Patterns (LBP), and various deep learning models are implemented. In order to evaluate the models and compare them with each other and the state-of-the-art in this field, standard metrics such as accuracy are calculated. The results show that deep learning models are significantly superior to manual models regarding performance in diagnosing DR and its degrees. Moreover, the proposed hybrid method shows notable improvement in classification performance. Furthermore, the results obtained in this study have shown better performance than some other recent studies in the literature.
authors: Önsen Toygar; Zeinab Jabbarbabouei
venue: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences

title: A quantitative and deployment-aware survey of AI-based techniques for IoT botnet detection and classification
abstract: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) systems has increased their exposure to botnet-based threats, while device heterogeneity, constrained resources, weak security configurations, and evolving attack behavior continue to complicate effective detection. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches have consequently become central to IoT botnet detection and classification, spanning machine learning, deep learning, hybrid and ensemble models, graph-based methods, deep reinforcement learning, federated learning, and edge-oriented frameworks. This survey presents a quantitative and deployment-aware analysis of 43 empirical studies published between 2020 and August 2026. In addition to methodological synthesis, the reviewed literature is analyzed across primary technique category, classification depth, dataset usage and breadth, cross-dataset validation, deployment evidence, evaluation practices, explainability, zero-day evaluation, and adversarial robustness. Hybrid approaches form the largest technique category (32.6%), followed by deep learning (23.3%). Binary detection and attack-type classification are each addressed in 62.8% of the studies, whereas malware-family classification and lifecycle-stage modeling remain less common at 27.9% and 14.0%, respectively. Dataset dependence also remains substantial: N-BaIoT is used in 48.8% of the corpus, while only 32.6% of studies perform explicit cross-dataset validation. Moreover, only 14.0% provide strong deployment evidence, and explicit XAI, zero-day evaluation, and adversarial-robustness assessment appear in 9.3%, 18.6%, and 7.0% of studies, respectively. These findings indicate that future IoT botnet research should move beyond benchmark-centered accuracy toward generalizable, deployment-efficient, behavior-aware, interpretable, and adversarially robust detection systems.
authors: Sara Afzal; Abraham Gebrehiwot; Filippo Maria Lauria; Farrukh Aslam Khan

title: TinyML-Optimised Multimodal Lstm for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Smart Home IoT Systems
abstract: The rapid rise in IoT smart home devices generates extensive time-series datasets, while anomaly detection solutions remain largely dependent on cloud-based processing, resulting in latency, privacy concerns, and connectivity requirements. Existing approaches often rely on a single modality and insufficiently address concept drift and edge-device constraints. This study proposes a TinyML-optimised multimodal LSTM model for unsupervised anomaly detection in smart home applications deployed on a Raspberry Pi edge device. Temperature, humidity, and power consumption modalities were combined to capture cross-modal relationships. A simulated dataset represented normal diurnal and seasonal behaviour and incorporated three anomaly types: heat spikes, power outages, and midnight appliance usage. Model training used only normal-value sequences within a 250-timestep sliding window. TinyML optimisation reduced the stored LSTM model size to 196 KB, which represents the model storage size and should not be interpreted as total runtime memory or direct evidence of real-time or low-power operation. An online learning strategy was employed to address concept drift through periodic retraining. On the simulated test set, the model achieved 98.97% recall, 8.79% precision, 8.86% F1-score, 0.294 Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), and an AUC-ROC of 0.9984. The confusion matrix comprised 83,416 true negatives, 3,994 false positives, 4 false negatives, and 385 true positives. Although the model detected nearly all injected anomalies, its low precision indicates a substantial false-alarm burden and limits claims regarding deployment readiness.
authors: Osaretin Edith Okoro; Nurudeen Mahmud Ibrahim; Kirubakaran Prema; Suleiman Aliyu Muhammad

title: Multimodal deep learning with particle swarm guided feature refinement for automated pain detection
abstract: Pain assessment remains a significant challenge in clinical practice because conventional self-reporting methods are subjective and unreliable for non-verbal, cognitively impaired, and critically ill patients. Existing automated pain detection approaches primarily rely on single-modality data or limited multimodal integration, resulting in inadequate feature representation, feature redundancy, and reduced classification performance. To address these limitations, this study proposes a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates physiological signals, facial images, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and clinical text for objective pain detection. The physiological branch employs a hybrid architecture comprising a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), and Deep Neural Network (DNN) to learn hierarchical spatial-temporal representations. The facial branch combines EfficientNet and Residual Network (ResNet) to extract discriminative facial features, while a CNN-based architecture processes MRI images. Clinical narratives are encoded using Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and BioBERT to capture contextual semantic information. An Adaptive Feature Refinement Layer (AFRL) enhances modality-specific feature learning, followed by Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) for feature selection and a novel PSO-Guided Feature Refinement Layer (PFRL) for adaptive feature weighting prior to multimodal fusion. We implement the framework in TensorFlow and PyTorch and evaluate it on the BioVid, UNBC-McMaster, and Trigeminal Neuralgia MRI datasets. Experimental results achieve 96.2% accuracy, outperforming Support Vector Machine (82.4%), K-Nearest Neighbors (79.6%), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (88.9%), and AdaBoost (90.7%). The proposed framework provides a robust, scalable, and clinically applicable solution for automated multimodal pain detection and improved clinical decision support.
authors: Karim Gasmi; Sarah Almaghrabi; Ibrahim Rizqallah Alzahrani; Adil Mahmoud Mohamed Mahmoud; Alameen Abdalrahman Eltoum; Abdullah Sawdi Alenzi; Osama R. Shahin; Ahmed I. Taloba; Fatma Al Zahraa Hamed Abdel Hameed

title: Metaheuristic and Nonlinear Optimization for Intelligent Energy and Environmental Systems: A Review of Renewable Generation, Smart Metering, Networks and Environmental Monitoring
abstract: Energy and environmental systems are full of decisions that must be tuned under uncertainty: how much power to draw from a solar panel, how to bill and balance consumption on a smart grid, how to share spectrum in a wireless network and how to read a biosensor in the field. Computing itself is part of the problem, since data centres, web services and smartphones draw a growing share of electricity. Many of these decisions have no closed-form solution because the underlying models are nonlinear, noisy or only partly known. Metaheuristic search, fuzzy reasoning, nonlinear analysis and data-driven forecasting are now used to find good settings, but studies are spread across power engineering, networking and environmental science. This chapter reviews optimization and learning methods for five groups of problems: renewable generation and grid interfacing, smart metering and energy forecasting, resource allocation and energy-aware computing in communication and IoT systems, environmental and agricultural monitoring, and the approximation of nonlinear physical models. The review finds that hybrid metaheuristics, such as grey wolf optimization with opposition-based learning, improve tracking and control in renewable systems, that tree ensembles and regression models are standard for consumption forecasting, that fuzzy optimization handles uncertainty in network resource allocation, that signal-aware transfer scheduling and green design guidelines reduce the energy used by smartphones and web services, and that neural approximation can stand in for expensive solvers of nonlinear equations. Few studies, however, compare methods on shared benchmarks or report computation cost. Future work should use common test systems, report run time next to solution quality and link optimization with forecasting in one loop.
authors: Kennedy R; Santhalakshmi M; Balamurali S
venue: International Journal Of Recent Trends In Multidisciplinary Research

title: Diabetes Mellitus Detection System Using Machine Learning with the Support Vector Machine (SVM) Method
abstract: Background: Diabetes Mellitus (DM) remains a major non-communicable disease with a continuously rising prevalence, and delayed diagnosis increases the risk of severe complications such as kidney failure, cardiovascular disease, and neuropathy. Objective: This study aims to design and build a web-based Diabetes Mellitus detection system using the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm and to measure the classification performance of the resulting model. Methods: The dataset consisted of 170 medical records from Rumah Sakit Cut Meutia collected over the 2023-2025 period, comprising eight predictor variables (gender, blood pressure, glucose level, insulin, skin thickness, Body Mass Index, diabetes family-history score, and age). The data were preprocessed through label encoding, median-based missing-value imputation, Interquartile Range (IQR) outlier clipping, and Min-Max normalization, then split into 80% training data (132 records) and 20% testing data (34 records). The SVM model, comparing Linear and Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernels, was optimized using GridSearchCV with Stratified 5-Fold Cross Validation. Results: The optimal model used an RBF kernel with C = 1 and gamma = 0.01, achieving a cross-validation ROC-AUC of 96.43%. On the test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 88.24%, precision of 94.12%, recall of 84.21%, and an F1-score of 88.89%, with a test-set AUC of 96.1%. Usability testing using the System Usability Scale (SUS) on 10 respondents produced an average score of 71.75, placed in the "Good" category. Conclusion: The SVM-based web system was able to classify Diabetes Mellitus status accurately and was assessed by users as easy to operate, indicating its feasibility as a decision-support tool for the early detection of Diabetes Mellitus.
authors: Syahira Ratu Fadilla; Sayed Fachrurrazi; Desvina Yulisda

title: OptimalStop: Predictability–complexity trade-off for optimising stop detection in human mobility data
abstract: Human mobility analysis increasingly relies on large-scale trajectory data, yet results remain highly sensitive to preprocessing choices that are rarely applied in a consistent or well-documented manner. Stop detection, which transforms raw location traces into sequences of visited places, is a particularly critical and bias-prone step, with parameter choices often guided by dataset-specific conventions. The absence of systematic and transparent parameter-selection practices risks introducing methodological bias and limits the comparability and reproducibility of mobility studies. Here, we introduce OptimalStop , a model-agnostic optimisation framework for stop detection that exploits a predictability–complexity trade-off in human mobility trajectories to guide preprocessing. OptimalStop operates as a higher-level tuning layer applicable to any method that produces symbolic mobility sequences. By framing stop detection as a multi-objective optimisation problem, the framework identifies compact Pareto-optimal sets of parameter configurations that balance predictability and structural complexity, avoiding over-fragmented or over-aggregated representations. We evaluate OptimalStop on both real-world and synthetic mobility datasets using multiple stop detection algorithms, and confirm through controlled synthetic experiments that the predictability–complexity trade-off is structurally grounded in recurrent return-to-place behaviour rather than being a mathematical artefact of discretisation. The results show that OptimalStop consistently retains near-optimal solutions while substantially reducing the effective parameter search space within a reasonable computational time. An optional automatic selection strategy further demonstrates that high-quality stop detection can be obtained without ground truth, outperforming or matching commonly used sensitivity-based tuning approaches. We release OptimalStop under an open licence, providing a transparent and reproducible framework for parameter selection that supports more structured mobility data preprocessing. While demonstrated here for stop detection, the underlying predictability–complexity balance offers a general perspective for mitigating methodological bias in mobility analytics.
authors: Kamil Smolak; Katarzyna Siła-Nowicka

title: Robust Range-Doppler Acoustic Feature Fusion for Unauthorised Personnel Crossing Detection on Underground Belt Conveyors
abstract: Unauthorised personnel crossing underground belt conveyors poses a serious safety risk in coal mines. To improve the reliability of non-contact crossing detection under complex acoustic interference, this paper proposes an acoustic sensing method based on distance-velocity feature fusion. An adaptive acoustic interference suppression and echo enhancement method is first employed to mitigate multipath interference and suppress mechanical vibration and background noise. Time-of-flight (ToF) and Doppler information are then jointly extracted from FMCW acoustic echoes to obtain the temporal distance trajectory and radial velocity of human targets. Based on these complementary features, a distance-velocity coupled temporal discrimination model is developed to distinguish continuous human crossing behavior from static obstacles and transient mechanical interference through spatial constraints, motion verification, and temporal state transitions. Experiments conducted on a simulated conveyor belt platform demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a detection accuracy of 96.5%, outperforming single-feature acoustic detection methods and maintaining stable detection performance under different sensing distances, motion directions, noise levels, and conveyor operating conditions.
authors: Yuqing Yin; Baoxuan Xu; Xu Yang; Guo Wenhao

title: A reinforcement learning-based intrusion detection system for internet of things with zero-day resilience
abstract: The conventional intrusion detection systems (IDS) are often found to be ineffective when faced with zero-day attacks that are novel compared to previously learned behavior patterns. This paper presents the development of a robust and adaptive IDS for the internet of things (IoT) using a deep Q-network (DQN) agent. A custom environment is designed in which state abstraction is applied to convert high-dimensional feature vectors into discrete state spaces. The proposed agent model is trained to detect normal and malicious traffic using a reward and penalty mechanism to encourage the agent to take correct decisions. The validation of the proposed methodology is carried out using the UNSW-NB15 dataset under both known attack and zero-day attack scenarios. The results showed detection accuracies of 99.56% for known attacks and 99.11% for zero-day attacks.
authors: Sowmya Somanath; Usha Banavikal Ajay; K N Sangeetha
venue: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence

title: Trustworthy Phishing URL Detection Using Machine Learning: Performance Analysis and Future Directions
abstract: Over the years, Uniform Resource Locator (URL) Phishing has been a threat to online security because their scams exploit trust in a misleading URL to trick unsuspecting users into disclosing their username or passwords and other personal information. Not only that, but it is also crucial to identify these malicious URLs and ensure online platforms and users are protected. The ISCXURL2016 data was utilized for the purpose of analyzing the performance of different Machine Learning (ML) models in differentiating phishing and legitimate URLs in this paper. A wide range of classifiers were explored including the classic classifiers as well as more advanced ensemble classifiers. The results of the experiments indicate that ensemble-based boosting models can be more beneficial for URL phishing detection. HistGradientBoost achieved the highest accuracy of 98.47%, followed closely by LightGBM and XGBoost that both outperformed the accuracy of 98%. The other classifiers, RandomForest and ExtraTrees, also performed well with accuracy above 97% and traditional classifiers such as Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) showed the poorest performance with an accuracy of 67.75%. The results show that the boosting-based ensembles provide a suitable negation of the complex and non-linear structure of phishing URLs. Along with empirical evaluation, it offers a Properties & Positioning viewpoint as well as the importance of the ML-based phishing detection in the broader context of cybersecurity issues. Moreover, it discusses the future directions, with Federated Learning (FL) in the context of decentralized and privacy-preserving collaboration and Large Language Models (LLM) in the context of semantic reasoning and flexibility. These insights together will provide the building blocks for more intelligent, adaptive and trustworthy phishing organizations.

title: Unsupervised Detection of Migraine-Related Anomalies in Nocturnal Blood Volume Pulse Dynamics Using a Convolutional Autoencoder
abstract: This study investigates whether sleep-time blood volume pulse (BVP) dynamics exhibit anomalous patterns during migraine days.Rather than framing migraine detection as a supervised classification problem, we adopt an unsupervised anomaly detection approach to identify deviations from patientspecific baseline sleep physiology.Participants were adults (18+ years) who met the criteria of the International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-3) for episodic migraine and reported between 4 and 14 migraine days per month.For each participant, a longitudinal BVP recording containing multiple nights of sleep data was analyzed in conjunction with a migraine diary.Participants with migraine data (n = 17) were compared using aggregated anomaly metrics.For most participants, the p99 ratio was higher with the 30 s / 5 s configuration compared to the 60 s/10 s setup, indicating greater separation between migraine and non-migraine days at finer temporal resolution.The results indicate that migraine days are generally associated with increased anomaly scores in sleep-time BVP signals.In addition, the majority of the participants exhibited a greater sensitivity to migraine-related changes in BVP dynamics.Overall, these findings support the use of a convolutional autoencoder for detecting migraine-associated deviations in sleep-time BVP signal dynamics, particularly in settings where labeled data are limited and inter-subject variability is high.
authors: Rūta Jankevičiūtė; Vytautas Abromavičius; Saulius Andruškevičius

title: An Edge-Enabled IoT Healthcare Monitoring Framework Using Raspberry Pi Pico W and Cloud-Based Physiological Data Management
abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has created significant opportunities for developing intelligent remote healthcare systems capable of continuous patient monitoring. However, many existing low-cost healthcare monitoring solutions are limited by single-parameter sensing, poor interoperability, inadequate cloud integration, and restricted scalability for multi-patient applications. This paper presents the design and development of an edge-enabled IoT-based smart healthcare monitoring platform using the Raspberry Pi Pico W for real-time acquisition, processing, and cloud storage of physiological data. The proposed system integrates three biomedical sensors, namely the MAX30102 sensor for heart rate and blood oxygen (SpO₂) monitoring, the DS18B20 digital sensor for body temperature measurement, and the AD8232 analog front-end for electrocardiogram (ECG) signal acquisition. The embedded edge node performs local signal preprocessing, physiological parameter extraction, timestamp synchronization, and secure wireless transmission of patient data to a cloud database through REST-based communication over Wi-Fi. A cloud-centric architecture is developed using Supabase to provide reliable data storage, multi-node scalability, and seamless integration with future intelligent healthcare applications. The proposed framework supports continuous remote patient monitoring while maintaining a low hardware cost, reduced computational overhead, and efficient data communication. Experimental implementation demonstrates reliable real-time physiological data acquisition, stable cloud synchronization, and effective management of multimodal healthcare data suitable for subsequent analytical and predictive applications. The developed platform establishes a scalable foundation for next-generation smart healthcare systems by combining low-cost embedded hardware, edge computing, and cloud technologies to improve accessibility, reliability, and remote medical monitoring.

title: SmartSign: Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition and Speech Generation Platform
abstract: Sign language is an essential means of communication for individuals with hearing and speech impairments. However, communication barriers often arise between sign language users and people who are unfamiliar with sign language. To address this challenge, this paper presents a SmartSign: Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition and Speech Generation Platform that uses computer vision and deep learning techniques to recognize hand gestures and convert them into understandable text. The proposed system is developed using Python, Flask, OpenCV, MediaPipe, and a trained machine learning model. It provides multiple detection methods, including image-based detection, video-based detection, multi-image processing, and real-time webcam recognition. The system also incorporates interactive learning features such as sign language practice, tutorials, a chatbot, progress tracking, history, and analytics to support continuous learning. Additionally, an administrative panel enables administrators to manage users, tutorials, detection history, and application settings. The system processes hand landmarks and extracts relevant features to identify corresponding signs and display the predicted results through a user-friendly web interface. By integrating sign recognition with learning and progress-monitoring facilities, the proposed application aims to improve accessibility, support sign language education, and reduce communication barriers. The system demonstrates the potential of combining computer vision, deep learning, and web technologies to develop an interactive and accessible sign language recognition platform

title: FCAE-Mixer: frequency-aware convolutional autoencoder with dual-branch mixing for time series anomaly detection
abstract: Abstract The core of complex time series anomaly detection lies in the effective extraction of multi-dimensional features. However, existing methods often separate the synergistic mechanism among local temporal, global variable, and frequency domain features. To this end, this paper proposes a network that balances temporal, variable, and frequency domain features. The model innovatively combines a one-dimensional convolutional autoencoder and a multi-layer perceptron to extract local temporal transient features and global variable spatial mappings, respectively. Furthermore, an FFT-Attention module is introduced to enhance adaptive focus on low-frequency spectral modes while suppressing high-frequency noise. Finally, the dual-branch reconstruction error is used as the anomaly judgment basis, and anomaly samples are identified via the reconstruction error, which jointly benefits from both time-domain morphological and frequency-domain spectral processing. Evaluation results on seven benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average F1 score (without point-adjustment) of 0.3317, outperforming all compared baseline methods with a 10.50% relative F1 improvement over the suboptimal baseline Transformer with an average F1 of 0.3002, demonstrating the effectiveness of multi-dimensional joint modeling in time series anomaly detection.
authors: Longfei Li; Yinghua Tong

title: A Method for Four-Property Detection of Electronic Financial Archive Data Based on Dynamic Particle Swarm Algorithm
abstract: Background/Objectives:The detection of the four properties Authenticity, Integrity, Usability, and Security (AIUS) of Electronic Financial Archive Data (EFAD) data involves multiple technical aspects, such as data encryption, integrity verification, and access control. This complexity prevents the static Particle Swarm Algorithm (PSA) from iteratively adapting to the dynamic changes in financial data, leading to high detection deviations and an elevated risk rate for electronic financial archive data. In order to ensure the reliability of financial data storage, a method for detecting the four properties of electronic financial file data based on a Dynamic Particle Swarm Algorithm (DPSA) is proposed to promote the standardization of intelligent financial management. The authenticity, integrity, usability and security requirements of Electronic Financial File Data (EFFD) are analyzed in depth. The SM2 algorithm in Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA) is used to encrypt and process the initial electronic financial file data to optimize the security of electronic financial file data. The four-property detection index of electronic financial file data is iteratively optimized based on the dynamic particle swarm algorithm, and the Fitness Value (FV) of the four-property detection index of electronic financial file data is calculated. The abnormality of electronic financial file data is judged based on the fitness value, so as to realize the Four-Property Detection (FPD) of electronic financial file data. Experimental verification shows that this method achieves good results in the four-propertyistic detection of electronic financial file data. The data encryption results are random, effectively improving the security of electronic financial file data. The detection deviation is less than 1%, and the risk rate of electronic financial file data is less than 1.5%. The detection results can be intuitively displayed on a visual page, proving that this method effectively ensures the quality of electronic financial file data and promotes intelligent management of electronic financial file data.

title: Electric field spread contributes to stimulation intensity-dependent expansion of navigated transcranial magnetic stimulation motor map
abstract: Objective Navigated transcranial magnetic stimulation (nTMS) is used for preoperative motor mapping, yet mechanisms of stimulation-intensity (SI)-dependent map expansion remain unclear. We investigated whether the extent of the induced electric field (EF) contributes to map expansion, using anatomical cavities adjacent to motor cortex as a model. Methods Two patients with postoperative and developmental cavities underwent nTMS mapping at 105% and 120% of resting motor threshold (rMT). Motor evoked potentials (MEPs) were recorded within cavities and intact cortex. Associations among distance from the cortical margin, rMT, and MEP amplitude were assessed. Map extension from reference points (RPs) was quantified toward cavities and intact tissue. In the postoperative case, finite-element modelling compared EF distributions in native and reconstructed anatomy. Results MEPs were elicited within cortex-free cavities despite absent cortical tissue beneath stimulation sites. Increasing distance from the cortical margin was associated with higher rMT and lower MEP amplitude. Higher SI expanded motor maps toward cavities and intact tissue. At 120% rMT, map extent from RPs was greater toward intact tissue, although directional distances are not physiologically equivalent because the functional motor-map boundary over intact cortex is unknown. Finite-element modelling showed high concordance between native and reconstructed anatomies, with a mean absolute EF difference of 1.34 V/m across stimulation sites. Conclusions Positive nTMS sites within cortex-free cavities demonstrate spatial dissociation between nominal stimulation sites and the neural elements generating MEPs. Findings support a contribution of EF spatial extent to SI-dependent map expansion. Significance Increasing SI improves response detection but may reduce spatial specificity.
authors: Evangelia Chatzikyriakou; Konstantinos Pastiadis; Theodoros Samaras; Nikolaos Foroglou; Marietta Tzirini; Symeon Damianidis; Κωνσταντίνος Κούσκουρας; Vasilios Papaliagkas; Evripidis Pityrigkas; Vasiliki Poulidou; IOANNIS K. VLACHOS; Dimitris Kugiumtzis; Vasilios Κ. Kimiskidis

title: สมรรถนะดานการสอสารของผนำทสงผลตอการสรางวฒนธรรมความยงยนในธรกจรานอาหารเครอขายของไทย
abstract: This study aimed (1) to examine the leadership communication competencies present in Thailand’s chain restaurant businesses and (2)to analyze the roles and communication-related factors of leaders influencing the formation of sustainability culture within these businesses. A qualitative research design was employed. In-depth interviews were conducted with nine executives from large chain restaurant businesses in Thailand that operated multiple branches nationwide and formally declared sustainability policies. The participants were selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using thematic content analysis. The findings revealed that leader’s communication competencies for fostering a culture of sustainability comprised four key dimensions: (1) message design competency, emphasizing clarity, conciseness, and the translation of policies into actionable practices; (2) relational communication competency, encompassing active learning, trust building, and positive reinforcement: (3) communication technology utilization competency, facilitating accessibility and continuity of communication across multiple business branches; and (4) shared meaning creation and persuasive communication competency, enabling employees to recognize the value of sustainability and translate this understanding into sustainable practices. Key factors that facilitated or hindered effective communication included top management support, internal communication structures, employee workload and technological readiness. The findings suggest that strengthening leaders’ communication competencies across all four dimensions can facilitate the effective implementation of sustainability initiatives in Thai chain restaurant business and foster an organizational culture that balances economic, social, and environmental responsibilities.
authors: Kittika Sapwetamornkul; Chatmongkol Naenna; Somsak Wanitchayaporn; Surawong Wannapak
venue: Journal of Administration and Social Science Review

title: Large language models as collaborative learning partners in higher education: a theoretical framework
abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into higher education environments reveals notable challenges within existing educational technology frameworks. Current theoretical models conceptualize artificial intelligence as an instrumental tool that supports human learning processes, yet numerous empirical studies demonstrate that LLMs function as collaborative learning partners with reciprocal agency, dynamic adaptation capabilities, and shared knowledge-construction behaviors. Research in Hungarian higher education contexts provides compelling evidence for this partnership phenomenon, with studies revealing that students primarily use AI systems for collaborative tasks such as brainstorming, information exploration, and iterative problem-solving rather than simple tool operation (Folmeg et al., 2024). I pro-pose the Collaborative Learning Partnership Model as a theoretical framework that reconceptualizes LLMs as active learning agents rather than passive educational instruments. Drawing from systematic analyses of recent implementation research across multiple educational domains, my model identifies four core components: reciprocal agency, dynamic contextual adaptation, shared knowledge construction, and transparent collaboration protocols. This frame-work addresses challenges in AI integration, including academic integrity concerns, assessment innovation, and pedagogical role transformation. The model provides a theoretical foundation for effective LLM integration while maintaining educational rigor and human agency in learning processes. Furthermore, I present a four-stage partnership development progression that guides practical implementation strategies.
authors: Zoltán Biczó

title: Longitudinal spatial changes of the contralesional corticospinal tract in high-grade glioma: a within-patient DTI tractography study
abstract: PURPOSE: The contralesional corticospinal tract (CST) is often used as an internal reference in glioma tractography, but its longitudinal stability remains poorly understood. We explored within-patient changes in contralesional CST characteristics between primary and recurrent high-grade glioma. METHODS: Twenty-nine patients with paired preoperative diffusion tensor imaging at primary and recurrent assessments were retrospectively analyzed. The contralesional CST was reconstructed using anatomically guided deterministic tractography at fractional anisotropy thresholds (FATs) of 0.10 and 0.15. Tract-averaged fractional anisotropy (FA), tract length, and tract volume were compared longitudinally. Spatial changes were assessed using patient-level slice-wise centroid trajectories and paired voxel-wise analyses in standardized space, with HCP842 used as a fixed normative spatial reference. RESULTS: No longitudinal differences in FA, tract length, or tract volume remained significant after BH-FDR correction. In contrast, slice-wise analyses showed a predominantly anterior CST displacement at recurrence, with mean paired Y-axis differences of 2.576 mm at FAT 0.10 and 2.078 mm at FAT 0.15; 57 and 21 slices, respectively, remained significant after correction. Mediolateral changes were smaller and less consistent, and no voxel-wise differences survived correction. Relative to HCP842, both assessments were posterior to the reference trajectory, while the recurrent CST was less posterior. CONCLUSION: The contralesional CST showed longitudinal spatial displacement without corresponding corrected changes in tractography-derived FA, tract length, or tract volume. These findings indicate that its spatial position may not remain fixed between primary and recurrent glioma assessments.
authors: Bingzhen Li; Raimunde Liang; Ghaith Altawalbeh; Lisa Stefanie Hönikl; Eugen Ursu; Axel Schroeder; Haosu Zhang; Philipp Karschnia; Chiara Negwer; Bernhard Meyer; Arthur Wagner

title: Designing optimal perturbation inputs for system identification in neuroscience
abstract: Investigating the dynamics of neural networks, which are governed by connectivity between neurons, is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Because passive (spontaneous) activity provides only limited information for estimating connectivity, perturbation-based approaches are widely applied in neuroscience, as they can evoke underlying hidden dynamics. However, the characteristics of such perturbations have typically been designed based on empirical or biological intuition. To enable more accurate estimation of connectivity, we propose a data-driven and theoretically grounded framework for optimally designing perturbation inputs, based on formulating the neural model as a control system. The core theoretical insight underlying our approach is that neural signals observed in the passive state lack sufficient latent information, which leads to failures in the system identification. Perturbations reveal these hidden dynamics and lead to improved estimation. Guided by these insights, we derive a theoretical basis for optimizing perturbation inputs that minimize estimation errors in neural system identification. Building upon this, we further explore the relationship of this theory with stimulation patterns commonly used in neuroscience, such as frequency, impulse, and step inputs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework for neuroscience through simulations grounded in experimental paradigms such as neural state classification and optimal control of neural states. Our theoretical analysis, together with multiple simulations, consistently shows that perturbations designed according to our framework achieve substantially more accurate system identification compared to the conventional, intuition-based inputs. This study provides a theoretical foundation for designing perturbation inputs to achieve accurate estimation of neural dynamics. This, in turn, enables reliable discrimination of neural states such as levels of consciousness and pathological conditions, and facilitates precise control of their transitions toward recovery from abnormal states.

title: Phosphorylated Analogs of Paracetamol and Their Anti‐Inflammatory Potential
abstract: Paracetamol is a widely used analgesic and antipyretic agent; however, its use is limited by minimal anti-inflammatory activity and the risk of hepatotoxicity from prolonged oral use or in acute overdose. To address these limitations, four novel phosphorylated paracetamol analogs (2a-2d) were synthesized via a UV-radical methodology and evaluated through integrated in silico, in vitro, and in vivo for anti-inflammatory dermal approaches. Molecular docking suggested plausible binding interactions with COX-1 and COX-2 for all analogs. In vitro cytotoxicity assays in THP-1 cells showed that 2a and 2b did not affect cell viability at 100 μM over 24 h. In a TPA-induced acute ear edema model in CD1 male mice, 2a produced about 50% inhibition of edema at the lowest tested quantity (0.5 mg/ear), representing a fourfold potency advantage over indomethacin at the same amount, while 2b displayed significant anti-inflammatory and vasoregulatory activity at higher quantities. Computational ADME profiling indicated that all analogs satisfy Lipinski's drug-likeness criteria and exhibit low predicted hERG channel risk. These results support N-phosphorylation of 4-aminophenol as a viable strategy to improve the topical anti-inflammatory efficacy of paracetamol analogs.

title: AquaMend: Minimal Re-probing and Conditional Rollback for Latent-Belief Failures in Embodied Agents
abstract: Physical changes or sensing errors can invalidate embodied agents' task-relevant beliefs. AquaMend compares re-probing, rollback, and supported continuation on a probe-belief-action graph under an expected-loss objective covering sensing, physical recovery, and uncorrected failures. A joint posterior guides a one-step policy with conditional detection-power screening. The per-belief three-way optimum requires independence, separability, and fully resolving probes; the general policy has no global optimality guarantee. Across 32 paired scenarios in a self-constructed simulation benchmark, AquaMend recovers in 28/32 cases and reduces mean complete loss by 21.6% versus restart. Its paired loss difference from decision-theoretic troubleshooting (DTT) is not statistically significant after Holm correction. Against the all-candidate ablation, online decision time decreases by 12.3% overall but increases by 3.4% in the uncovered late stage.
authors: Yufan Liu; Shang Luo; Yang Liu; Haoxuan Jia; Feiyu Han; Qian Li; Chen Li; Yingguang Yang; Chongyang Zhang; Hao Zheng; Kefu Xu; Bin Chong

title: Identifying Neural Source Dynamics from Unknown Local Interventions
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) records mixtures of brain-source activity. Even with a known anatomical forward model, experiments that excite only part of the source-state space leave the dynamics unidentified, and repetition cannot resolve the ambiguity. We show that unknown local mechanism changes can supply the missing information. We consider linear dynamics among fixed anatomical sources with known source-state initialization patterns. Changing one source's update rule for one transition leaves a rank-one, source-specific signature in subsequent EEG: subtracting matched baseline responses isolates it, and the forward model identifies the source and calibrates its response history. Combining these histories with initialization responses recovers source interactions without baseline reachability and without first identifying the intervention coefficients. We establish sufficient recovery conditions, a direct estimator, and a noise-sensitivity bound conditional on correct source labels. Simulated EEG on anatomy derived from magnetic resonance imaging confirms the information gain: with baseline excitation confined to four of twelve source coordinates, eight unknown changes recover all dynamics in 32/32 systems, whereas baseline realization, baseline regression through an invertible forward model, and changes that leave the tested states unexposed all fail, and explicitly constructed alternative dynamics reproduce every baseline mean. Where baseline information suffices, direct reconstruction is also more reliable than a matched-information spectral estimator. Nonlocal changes and forward-model error limit accuracy even when source labels are correct.
authors: Ayana Mussabayeva; Jiaqi Sun; Anuar Aimoldin; Olivier Oullier; Kun Zhang

title: Scientific Curiosity Building through Guided Inquiry in Secondary Science
abstract: This study examined how guided inquiry contributed to the development of scientific curiosity among Grade 9 learners in San Pablo, Isabela. Using a cross-sectional predictive survey design with a quantile-regression framework, the research involved 190 learners selected through proportionate stratified random sampling. Data were gathered using validated measures of guided inquiry experiences and scientific curiosity. Median, interquartile range, and median absolute deviation were used to describe the distributions of the variables, while quantile regression with 5,000 bootstrap resamples determined whether the predictive contribution of guided inquiry varied across levels of scientific curiosity. Results showed that learners experienced guided inquiry at a moderate level, while overall scientific curiosity was also moderate. Among the dimensions of curiosity, stretching and engagement in science practices were relatively stronger, whereas embracing uncertainty emerged as the weakest area. Guided inquiry significantly predicted scientific curiosity at the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles, with the strongest coefficient observed among learners in the lower curiosity group. The findings indicate that guided inquiry may be particularly beneficial for learners who demonstrate limited inclination to question, investigate, or persist in uncertain scientific situations. Strengthening guided questioning, evidence-based investigation, experimentation, and reflective explanation is therefore recommended, with differentiated teacher scaffolding based on learners’ levels of scientific curiosity.
authors: Amilyn P. Maramag; Alma P. Gonzales

title: EXPRESS: BOLD Contrast in Cerebral Diffuse Glioma Imaging: Biological Foundations and Clinical Applications – A Review of the Literature
abstract: Diffuse cerebral gliomas are the most common malignant brain tumors in adults. In the present work we conducted a narrative review on the role of blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD)-MRI in diffuse glioma imaging, from historical and clinical applications to recent translational studies including approaches to detect vascular and metabolic alterations as well as its expanding potential to enhance tumor infiltration assessment and treatment surveillance. Task-based and resting-state BOLD-MRI enable localization of eloquent cortical areas and assessment of functional reorganization, though their accuracy is challenged by neurovascular uncoupling and patient-related variability. Combination with vasoactive stimuli allows cerebrovascular reactivity mapping to uncover vascular dysfunction propagating beyond visible tumor margins, correlating with tumor grade and hemodynamic impairment. Quantitative and calibrated BOLD approaches as well as oxygen modulation during BOLD sequence acquisition provide noninvasive biomarkers of tissue hypoxia, oxygen metabolism, and tumor aggressiveness. Despite extensive research, BOLD contrast holds unexploited potential for enhancing glioma diagnosis and management by capturing critical vascular and metabolic alterations. Although challenges remain pertaining to accuracy and standardization, emerging techniques offer substantial potential for the assessment of tumor infiltration extent and therapy surveillance. Advancing clinical integration will require robust standardization, large-scale validation, and correlation with clinical, molecular, and histopathological data.

title: Digital multimodal vocabulary projects in Indonesian EFL higher education: Design, assessment, and students’ perceptions
abstract: Vocabulary assessment in Indonesian EFL higher education remains predominantly focused on discrete-item tests, prioritizing individual receptive knowledge. To address limitations of such tests, this study examined collaborative, digital, multimodal vocabulary projects in a pre-service teacher class in Indonesia and explored students’ perceptions. This study is an exploratory, single-case qualitative study conducted with a class of 30 third-semester EFL teacher-education students. They collaboratively created two digitally mediated multimodal projects: a Quizizz-based vocabulary quiz set and an idiom-based conversation video. The project artefacts, rubric notes, the lecturer’s reflection notes, and semi-structured interview scripts were analyzed thematically. The study revealed that students experienced gains in creativity, critical thinking, collaboration, digital skills, and enjoyment throughout the process. However, they reported time constraints, communication challenges, and performance anxiety. Group-based digital projects were evident to make vocabulary use in context observable, and multimodal assessment was found to support vocabulary learning and learning-oriented assessment. The research contributes empirical evidence on multimodal assessment for vocabulary learning in Indonesian EFL higher education, a context that remains underrepresented in the literature. It is recommended that collaborative, multimodal task design be integrated into pre-service teacher education to scaffold digital literacy, collaboration, culturally relevant development, and contextually grounded vocabulary assessment practices.
authors: Nurmala Hendrawaty; Zulfa Sakhiyya; Sri Wahyuni; Yuliati Yuliati
